topics.name: Equation of a circle and tangents
Sine rule, cosine rule, area and bearings
Volume and surface area (cones, spheres, pyramids, frustums)

questions.q: [Non-calculator] In a sale, the price of a coat is reduced by 15%. The sale price is £68. What was the original price?
questions.tip: Never add 15% back on to the sale price. Divide by the multiplier 0.85.

questions.q: [Calculator] The price of a laptop is increased by 8% and then the new price is decreased by 5%. What is the overall percentage change?
questions.tip: Percentage changes multiply, they do not add. 8 - 5 = 3 is the trap.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Work out 3 1/3 × 2 1/4 - 1 5/6
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
ms: M1 converts to improper fractions, e.g. 10/3 × 9/4
M1 correct product 90/12 (= 15/2) and attempts common denominator with 11/6, e.g. 45/6 - 11/6
A1 5 2/3 (do not accept 17/3 as a final answer, a mixed number is required)
questions.tip: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions before multiplying. Do not multiply the whole parts and fraction parts separately.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A TV costs £714 including VAT at 20%.
Amir says, 'The VAT is 20% of £714, so the VAT is £142.80.'
(a) Explain what Amir has done wrong. (1)
(b) Work out the correct amount of VAT. (2)
questions.answer: (a) £714 is 120% of the price, not 100%, so 20% must be found of the pre-VAT price. (b) £119
ms: B1 explanation that £714 already includes VAT / is 120% so he should not take 20% of £714
questions.tip: Reverse percentage: the amount you are given is 120%, so divide by 1.2 first.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A shop buys 90 mugs for a total of £540.
It sells 70 of the mugs for £8.50 each.
It sells the rest at half that price.
Work out the percentage profit. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: Percentage profit is always profit ÷ ORIGINAL cost, not ÷ selling price.

questions.q:
[Calculator] In January the price of a bike was increased by x%.
In March the new price was reduced by 5%.
The price in March is 2.6% more than the original price.
Work out the value of x.
questions.tip: Work with multipliers throughout. 2.6 + 5 = 7.6 is wrong because percentage changes do not add.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In a club, 3/8 of the members are juniors. The rest are seniors.
2/5 of the juniors and 1/3 of the seniors play tennis.
129 members play tennis.
How many members are in the club?
ms: M1 fraction of juniors playing: 3/8 × 2/5 (= 3/20 or 6/40)
questions.tip: Find each group's fraction of the WHOLE club first, then add. Do not add 2/5 and 1/3 directly.

questions.q: [Calculator] £2000 is invested at 3% per year compound interest. What is it worth after 4 years, to the nearest penny?
questions.tip: £2240 is simple interest. Compound means multiply by 1.03 each year.

questions.q: [Calculator] A car is worth £15 000. Its value depreciates by 12% per year. What is it worth after 3 years, to the nearest pound?
questions.tip: £9600 comes from taking 36% off in one go. Depreciation is compound.

questions.q: [Calculator] The number of animals in a reserve is N = 24 000 × 0.85^t, where t is the number of years from now. After how many complete years will N first be below 10 000?
ms: t = 5 gives 10 648.9 (above 10 000); t = 6 gives 9051.6 (below), so 6 years.
questions.tip: Trial and improvement: test the whole numbers either side and state which one first drops below.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A house is worth £250 000. Its value increases by 4% each year.
Work out the value of the house after 6 years. Give your answer to the nearest pound.
questions.tip: Use the multiplier to the power of the number of years. Do not do 6 × 4% = 24%.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Ben invests £5000 for 5 years.
Account A: 2.8% per year compound interest for all 5 years.
Account B: 4% per year compound interest for the first 2 years, then 1.5% per year compound interest for the next 3 years.
Which account gives more money at the end of 5 years, and by how much?
ms: A1 Account A, by £85.28 (accept £85.29 from rounding)
questions.tip: Two different rates: multiply by each multiplier the right number of times in one chain.

questions.q:
[Calculator] £5000 is invested at 12% per year compound interest.
Work out the least number of whole years it will take for the investment to be worth more than £20 000.
ms: M1 uses 5000 × 1.12^n for at least one n ≥ 10
M1 shows n = 12 gives 19 479.88 (less than 20 000) and n = 13 gives 21 817.47 (more than 20 000)
questions.tip: Show the value for the year before AND the year it first passes the target, or you lose the method marks.

questions.q:
[Calculator] £6000 is invested at r% per year compound interest.
After 2 years the investment is worth £6615.
Work out the value of r.
questions.tip: Square root to undo 2 years of growth, then convert the multiplier back to a percentage.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A van was bought for £18 000.
In the first year its value fell by 15%.
In each of the next two years its value fell by x%.
After 3 years the van was worth £12 393.
(a) Work out the value of x. (3)
(b) Work out the overall percentage decrease in value over the 3 years. (1)
questions.tip: Undo the known year first, then take the square root for the two equal years.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Work out (8.4 × 10⁷) ÷ (2.1 × 10³). Give your answer in standard form.
questions.tip: Divide the numbers, SUBTRACT the powers.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Work out 3.2 × 10⁵ + 4.5 × 10⁴. Give your answer in standard form.
questions.tip: For adding, convert to ordinary numbers (or the same power) first. Never add the powers.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (a) Write 0.000706 in standard form. (1)
(b) Write 3.4 × 10⁻² as an ordinary number. (1)
questions.tip: The number in front must be at least 1 and less than 10. Small numbers have negative powers.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Work out (6 × 10⁻³) × (5 × 10⁸). Give your answer in standard form.
questions.tip: 30 × 10⁵ is not standard form. Adjust so the first number is between 1 and 10.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The mass of the Earth is 5.97 × 10²⁴ kg. The mass of the Moon is 7.35 × 10²² kg.
How many times heavier is the Earth than the Moon? Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.tip: Use brackets or the ×10ˣ key on your calculator so the division is done correctly.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Proxima Centauri is 4.24 light years from Earth.
1 light year = 9.46 × 10¹² km.
A spacecraft travels at an average speed of 6.2 × 10⁴ km/h.
How many years would the spacecraft take to reach Proxima Centauri? Assume 1 year = 365 days.
Give your answer in standard form to 2 significant figures.
questions.tip: Keep full calculator values until the end. Rounding the hours early can change the 2 s.f. answer.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] a = 4 × 10ⁿ and b = 5 × 10ⁿ⁻² where n is an integer.
(a) Find ab. Give your answer in standard form in terms of n. (2)
(b) Find a ÷ b as an ordinary number. (1)
questions.tip: When 20 becomes 2.0, add 1 to the power: 20 × 10^(2n-2) = 2 × 10^(2n-1).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the value of 27^(-2/3)?
questions.tip: A negative power means reciprocal, it never makes the answer negative.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the value of (81/16)^(3/4)?
ms: Fourth root of 81/16 is 3/2, cubed is 27/8.
questions.tip: Take the root (denominator) first to keep the numbers small, then the power.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Simplify fully
(a) (3x²y)³ (1)
(b) x⁷ ÷ x⁻² (1)
questions.tip: Cube the 3 as well: 3³ = 27, not 9. Subtracting a negative power adds.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Work out the value of 5⁰ + 4^(-1/2)
questions.tip: Anything to the power 0 is 1, not 0.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 25√5 ÷ 125^(2/3) as a power of 5.
questions.tip: Write every part as a power of 5 first, then use the index laws.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 9^(x+1) = 27^(2x-1)
ms: M1 writes both sides as powers of 3: 3^(2x+2) = 3^(6x-3)
questions.tip: You must have the same base on both sides before you set the powers equal.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] x = 2^p and y = 2^q
Express 2^(3p - q + 2) in terms of x and y.
questions.tip: 2^(+2) becomes a multiplier of 4. Do not leave it as 2².

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Simplify √72
questions.tip: Look for the LARGEST square factor. 3√8 is not fully simplified.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Simplify √75 + √48 - √27
questions.tip: You cannot add the numbers under the roots. Simplify each surd first.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Expand and simplify (5 - 2√3)²
ms: M1 three of the four terms correct from 25 - 10√3 - 10√3 + 12
questions.tip: (2√3)² = 4 × 3 = 12, not 6. And squaring a bracket gives FOUR terms.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Rationalise the denominator of 6/(3 - √7). Simplify your answer fully.
ms: M1 multiplies numerator and denominator by (3 + √7)
questions.tip: Multiply by the conjugate with the opposite sign. Remember to cancel the 2 at the end.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Show that 1/(√5 + √3) = (√5 - √3)/2
ms: M1 multiplies top and bottom by (√5 - √3)
A1 denominator shown to be 5 - 3 = 2 giving (√5 - √3)/2
questions.tip: In 'show that' questions write every line, including the denominator working.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write (5 + √3)/(2 - √3) in the form a + b√3, where a and b are integers.
ms: M1 multiplies numerator and denominator by (2 + √3)
questions.tip: Expand the numerator carefully: √3 × √3 = 3 gives an extra whole number.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A rectangle has length (3 + √5) cm and area (11 + 5√5) cm².
Work out the perimeter of the rectangle. Give your answer in the form a + b√5, where a and b are integers.
questions.tip: Check your width by multiplying back: (3 + √5)(2 + √5) = 11 + 5√5.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The length, l cm, of a pencil is 6.4 cm correct to 1 decimal place. Which is the error interval for l?
questions.tip: Lower bound uses ≤, upper bound uses <.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] x = 7.6 when truncated to 1 decimal place. Which is the error interval for x?
ms: Truncating chops digits off, so x is from 7.6 up to (not including) 7.7.
questions.tip: Truncation is not rounding: the true value is never below the truncated value.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A number n is rounded to 2 significant figures. The result is 4300.
Write down the error interval for n.
ms: B1 4250 ≤ n < 4350 with correct inequality signs
questions.tip: 2 s.f. of 4300 means to the nearest 100, so go 50 either side.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A rectangle has length 12.6 cm, correct to 3 significant figures, and width 8.4 cm, correct to 2 significant figures.
Work out the upper bound for the area of the rectangle.
questions.tip: Upper bound of a product: upper × upper.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A boat travels 122 km, correct to the nearest km, in 11.4 hours, correct to 1 decimal place.
Work out the lower bound for the average speed of the boat. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
questions.tip: Lower bound of a division: LOWER ÷ UPPER.

questions.q:
[Calculator] a = 18.6 correct to 1 decimal place
b = 7.3 correct to 1 decimal place
c = 3.4 correct to 1 decimal place
k = (a - b)/c
By considering bounds, work out the value of k to a suitable degree of accuracy. You must show all your working and give a reason for your final answer.
ms: C1 k = 3 because both bounds round to 3 to 1 significant figure
questions.tip: For a subtraction, the upper bound is UB - LB. You must give the reason that both bounds agree to 1 s.f.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A car travels 645 km, correct to the nearest 5 km.
It uses 80.5 litres of fuel, correct to 3 significant figures.
The manufacturer claims the car always does at least 8 km per litre.
Does this journey show the claim is definitely true? You must show your working.
questions.answer: No. Lower bound 642.5 ÷ 80.55 = 7.98 km/l, which is below 8.
ms: C1 conclusion: not definitely true because the lower bound is less than 8 (accept use of UB 8.05 as well)
questions.tip: 'Nearest 5' means 2.5 either side. 'Definitely' questions need the bound that could break the claim.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 0.363636... (0.36 recurring) as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.tip: Two recurring digits means denominator 99, not 100.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which of these fractions gives a recurring decimal?
ms: 12 = 2² × 3. A prime factor other than 2 or 5 in the denominator gives a recurring decimal.
questions.tip: Simplify first, then check the denominator's prime factors.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 0.1363636... (0.136 with the 36 recurring) as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.tip: Only the 36 recurs, so subtract 10x from 1000x, not x from 1000x.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove algebraically that the recurring decimal 0.3151515... (0.3 with 15 recurring) can be written as 52/165.
ms: M1 two correct recurring decimals that differ by a whole number e.g. 1000x = 315.1515... and 10x = 3.1515...
questions.tip: Write out the recurring parts so they visibly cancel. 'Prove' needs algebra, not a calculator.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 1.2777... (1.2 with the 7 recurring) as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.tip: Do not forget the whole number part when you set up x.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] x = 0.242424... and y = 0.444...
Show that x + y = 68/99
ms: A1 4/9 written as 44/99 and sum shown = 68/99
questions.tip: Show the algebra for each decimal. Writing 24/99 from memory may not get the method marks.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 0.1353535... (0.1 with 35 recurring) as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.tip: Simplify fully: 134/990 halves to 67/495.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 360 as a product of its prime factors.
questions.tip: 10 and 15 are not prime. Every factor must be prime.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 84 and 90?
questions.tip: 84 × 90 = 7560 is a common multiple but not the lowest.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (a) Write 252 as a product of its prime factors. (2)
(b) Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 252 and 294. (1)
ms: M1 correct factor tree or division method for 252
questions.tip: 294 = 2 × 3 × 7². HCF takes the LOWEST power of each shared prime.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Bus A leaves the station every 12 minutes, bus B every 18 minutes and bus C every 20 minutes.
All three buses leave the station together at 9 am.
When will all three next leave together?
ms: M1 lists multiples or uses prime factors 12 = 2² × 3, 18 = 2 × 3², 20 = 2² × 5
questions.tip: Recognise 'together again' as an LCM question, then convert minutes to a time.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A = 2³ × 3² × 5 and B = 2 × 3³ × 5²
(a) Find the HCF of A and B. (1)
(b) Find the LCM of A and B. Give your answer in index form. (1)
questions.tip: HCF: lowest powers of shared primes. LCM: highest powers of all primes.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two numbers have a highest common factor of 6 and a lowest common multiple of 180.
The difference between the two numbers is 6.
Find the two numbers.
ms: M1 recognises both numbers are multiples of 6 that are factors of 180
M1 lists possible pairs e.g. 6 and 180, 12 and 90, 18 and 60, 30 and 36
questions.tip: Check both conditions: HCF(30, 36) = 6 and LCM(30, 36) = 180.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] N = 2³ × 3 × 5²
M is the smallest positive integer such that NM is a cube number.
(a) Find M. (2)
(b) Find the cube root of NM. (1)
ms: M1 recognises powers must be multiples of 3, e.g. needs 3² and 5¹ more
questions.tip: For a cube every prime power must be a multiple of 3. 2³ already works.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A café offers 4 starters, 6 main courses and 3 desserts. How many different three-course meals (one of each) are possible?
questions.tip: Product rule: multiply the choices, do not add them.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A 4-digit PIN uses the digits 0 to 9. No digit can be used more than once. How many different PINs are possible?
questions.tip: No repeats means the choices go down by one each time.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A café sells x types of sandwich and 5 types of drink.
There are 60 different ways to choose one sandwich and one drink.
Work out x.
questions.tip: Set up the product rule as an equation.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A number plate has 3 letters followed by 2 digits.
Any of the 26 letters can be used and letters may repeat.
The two digits must be different.
How many different number plates are possible?
questions.tip: Read the conditions for each part separately: repeats allowed for letters, not for digits.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] There are 13 teams in a league. Each team plays every other team exactly once.
How many matches are played?
questions.tip: Divide by 2 because A v B is the same match as B v A.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] How many even 4-digit numbers between 3000 and 5000 have four different digits?
ms: M1 splits into first digit 3 and first digit 4
M1 first digit 3: 5 × 8 × 7 (= 280) OR first digit 4: 4 × 8 × 7 (= 224)
questions.tip: When the first digit is 4 (even), only 4 even last digits remain. Deal with the restricted places first.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Three-digit codes are made using the digits 1 to 7. No digit can be repeated.
The first digit must be 5 or more and the last digit must be odd.
How many codes are possible?
ms: M1 considers first digit odd (5 or 7) and even (6) separately
questions.tip: If the first digit is odd it uses up one of the odd options for the last digit.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise x² - 49
ms: Difference of two squares: a² - b² = (a + b)(a - b).
questions.tip: (x - 7)² expands to x² - 14x + 49, not x² - 49.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise 6x² + x - 12
questions.tip: Always expand your answer to check the middle term and its sign.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Expand and simplify (x - 7)(x + 2)
ms: M1 three of the four terms x², 2x, -7x, -14 correct
questions.tip: Watch the signs: -7 × 2 = -14.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Expand and simplify (2x - 1)(x + 3)(x - 4)
ms: M1 expands two brackets correctly, e.g. (x + 3)(x - 4) = x² - x - 12
M1 multiplies by the third bracket with at least 4 of the 6 terms correct
questions.tip: Expand two brackets first and simplify before multiplying by the third.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise fully 18x² - 50y²
ms: M1 takes out common factor 2 or writes as difference of two squares
questions.tip: 'Fully' means take out the common factor 2 first.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Expand and simplify (3x - 2)³
ms: M1 multiplies by (3x - 2) with at least 4 of the 6 terms correct
questions.tip: (3x - 2)³ is not 27x³ - 8. Write it as three brackets.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (a) Factorise 12x² - 7x - 10 (2)
(b) Factorise fully x⁴ - 13x² + 36 (2)
questions.tip: Treat x⁴ - 13x² + 36 as a quadratic in x², then spot two differences of two squares.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 3/x + 2/(5x) as a single fraction.
questions.tip: Use a common denominator. Never add the denominators.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Simplify fully (x² - 9)/(x² + 5x + 6)
questions.tip: Factorise top and bottom first. You can only cancel whole brackets, not single terms.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 3/(x + 2) - 2/(x - 1) as a single fraction in its simplest form.
questions.tip: When you subtract, the minus sign applies to every term: -2(x + 2) = -2x - 4.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Simplify fully (2x² + 5x - 3)/(4x² - 1)
questions.tip: 4x² - 1 is a difference of two squares: (2x + 1)(2x - 1).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Show that x/(x - 2) - 8/(x² - 4) simplifies to (x + 4)/(x + 2)
questions.answer: Common denominator (x - 2)(x + 2); numerator x(x + 2) - 8 = x² + 2x - 8 = (x + 4)(x - 2); cancel (x - 2).
ms: A1 cancels (x - 2) to reach (x + 4)/(x + 2) with no errors
questions.tip: Spot that x² - 4 already contains (x - 2), so use (x - 2)(x + 2) as the common denominator.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 3/(x + 2) + 2/(x - 4) = 1
questions.tip: Do not divide by x when you get x² - 7x = 0, you will lose the solution x = 0.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Simplify fully (x² - 4)/(3x² + 5x - 2) ÷ (x² - x - 2)/(3x² + 4x + 1)
ms: M1 flips the second fraction and multiplies
questions.tip: Factorise everything before cancelling, and remember to turn the second fraction upside down.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 5(x - 3) = 2x + 9
questions.tip: Expand the bracket fully: 5 × -3 = -15.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write x² + 6x - 7 in the form (x + a)² + b
questions.tip: Halve the coefficient of x, then subtract the square of that number.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 2x² - 7x - 15 = 0
ms: M1 (2x + 3)(x - 5) or correct use of formula
questions.tip: Setting 2x + 3 = 0 gives x = -3/2, not -3.

questions.q: [Calculator] Solve 3x² - 5x - 4 = 0. Give your solutions correct to 2 decimal places.
ms: M1 correct substitution into the quadratic formula: (5 ± √(25 + 48))/6
questions.tip: b² - 4ac = 25 - 4(3)(-4) = 73. The double negative is where most marks go.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve (x + 3)/4 - (2x - 1)/3 = 1
questions.tip: Use a bracket for each numerator so the minus sign changes both terms.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (a) Write x² + 8x + 3 in the form (x + a)² + b (2)
(b) Hence solve x² + 8x + 3 = 0, giving your answers in the form p ± √q (2)
questions.tip: Remember the ± when you square root, otherwise you lose a solution.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A rectangle has length (2x + 1) cm and width (x - 3) cm.
A square has side length (x + 1) cm.
The area of the rectangle is 13 cm² more than the area of the square.
Work out the value of x. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places. You must show why only one solution is possible.
ms: A1 x = 8.91, rejecting -1.91 because the width x - 3 must be positive
questions.tip: Bracket the square's area when subtracting, and always reject solutions that give negative lengths.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
3x + 2y = 16
5x - 2y = 16
ms: Adding gives 8x = 32, so x = 4, then 12 + 2y = 16 gives y = 2.
questions.tip: Check your answer in BOTH equations.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which of these is one of the solutions of the simultaneous equations y = x² and y = x + 6?
ms: x² = x + 6 gives (x - 3)(x + 2) = 0, so x = 3, y = 9 or x = -2, y = 4.
questions.tip: Substitute your x back into the LINEAR equation to find the matching y.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
2x + 3y = 13
5x - 2y = 4
ms: M1 correct method to eliminate one variable, e.g. 4x + 6y = 26 and 15x - 6y = 12
questions.tip: Multiply BOTH whole equations, including the right-hand sides.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 3 adult tickets and 2 child tickets for a cinema cost £39.
2 adult tickets and 5 child tickets cost £48.
Work out the cost of one adult ticket and the cost of one child ticket.
ms: M1 correct method to eliminate a variable
questions.tip: Define your letters clearly and form two equations before solving.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
x² + y² = 25
y = x + 1
questions.tip: (x + 1)² is x² + 2x + 1, not x² + 1. Pair each x with its own y.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
y = x² - 4x + 1
2x + y = 4
ms: A1 y = -2 and y = 6 correctly paired
questions.tip: Make y the subject of the linear equation first, then set the two expressions equal.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The line y = 2x - 5 meets the circle x² + y² = 20 at the points A and B.
(a) Find the exact coordinates of A and B. (5)
(b) Find the exact length of AB. Give your answer as a simplified surd. (2)
ms: M1 correct method to solve, e.g. (x - 2)² = 3 or formula
M1 differences 2√3 and 4√3 used in Pythagoras
questions.tip: When the quadratic does not factorise, complete the square or use the formula and keep exact surds.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 4x - 7 < 2x + 5
questions.tip: Only flip the inequality sign when you multiply or divide by a negative.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve x² < 16
ms: x² < 16 is true between the roots -4 and 4.
questions.tip: x < 4 alone includes x = -10, which does not work. Sketch y = x² - 16.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] -7 ≤ 3n - 1 < 8
n is an integer.
Write down all the possible values of n.
questions.tip: Include -2 because of ≤, but not 3 because of <.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 5 - 3x ≥ 17
questions.tip: Dividing by -3 reverses the sign. Safer: move the x term to the side where it is positive.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve x² - 2x - 15 > 0
questions.tip: For '> 0' on a U-shaped graph the answer is OUTSIDE the roots, written as two separate inequalities.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Find the integer values of x that satisfy both
2x² + 5x - 3 ≤ 0
and
3x + 7 > 0
questions.tip: Solve each inequality separately, then find the overlap on a number line.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The region R satisfies all three inequalities
y ≥ 1
x + y ≤ 6
y ≤ 2x
(a) Find the coordinates of the three vertices of R. (3)
(b) Work out the area of R. (2)
ms: M1 solves a pair of boundary equations simultaneously, e.g. y = 2x and x + y = 6
questions.tip: Each vertex is where two boundary lines cross. Sketch the lines to see which side is the region.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A rectangle has length (x + 3) cm and width (x - 1) cm.
The perimeter of the rectangle is more than 20 cm.
The area of the rectangle is less than 32 cm².
Find the range of possible values of x.
questions.tip: Combine the two conditions at the end. The quadratic gives a range BETWEEN its roots.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make t the subject of v = u + at
ms: v - u = at so t = (v - u)/a
questions.tip: Undo the operations in reverse order: subtract u first, then divide by a.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make r the subject of V = (1/3)πr²h
questions.tip: Multiply by 3 to clear the fraction, then square root at the very end.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make x the subject of 5(x - 2y) = 3 + y
questions.tip: Expand first or divide by 5 first, both work, but keep all y terms together.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make a the subject of T = 2π√(a/g)
questions.tip: Square everything on the other side: (2π)² = 4π².

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make x the subject of y = (2x + 3)/(x - 4)
questions.tip: Subject appears twice: get both x terms on one side and factorise x out.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make p the subject of 3p + q = ap - 4
ms: M1 collects p terms: q + 4 = ap - 3p
questions.tip: Factorise p out of both terms; do not leave p on both sides.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 1/u + 1/v = 1/f
Make v the subject of the formula.
ms: M1 multiplies through by uvf: vf + uf = uv
M1 uf = uv - vf = v(u - f)
questions.tip: 1/v = 1/f - 1/u does not give v = f - u. Combine into one fraction then flip.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make x the subject of √((x + a)/x) = b
questions.tip: Square both sides first to remove the root, then the subject appears twice.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find the nth term of the sequence 7, 11, 15, 19, ...
questions.tip: Check with n = 1: 4(1) + 3 = 7.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find the nth term of the geometric sequence 2, 6, 18, 54, ...
ms: First term 2, ratio 3: 2 × 3^(n-1). Check n = 1 gives 2.
questions.tip: 2 × 3^n gives 6 as the first term. Use power n - 1.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The nth term of a sequence is 5n - 3.
Is 100 a term in the sequence? You must show how you get your answer.
questions.answer: No, because 5n - 3 = 100 gives n = 20.6, which is not a whole number.
ms: A1 No, with n = 20.6 not an integer (or 100 between 97 and 102)
questions.tip: Always give a reason. 'No' on its own scores nothing.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find the nth term of the quadratic sequence 4, 11, 22, 37, 56, ...
questions.tip: Halve the second difference to get the n² coefficient.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The first three terms of a geometric sequence are 2, 2√3, 6.
Find the 6th term. Give your answer in the form k√3.
questions.tip: (√3)² = 3, so the terms alternate between whole numbers and multiples of √3.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A Fibonacci-type sequence has first term a and second term b. Each term after that is the sum of the two terms before it.
The 3rd term is 7 and the 6th term is 31.
Find a and b.
ms: M1 6th term 3a + 5b (from a, b, a + b, a + 2b, 2a + 3b, 3a + 5b)
M1 solves a + b = 7 and 3a + 5b = 31 simultaneously
questions.tip: Write each term in terms of a and b carefully: 4th = a + 2b, 5th = 2a + 3b, 6th = 3a + 5b.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The nth term of a sequence is an² + bn, where a and b are integers.
The 3rd term is 21 and the 5th term is 55.
(a) Find a and b. (3)
(b) Which term of the sequence is equal to 300? (2)
questions.tip: Reject the negative or fractional solution: term numbers must be positive integers.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] f(x) = 3x² - 2. Find f(-2).
questions.tip: Square first, then multiply by 3. (-2)² = 4.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] f(x) = 2x + 1 and g(x) = x². Find fg(x).
questions.tip: fg means do g FIRST, then f.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = 5x - 3
Find the value of x for which f(x) = 22
questions.tip: Set the function equal to the value and solve.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = (x + 4)/3
Find f⁻¹(x)
ms: M1 y = (x + 4)/3 rearranged to x = 3y - 4 (or swaps x and y)
questions.tip: Write the final answer in terms of x, not y.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = 4 - x and g(x) = x² + 3
(a) Find gf(2) (2)
(b) Solve fg(x) = -8 (2)
questions.tip: Bracket the inner function when substituting: 4 - (x² + 3) = 1 - x².

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = (2x + 1)/(x - 3)
Find f⁻¹(x)
questions.tip: This is a 'subject appears twice' rearrangement. Factorise to isolate x.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = 3x - 1 and g(x) = 2x + k, where k is a constant.
fg(x) = gf(x) for all values of x.
Find the value of k.
questions.tip: Equate the constant terms; the 6x terms are already equal.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = 2x - 3 and g(x) = x²
Solve gf(x) = fg(x). Give your answers in the form p ± √q.
ms: M1 x² - 6x + 6 = 0 and attempts to solve (completing the square or formula)
questions.tip: gf means f first: (2x - 3)². fg means g first: 2x² - 3. Mixing them up loses every mark.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] n is an integer. Which expression is always odd?
ms: 2n is always even, so 2n + 1 is always odd.
questions.tip: Always odd means it must work for every integer n, so test odd and even n.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] n is an integer. Which statement about (n + 1)² - n² is correct?
options: It equals 2n + 1, so it is always even
It equals 2n + 1, so it is always odd
It equals 1, so it is always 1
It equals 2n, so it is always even
questions.tip: Expand fully. (n + 1)² is not n² + 1.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove that the sum of any three consecutive integers is a multiple of 3.
ms: M1 uses n, n + 1, n + 2 (or equivalent)
A1 3(n + 1) with conclusion that it is a multiple of 3
questions.tip: Examples are not a proof. Use algebra and finish with a conclusion sentence.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove that (3n + 1)² - (3n - 1)² is a multiple of 12 for all positive integer values of n.
ms: M1 expands at least one bracket correctly
A1 states 12n is a multiple of 12 (since n is an integer)
questions.tip: Bracket the second expansion so all its signs change.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove that the sum of the squares of any two consecutive integers is always odd.
ms: A1 2(n² + n) + 1 with conclusion: one more than a multiple of 2 so odd
questions.tip: Show the 2( ) + 1 form explicitly, then say why it is odd.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove that the difference between the squares of any two consecutive odd numbers is a multiple of 8.
ms: M1 uses two consecutive odd numbers e.g. 2n + 1 and 2n + 3
questions.tip: 2n + 1 and 2n + 2 are not both odd. Consecutive odd numbers differ by 2.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove that the product of two consecutive odd numbers is always one less than a multiple of 4.
ms: A1 conclusion: 4n² is a multiple of 4 so the product is one less than a multiple of 4
questions.tip: Write the result in the exact form the question asks for: 4( ) - 1.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove that x² - 6x + 11 > 0 for all values of x.
ms: A1 argues (x - 3)² ≥ 0 so the expression is at least 2, which is always positive
questions.tip: Completing the square is the key. You must explain why a square can never be negative.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove that the square of any odd number is always 1 more than a multiple of 8.
questions.answer: (2n + 1)² = 4n² + 4n + 1 = 4n(n + 1) + 1. n(n + 1) is even so 4n(n + 1) is a multiple of 8.
ms: A1 states n(n + 1) is the product of consecutive integers so is even
A1 concludes 4n(n + 1) = 8k so the square is 8k + 1
questions.tip: The grade 9 step: one of n and n + 1 must be even, so 4 × even is a multiple of 8.

questions.q: [Calculator] f(x) = x³ + x - 3. Which statement correctly shows that f(x) = 0 has a solution between x = 1 and x = 2?
options: f(1) = -1 and f(2) = 7, both less than 10
f(1) = -1 and f(2) = 7, there is a change of sign
f(1) = 1 and f(2) = 2, so the root is 1.5
f(1) = 3 and f(2) = 13, there is a change of sign
ms: f(1) = 1 + 1 - 3 = -1 and f(2) = 8 + 2 - 3 = 7. The sign changes and f is continuous, so there is a root between.
questions.tip: State the values AND say 'change of sign'.

questions.q: [Calculator] Using xₙ₊₁ = 7/(xₙ² + 4) with x₀ = 1, find x₂. Give your answer to 4 decimal places.
questions.tip: Use the ANS key so you do not round between steps.

questions.q: [Calculator] Using xₙ₊₁ = ∛(xₙ + 5) with x₀ = 2, find the values of x₁, x₂ and x₃. Give each to 4 decimal places.
questions.tip: Use ANS on your calculator. Rounding each value before the next step can change the 4th decimal place.

questions.q: [Calculator] Show that the equation x³ + 4x - 7 = 0 has a solution between x = 1 and x = 2.
questions.answer: f(1) = -2 < 0 and f(2) = 9 > 0, change of sign so a root lies between 1 and 2
ms: M1 substitutes x = 1 and x = 2 giving -2 and 9
A1 states there is a change of sign so a solution between 1 and 2
questions.tip: You need both values and the words 'change of sign'.

questions.q: [Calculator] Show that the equation x³ + 4x - 7 = 0 has a solution of x = 1.26 correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.answer: f(1.255) = -0.0033... < 0 and f(1.265) = 0.0843... > 0, change of sign so root rounds to 1.26
ms: A1 f(1.255) = -0.0033... and f(1.265) = 0.0843... (allow truncated values)
A1 change of sign, so 1.255 < x < 1.265 and x = 1.26 to 2 d.p.
questions.tip: Test the BOUNDS 1.255 and 1.265, not 1.25 and 1.27. That is what proves the 2 d.p. value.

questions.q:
[Calculator] (a) Show that the equation x³ - 3x - 5 = 0 can be rearranged to give x = ∛(3x + 5) (1)
(b) Using xₙ₊₁ = ∛(3xₙ + 5) with x₀ = 2, find the values of x₁, x₂ and x₃ to 4 decimal places. (3)
(c) Explain what the values of x₁, x₂ and x₃ represent. (1)
(d) Use your answer to (b) to suggest the solution to 1 decimal place. (1)
questions.answer: (a) x³ = 3x + 5 so x = ∛(3x + 5) (b) 2.2240, 2.2684, 2.2770 (c) estimates of a solution of x³ - 3x - 5 = 0 getting closer to it (d) 2.3
ms: B1 x³ = 3x + 5 then cube root both sides
B1 they are successive approximations to a solution of x³ - 3x - 5 = 0
questions.tip: In (c), say they are estimates of the solution of the ORIGINAL equation, not just 'answers'.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Using xₙ₊₁ = 5 - 2/xₙ with x₀ = 4
(a) find x₁, x₂ and x₃, giving x₂ and x₃ to 4 decimal places. (2)
(b) The iteration converges to a value α. Show that α is a solution of x² - 5x + 2 = 0. (2)
(c) Find the exact value of α. (1)
ms: A1 multiplies by α and rearranges to α² - 5α + 2 = 0
questions.tip: When an iteration converges, xₙ₊₁ and xₙ both become the same number, so replace both with x.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What are the gradient and y-intercept of the line 2y = 6x - 8?
questions.tip: Get y on its own first, then read off m and c.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the gradient of a line perpendicular to y = 4x - 1?
questions.tip: Negative reciprocal: flip AND change the sign.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find the equation of the line that passes through (2, 5) and (6, 13).
questions.tip: Gradient is change in y over change in x. Then substitute a point to find c.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find the equation of the line that passes through (3, -1) and is perpendicular to y = (3/2)x + 4.
questions.tip: Find the perpendicular gradient first, then use the point.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find the equation of the line parallel to 3x + 2y = 7 that passes through (4, -1).
ms: M1 rearranges to y = -3x/2 + 7/2 so gradient -3/2
questions.tip: Parallel lines have the same gradient. Rearrange first; the gradient is not 3.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A is the point (-2, 1) and B is the point (4, 9).
Find the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB. Give your answer in the form ax + by = c, where a, b and c are integers.
ms: M1 perpendicular gradient -3/4 used with the midpoint
questions.tip: Perpendicular bisector = perpendicular gradient through the MIDPOINT.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The line L₁ has equation y = 2x + 4 and crosses the x-axis at A.
The line L₂ is perpendicular to L₁ and passes through B(6, 0).
L₁ and L₂ intersect at P.
Work out the area of triangle ABP.
questions.tip: The base AB lies on the x-axis, so the height is the y-coordinate of P.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Where does the graph of y = (x - 3)(x + 5) cross the x-axis?
ms: Set each bracket to zero: x = 3, x = -5
questions.tip: The signs flip when you solve each bracket = 0.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What are the coordinates of the turning point of y = (x - 4)² + 7?
questions.tip: (x - a)² + b has turning point (a, b). Note the sign of a.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The graph of y = x² - 6x + 8 is drawn.
Find the coordinates of the points where the graph crosses the axes.
questions.tip: The y-intercept is the constant term. Roots come from solving y = 0.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] By completing the square, find the coordinates of the turning point of y = x² + 10x + 18.
questions.tip: Turning point x is the opposite sign of the number in the bracket.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y = -2x² + 8x + 3
Find the coordinates of the turning point of the graph and state whether it is a maximum or a minimum. You must show your working.
ms: B1 maximum, because the coefficient of x² is negative
questions.tip: Factor out -2 from the x terms only. -2 × -4 = +8 is added back.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A quadratic graph crosses the x-axis at x = -1 and x = 5 and crosses the y-axis at (0, -10).
(a) Find the equation of the graph in the form y = ax² + bx + c. (2)
(b) Find the coordinates of the turning point. (2)
questions.tip: The turning point is halfway between the roots by symmetry.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A ball is thrown upwards. Its height, h metres, after t seconds is h = 1 + 20t - 5t².
(a) Find the maximum height of the ball. (3)
(b) Find the time when the ball hits the ground. Give your answer to 2 decimal places. (2)
questions.tip: Time cannot be negative, so reject the negative solution with a reason.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Describe the transformation that maps y = f(x) onto y = f(x) + 3.
ms: Adding outside the function moves the graph up: vector (0, 3).
questions.tip: Outside the bracket affects y, in the expected direction.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The point (5, 1) lies on y = f(x). Which point lies on y = f(x - 2)?
ms: f(x - 2) is a translation 2 units right: (7, 1).
questions.tip: Inside the bracket works the opposite way to what you expect: x - 2 means RIGHT 2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The point P(4, -3) lies on the curve y = f(x).
Write down the coordinates of the image of P on
(a) y = -f(x) (1)
(b) y = f(-x) (1)
questions.tip: -f(x) reflects in the x-axis (y changes sign). f(-x) reflects in the y-axis (x changes sign).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The curve y = f(x) has a turning point at (2, 5).
Write down the coordinates of the turning point of
(a) y = f(x + 3) (1)
(b) y = f(x) - 4 (1)
questions.tip: f(x + 3) moves LEFT 3, not right.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The graph of y = x² is transformed to the graph of y = x² - 6x + 4.
Describe fully the single transformation.
questions.tip: Complete the square first. 'Describe fully' needs the word translation AND the vector.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The curve y = f(x) has a minimum point at (3, -2).
(a) Write down the coordinates of the turning point of y = f(-x) - 1, and state its nature. (2)
(b) Write down the coordinates of the turning point of y = -f(x + 2), and state its nature. (2)
questions.tip: A reflection in the x-axis turns a minimum into a maximum; a reflection in the y-axis does not.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = x² - 4x + 7
The graph of y = g(x) is the graph of y = f(x) translated 1 unit left and then reflected in the x-axis, then translated 3 units up.
So g(x) = -f(x + 1) + 3.
Show that g(x) = -(x - 1)² and hence write down the coordinates of the turning point of y = g(x).
questions.answer: f(x + 1) = x² - 2x + 4, so g(x) = -x² + 2x - 1 = -(x - 1)². Turning point (1, 0), a maximum.
questions.tip: Substitute (x + 1) for every x, using brackets, before simplifying.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the radius of the circle x² + y² = 49?
questions.tip: The number on the right is r², not r.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which point lies on the circle x² + y² = 25?
questions.tip: Substitute and check the total equals 25.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (a) Write down the equation of the circle with centre (0, 0) and radius 6. (1)
(b) Does the point (4, 5) lie inside or outside this circle? Give a reason. (1)
questions.tip: Compare x² + y² with r² to decide inside, on or outside.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The point P(3, 4) lies on the circle x² + y² = 25.
Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at P.
questions.tip: The tangent is perpendicular to the RADIUS at the point of contact.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The circle C has centre the origin and passes through P(-8, 6).
(a) Write down the equation of C. (1)
(b) The tangent to C at P meets the y-axis at Q. Find the coordinates of Q. (3)
ms: M1 gradient OP = -3/4 so tangent gradient 4/3
questions.tip: Gradient of radius from (0, 0) to (-8, 6) is 6/(-8). Watch the sign.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The point P(2, -4) lies on the circle x² + y² = 20.
The tangent to the circle at P crosses the x-axis at A and the y-axis at B.
O is the origin.
Work out the area of triangle OAB.
questions.tip: Area uses lengths, so use 5 not -5 for the height.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Show that the line y = x + 10 is a tangent to the circle x² + y² = 50, and find the coordinates of the point where it touches the circle.
questions.answer: x² + (x + 10)² = 50 gives (x + 5)² = 0, one repeated root so tangent at (-5, 5)
ms: A1 (x + 5)² = 0, only one solution so the line is a tangent
questions.tip: A tangent meets the circle at exactly one point, so the quadratic has a repeated root.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A distance-time graph is a straight line from (0, 0) to (4, 20), where time is in hours and distance in km. What is the speed?
questions.tip: Speed is the gradient: distance ÷ time.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What does the area under a velocity-time graph represent?
questions.tip: Gradient of a velocity-time graph is acceleration; area is distance.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A car accelerates uniformly from rest to 18 m/s in 6 seconds.
(a) Work out the acceleration. (1)
(b) Work out the distance travelled in the 6 seconds. (2)
questions.tip: Distance is the area of the triangle: 1/2 × base × height.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cyclist's velocity-time graph has three straight sections:
from (0, 0) to (10, 20), then horizontal from (10, 20) to (30, 20), then from (30, 20) to (40, 0).
Time is in seconds and velocity in m/s.
(a) Work out the total distance travelled. (3)
(b) Work out the average speed for the whole journey. (1)
ms: M1 correct area of at least one section, e.g. 1/2 × 10 × 20 (= 100) or 20 × 20 (= 400), or uses the trapezium formula
M1 complete method for the total area: 100 + 400 + 100 or 1/2 × (20 + 40) × 20
questions.tip: The whole shape is one trapezium: 1/2 × (a + b) × h with parallel sides 20 and 40.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The velocity of a particle, v m/s, at time t seconds is shown in the table.
t: 0 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8
v: 0 | 8 | 12 | 12 | 8
The graph of v against t is a smooth curve that bends downwards (it is concave).
(a) Use 4 strips of equal width to estimate the distance travelled in the first 8 seconds. (3)
(b) Is your answer an overestimate or an underestimate? Give a reason. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 72 m (b) underestimate, the straight tops of the trapezia lie below the curve
ms: M1 splits into 4 trapezia (or triangle + trapezia) of width 2
B1 underestimate with reason that the curve is above the chords
questions.tip: For a curve bending downwards, the straight-line tops cut below it, so the area is underestimated.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The depth, d cm, of water in a tank after t minutes is d = 0.5t² + 2.
(a) Work out the average rate of increase of depth between t = 2 and t = 6. (2)
(b) A tangent to the curve at t = 4 passes through (4, 10) and (6, 18). Estimate the rate of increase of depth at t = 4, and say what it represents. (2)
questions.answer: (a) 4 cm/min (b) 4 cm/min, the instantaneous rate at which the depth is increasing at 4 minutes
ms: A1 4 cm per minute, the rate the depth increases at exactly t = 4
questions.tip: Average rate uses a chord; instantaneous rate uses a tangent. Always include units.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A particle starts from rest and accelerates uniformly to V m/s in 8 seconds.
It travels at V m/s for 12 seconds.
It then decelerates uniformly to rest in 5 seconds.
The total distance travelled is 370 m.
(a) Find V. (3)
(b) Work out the acceleration in the first 8 seconds. (2)
questions.tip: Sketch the graph and use area = distance to form an equation in V.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which of these equations has a reciprocal graph?
ms: y = k/x is a reciprocal graph with asymptotes x = 0 and y = 0.
questions.tip: y = 3^x is exponential; y = x³ is cubic.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The curve y = abˣ passes through (0, 5) and (2, 45), where b > 0. Find a and b.
ms: x = 0 gives a = 5. Then 5b² = 45 so b² = 9, b = 3.
questions.tip: b⁰ = 1, so the point with x = 0 gives a directly.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Complete the table of values for y = x³ - 2x
x: -2 | -1 | 0 | 1 | 2
y: ? | ? | ? | ? | ?
questions.tip: Cube negatives carefully: (-2)³ = -8, so -8 + 4 = -4.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write down the equations of the asymptotes of the graph of y = 1/x.
questions.tip: An asymptote is a line the curve approaches but never meets. Give equations, not just 'the axes'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The graph of y = (x - 1)(x + 2)(x - 3) is a cubic curve.
(a) Write down the x-coordinates where it crosses the x-axis. (1)
(b) Find where it crosses the y-axis. (1)
(c) Describe what happens to y as x becomes large and positive. (1)
ms: B1 y increases without limit (curve goes up to the right since the x³ coefficient is positive)
questions.tip: y-intercept: substitute x = 0 into all three brackets: (-1)(2)(-3) = 6.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The value of a painting, £V, t years after 2020 is modelled by V = A × kᵗ.
In 2020 the painting was worth £4000. In 2023 it was worth £5324.
(a) Find the values of A and k. (2)
(b) Use the model to predict the value of the painting in 2030. Give your answer to the nearest pound. (2)

[Non-calculator] The curve y = pqˣ passes through the points (1, 6) and (3, 54), where q > 0.
(a) Find p and q. (3)
(b) Find y when x = -1. (1)
questions.tip: Divide the two equations to eliminate p. 3⁻¹ = 1/3, so y = 2/3.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] £360 is shared between Amir and Bella in the ratio 4 : 5. How much does Bella get?
questions.tip: Add the ratio parts first (4 + 5 = 9). £160 is Amir's share, not Bella's.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Sweets are shared between Cal and Dev in the ratio 3 : 7. Dev gets 48 more sweets than Cal. How many sweets are there altogether?
ms: Difference is 7 - 3 = 4 parts = 48, so 1 part = 12. Total = 10 × 12 = 120.
questions.tip: The 48 is the difference, so it matches 4 parts, not 10 parts.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] a : b = 2 : 3 and b : c = 4 : 5. Find a : b : c in its simplest form.
ms: Make b the same: 2:3 = 8:12 and 4:5 = 12:15, so a:b:c = 8:12:15.
questions.tip: Scale both ratios so the shared letter has the same number (LCM of 3 and 4 is 12).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In a club, the ratio of boys to girls is 5 : 3. There are 64 members. 8 more girls join the club and no one leaves.
Find the new ratio of boys to girls. Give your answer in its simplest form.
ms: M1 for 64 ÷ 8 = 8 (value of one part) or for 40 boys or 24 girls
A1 for 5 : 4 (accept 40 : 32 for M1 M1 only)
questions.tip: Leaving the answer as 40 : 32 loses the final mark when the question says simplest form.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains red and blue counters in the ratio 3 : 5.
12 red counters are added to the bag. The ratio of red to blue counters is now 6 : 5.
How many counters were in the bag at the start?
ms: M1 for setting up red = 3x, blue = 5x (or equivalent use of parts)
M1 for solving to get x = 4
questions.tip: The blue counters do not change, so keep 5x the same in both ratios and form an equation.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Cereal is sold in two sizes.
Small box: 400 g for £2.60
Large box: 750 g for £4.50
Which box is better value for money? You must show your working.
questions.answer: Large box (60p per 100 g vs 65p per 100 g)
ms: M1 for a correct comparable unit price for one box, e.g. 2.60 ÷ 4 = 0.65 per 100 g, or 400 ÷ 2.60 = 153.8 g per £1
M1 for a correct comparable unit price for the other box, e.g. 4.50 ÷ 7.5 = 0.60 per 100 g, or 750 ÷ 4.50 = 166.7 g per £1
A1 for Large box, with correct comparable figures
questions.tip: A bare answer with no comparable figures scores zero. Compare the same unit for both.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] At a concert, 2/5 of the audience are adults and the rest are children.
The ratio of men to women among the adults is 3 : 1.
There are 18 women. How many people are in the audience?
questions.tip: Work out the number of adults first, then use the fraction 2/5 to get back to the whole audience.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The ratio of Ella's age to Finn's age is 2 : 3.
In 5 years' time the ratio of their ages will be 3 : 4.
Work out Ella's age now.
questions.tip: Add the 5 years to both ages. Cross-multiply the ratio to form a linear equation.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] x : y = 7 : 2. Which of these is true?
questions.tip: Cross-multiply carefully: x : y = 7 : 2 means 2x = 7y, not 7x = 2y.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Lilac paint is made by mixing white paint and blue paint in the ratio 3 : 2 by volume.
White paint costs £6 per litre and blue paint costs £11 per litre.
Work out the cost of making 20 litres of lilac paint.
ms: M1 for 20 ÷ 5 = 4, giving 12 litres white or 8 litres blue
questions.tip: Split the 20 litres in the ratio before multiplying by the prices.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] y is directly proportional to x. When x = 4, y = 12. Find y when x = 7.
questions.tip: Find k first. Do not just add 3 to 12 because x went up by 3.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] 6 workers take 15 days to build a wall. How long would 9 workers take, working at the same rate?
questions.tip: More workers means fewer days: this is inverse proportion, so do not scale up.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y is directly proportional to the square of x. When x = 5, y = 50.
Find the value of y when x = 8.
ms: M1 for y = kx² (allow y ∝ x² stated with k)
questions.tip: Square x before dividing to find k: 50 ÷ 5 = 10 is a common wrong k.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] F is inversely proportional to the square of d. When d = 3, F = 20.
(a) Find a formula for F in terms of d.
(b) Find the positive value of d when F = 5.
questions.tip: Inversely proportional to the square means k/d², not k/d and not kd².

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which equation describes y being inversely proportional to x?
ms: Inverse proportion: y = k/x. Its graph is a curve that never touches the axes.
questions.tip: y = x + 4 is linear but not proportional because it does not pass through the origin.

questions.q: [Calculator] y is directly proportional to x². x is increased by 20%. What is the percentage increase in y?
ms: New y = k(1.2x)² = 1.44kx², so y increases by 44%.
questions.tip: Square the multiplier (1.2² = 1.44), do not just double the percentage.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The time, t seconds, for an object to fall a distance h metres is directly proportional to the square root of h.
When h = 25, t = 2.
(a) Find a formula for t in terms of h.
(b) Find h when t = 3.
questions.tip: Once you have √h, remember to square it to get h.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] a is directly proportional to b². b is inversely proportional to c.
When b = 2, a = 8. When c = 1, b = 6.
Find the value of a when c = 4.
ms: M1 for a = kb² with k = 2, i.e. a = 2b²
M1 for b = m/c with m = 6, i.e. b = 6/c
questions.tip: Use two separate constants of proportionality. Find b from c first, then a from b.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A car travels 150 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. What is its average speed?
questions.tip: 2 hours 30 minutes is 2.5 hours, not 2.3 hours (which gives 65.2).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Aluminium has a density of 2.7 g/cm³. A block has mass 540 g. What is its volume?
questions.tip: Use the formula triangle: V = M ÷ D. Multiplying gives 1458, which is the wrong way round.

questions.q: [Calculator] A box exerts a force of 600 N on an area of 1.5 m². What pressure does it exert?
questions.tip: Pressure = F/A. Larger area means smaller pressure.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A cyclist travels at 15 m/s. Change this speed to km/h.
questions.tip: Multiply by 3600 to go from per second to per hour, then divide by 1000 for km.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Priya drives 90 km at an average speed of 60 km/h. She then drives a further 40 km at an average speed of 80 km/h.
Work out her average speed for the whole journey.
questions.tip: Average speed is total distance ÷ total time. Averaging 60 and 80 to get 70 scores zero.

questions.q:
[Calculator] An alloy is made by melting together 20 cm³ of metal A and 30 cm³ of metal B.
Metal A has density 8 g/cm³. Metal B has density 3 g/cm³.
Work out the density of the alloy. (Assume the volume does not change.)
questions.tip: Work out total mass and total volume. Do not average the two densities (5.5 is wrong).

questions.q:
[Calculator] A solid cuboid measures 2 m by 0.5 m by 0.4 m.
When it rests on its smallest face, it exerts a pressure of 1500 N/m² on the ground.
Work out the pressure when it rests on its largest face.
ms: M1 for smallest face area 0.5 × 0.4 = 0.2 m²
M1 for largest face area 2 × 0.5 = 1 m² and 300 ÷ 1
questions.tip: The force (weight) stays the same whichever face it rests on. Only the area changes.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A water tank holds 1.2 m³ of water when full. Water flows into the empty tank at 15 litres per minute.
1 m³ = 1000 litres.
How long does it take to fill the tank? Give your answer in hours and minutes.
questions.tip: 80 minutes is not 1 hour 80 minutes or 1.8 hours. Convert carefully.

questions.q: [Calculator] £5000 is invested at 3% compound interest per year. Which calculation gives the value after 4 years?
ms: Compound interest uses the multiplier 1.03 raised to the number of years.
questions.tip: 5000 + 5000 × 0.03 × 4 is simple interest.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A car is bought for £18 000. Its value depreciates by 15% each year.
Work out the value of the car after 3 years.
questions.tip: Do not subtract 45%. Depreciation compounds, so use 0.85³.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Sam invests £2000 at 4.5% compound interest per year.
What is the least number of whole years before the investment is worth more than £2500?
ms: M1 for 2000 × 1.045ⁿ with at least one trial, e.g. 2000 × 1.045⁵ = 2492.36
M1 for 2000 × 1.045⁶ = 2604.52 (or both 5 and 6 values compared with 2500)
questions.tip: Show the values for both years either side of 2500 so the examiner can see your decision.

questions.q: [Calculator] After an 8% increase, the price of a laptop is £1404. What was the price before the increase?
questions.tip: Do not take 8% off £1404 (that gives £1291.68). Divide by the multiplier.

questions.q: [Calculator] A colony has 8000 bacteria. The number increases by 12% each hour. How many bacteria are there after 5 hours, to 3 significant figures?
questions.tip: 12 800 is simple growth (12% × 5 = 60%). Growth compounds.

questions.q:
[Calculator] An investment grows from £2000 to £2420 in 2 years at a fixed rate of compound interest.
Work out the annual rate of interest.
questions.tip: Find the overall multiplier first, then take the square root because there are 2 years. 10.5% (21% ÷ 2) is wrong.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The value of a house was £40 000 in 1990.
The value increased by 5% per year for 2 years, then decreased by 3% per year for the next 3 years.
Work out the value of the house at the end of the 5 years. Give your answer to the nearest pound.
questions.tip: Apply each multiplier the correct number of times. Do not combine as a 2% change per year.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A machine loses 20% of its value each year. After 3 years it is worth £2560.
Work out its value when it was new.
questions.tip: Work backwards by dividing by the multiplier. Adding 60% to £2560 is wrong.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 20°. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.tip: 160° is the interior angle, not the number of sides.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the sum of the interior angles of a decagon (10 sides)?
questions.tip: Use (n - 2) × 180, not n × 180. 144° is one interior angle of a regular decagon.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The interior angle of a regular polygon is 150°.
Work out the number of sides of the polygon.
questions.tip: Convert to the exterior angle first, because exterior angles always add to 360°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Lines AB and CD are parallel. A straight line EF crosses AB at P and CD at Q, with E above AB and F below CD. B and D are on the same side of EF.
Angle EPB = 68°. Work out the size of angle PQD. Give a reason for each stage of your working.
ms: B1 for a correct reason: corresponding angles are equal
B1 for a fully correct chain of reasons (e.g. angle APQ = 68° as vertically opposite angles are equal, then angle PQD = 68° as alternate angles are equal, or corresponding angles stated directly)
questions.tip: Use the proper words: 'corresponding', 'alternate', 'co-interior'. 'F angles' or 'Z angles' do not score.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A regular pentagon and a regular hexagon share a common side AB. They are drawn on opposite sides of AB.
C is the vertex of the pentagon next to B (not A), and D is the vertex of the hexagon next to B (not A).
Work out the size of angle CBD, measured outside both shapes.
ms: M1 for interior angle of pentagon = 108° or of hexagon = 120°
questions.tip: Learn how to find interior angles: (n - 2) × 180 ÷ n.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle ABC has side BC extended to point D. Angle BAC = x and angle ABC = y.
Prove that angle ACD = x + y. Give reasons.
questions.answer: Angle ACB = 180 - x - y (angles in a triangle sum to 180°). Angle ACD = 180 - (180 - x - y) = x + y (angles on a straight line sum to 180°).
ms: M1 for angle ACB = 180° - x - y
M1 for angle ACD = 180° - angle ACB = x + y
A1 for both reasons stated: angles in a triangle add up to 180°, and angles on a straight line add up to 180°
questions.tip: A proof must be in terms of x and y, not numbers. Every step needs a reason.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The interior angle of a regular polygon is 4 times the size of its exterior angle. How many sides does it have?
questions.tip: Interior + exterior = 180°. Set up e + 4e = 180.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] ABCDEF is a regular hexagon. Prove that angle ACD = 90°. Give reasons for each step.
questions.answer: Interior angle = 120°. Triangle ABC is isosceles (AB = BC), so angle BCA = (180 - 120) ÷ 2 = 30°. Angle ACD = 120 - 30 = 90°.
ms: B1 for interior angle of regular hexagon = 120° (from (6 - 2) × 180 ÷ 6 or 180 - 360/6)
M1 for angle BCA = 30° using triangle ABC isosceles because AB = BC (sides of a regular hexagon are equal)
A1 for 90° with reasons: base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal, angles in a triangle add to 180°
questions.tip: Say why triangle ABC is isosceles. Without the reason the proof is incomplete.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Points A, B and C lie on a circle with centre O. Angle AOB = 130° (at the centre). C is on the major arc. What is angle ACB?
ms: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference, so ACB = 130 ÷ 2 = 65°.
questions.tip: Halve the angle at the centre. Do not double it.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. Angle ABC = 74°. What is angle ADC?
ms: Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°, so ADC = 180 - 74 = 106°.
questions.tip: Opposite angles add to 180°, they are not equal.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] AB is a diameter of a circle and C is a point on the circumference. Angle CAB = 35°. What is angle CBA?
ms: Angle ACB = 90° (angle in a semicircle). CBA = 180 - 90 - 35 = 55°.
questions.tip: Spot the diameter: the angle opposite it at the circumference is 90°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A and B are points on a circle with centre O. PA and PB are tangents to the circle from an external point P. Angle APB = 48°.
Work out the size of angle AOB. Give a reason for each stage of your working.
ms: M1 for angle OAP = angle OBP = 90°
B1 for reasons: tangent is perpendicular to the radius (at the point of contact) and angles in a quadrilateral add to 360°
questions.tip: Write the full reason 'the tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius'. Just 'tangent' does not score.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B, C and D lie on a circle. AC and BD are chords that cross at X. Angle BAC = 31° and angle ABD = 47°.
(a) Find angle BDC. Give a reason.
(b) Find angle ACD. Give a reason.
ms: B1 for reason: angles in the same segment are equal (angles subtended by the same arc are equal)
B1 for reason: angles in the same segment are equal
questions.tip: Identify the chord both angles stand on. BAC and BDC both stand on chord BC.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B and C lie on a circle. The straight line TAS is a tangent to the circle at A. B is on the same side of the circle as T, and C is on the same side as S.
Angle TAB = 58° and angle BAC = 70°.
Find angle ABC. Give reasons for your answer.
ms: M1 for angle CAS = 180 - 58 - 70 = 52° (angles on a straight line add to 180°)
B1 for reason: alternate segment theorem (the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment)
questions.tip: Pair the tangent-chord angle with the angle at the circumference in the opposite segment.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B and C are points on a circle with centre O. Angle OAC = x and angle OBC = y, with O inside triangle ABC.
Prove that angle AOB = 2 × angle ACB. Do not quote the theorem 'angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference'.
questions.answer: OA = OC = OB (radii), so triangles OAC and OBC are isosceles: angle OCA = x, angle OCB = y, so angle ACB = x + y. Angle AOC = 180 - 2x, angle BOC = 180 - 2y. Angle AOB = 360 - (180 - 2x) - (180 - 2y) = 2x + 2y = 2(x + y) = 2 × angle ACB.
ms: M1 for angle OCA = x and angle OCB = y, with reason: OA = OC = OB (radii), so base angles of isosceles triangles are equal
M1 for angle AOC = 180 - 2x and angle BOC = 180 - 2y (angles in a triangle add to 180°)
M1 for angle AOB = 360 - (180 - 2x) - (180 - 2y) (angles around a point add to 360°)
A1 for 2x + 2y = 2(x + y) = 2 × angle ACB, with all reasons given
questions.tip: A proof must state why the triangles are isosceles (radii are equal). Missing reasons lose the final mark.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B and C are points on a circle with centre O. C lies on the major arc AB. Angle OBA = 24°.
Work out the size of angle ACB. Give reasons for each stage of your working.
ms: M1 for angle OAB = 24° (OA = OB as radii, so triangle OAB is isosceles)
M1 for angle AOB = 180 - 24 - 24 = 132° (angles in a triangle add to 180°)
B1 for reason: the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference
questions.tip: Join to the centre and look for isosceles triangles made by two radii.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. The line PCQ is a tangent to the circle at C, with P on the same side of C as B.
Angle ADC = 100° and angle PCB = 40°.
Work out the size of angle ACB. Give reasons for each stage of your working.
ms: B1 for reason: opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°
B1 for reason: alternate segment theorem
A1 for angle ACB = 180 - 80 - 40 = 60° (angles in a triangle add up to 180°)
questions.tip: The tangent PC and chord CB make an angle equal to angle CAB in the alternate segment.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A circle has centre O and radius 13 cm. A chord AB has length 24 cm. What is the perpendicular distance from O to AB?
ms: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord, so half chord = 12. √(13² - 12²) = 5 cm.
questions.tip: Halve the chord before using Pythagoras.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which of these is NOT a valid condition for proving two triangles congruent?
ms: AAA shows triangles are similar, but they can be different sizes, so it does not prove congruence.
questions.tip: The valid conditions are SSS, SAS, ASA (or AAS) and RHS.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Triangles PQR and XYZ are similar. PQ = 9 cm corresponds to XY = 15 cm. QR = 6 cm. Find YZ.
questions.tip: Adding 6 to each side (giving 12) is wrong. Similar shapes use multiplication.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Two similar shapes have lengths in the ratio 1 : 3. The smaller shape has area 20 cm². What is the area of the larger shape?
questions.tip: Square the length scale factor for area and cube it for volume.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two mathematically similar containers have surface areas of 160 cm² and 360 cm².
The volume of the smaller container is 240 cm³.
Work out the volume of the larger container.
questions.tip: Go area → length (square root) → volume (cube). Multiplying 240 by 2.25 is the common wrong answer.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Two solid cones are mathematically similar. The smaller cone has volume 54 cm³ and height 12 cm. The larger cone has volume 250 cm³.
Work out the height of the larger cone.
questions.tip: Volume ratio must be cube-rooted to get the length scale factor.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In triangle ABC, D is a point on CA and E is a point on CB such that DE is parallel to AB.
CD = 4 cm, DA = 6 cm and DE = 5 cm.
Work out the length of AB.
ms: M1 for CA = 10 cm (or recognising triangles CDE and CAB are similar)
questions.tip: Use CA = CD + DA, not DA alone. The scale factor is 10/4, not 6/4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCD is a parallelogram. The diagonal AC is drawn.
Prove that triangle ABC is congruent to triangle CDA.
questions.answer: AB = CD (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal). BC = DA (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal). AC is common to both triangles. So the triangles are congruent (SSS).
ms: B1 for one pair of equal sides with reason, e.g. AB = CD (opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal)
B1 for the other pair, BC = DA, and AC is a common side
B1 for a full proof concluding congruent with condition SSS (allow SAS or ASA if alternate angles are correctly used with reasons)
questions.tip: State the congruence condition at the end, e.g. 'congruent by SSS'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCD is a square. Point P lies outside the square so that triangle ABP is equilateral. Point Q lies outside the square so that triangle BCQ is equilateral.
Prove that AQ = CP.
questions.answer: AB = BC (sides of a square). BP = AB and BQ = BC (equilateral triangles), so BP = BQ. Angle ABQ = 90 + 60 = 150° and angle PBC = 60 + 90 = 150°. So triangles ABQ and PBC are congruent (SAS), so AQ = PC.
ms: B1 for AB = BC with reason (sides of a square are equal)
B1 for BQ = BP (equal to the sides of the square, as the triangles are equilateral)
B1 for angle ABQ = angle PBC = 150° (90° + 60°)
B1 for triangles ABQ and PBC congruent by SAS, therefore AQ = CP (corresponding sides of congruent triangles)
questions.tip: Pick the two triangles that contain AQ and CP. Show the included angle matches.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Two similar cylinders have volumes in the ratio 8 : 27. What is the ratio of their curved surface areas?
questions.tip: Cube root the volume ratio to get lengths, then square for areas.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A right-angled triangle has shorter sides 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.tip: Square, add, then square root. Do not just add the sides.

questions.q: [Calculator] In triangle ABC, angle B = 90°, AC = 12 cm and angle A = 35°. Find BC to 3 significant figures.
ms: BC is opposite angle A and AC is the hypotenuse: BC = 12 sin 35° = 6.88 cm.
questions.tip: Label O, A, H from the given angle. 9.83 comes from using cos.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the exact value of tan 60°?
questions.tip: Learn the exact values table: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle PQR has angle Q = 90°, angle P = 30° and PR = 10 cm.
(a) Find the exact length of QR.
(b) Find the exact length of PQ. Give your answer as a surd.
questions.tip: 'Exact' means leave it as a surd. Simplify √75 to 5√3.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A ladder leans against a vertical wall. The foot of the ladder is 4 m from the wall and the top is 7 m up the wall.
Work out the angle the ladder makes with the ground. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: Check your calculator is in degrees mode (D on screen).

questions.q:
[Calculator] ABCDEFGH is a cuboid. The base ABCD is horizontal with AB = 8 cm and BC = 6 cm. The vertical edges AE, BF, CG and DH are each 5 cm long.
(a) Work out the length of the diagonal AG.
(b) Work out the angle between AG and the base ABCD.
Give your answers to 1 decimal place.
ms: M1 for tan θ = 5/10 (or sin θ = 5/11.18)
questions.tip: The angle with the base is between AG and AC (its projection on the base), not AB.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A pyramid VABCD has a square base ABCD of side 6 cm. The apex V is vertically above the centre M of the base. Each sloping edge (VA, VB, VC, VD) is 9 cm.
(a) Work out the height VM.
(b) Work out the angle between VA and the base.
Give your answers to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for cos θ = √18/9 or tan θ = 7.94/4.243 or sin θ = 7.94/9
questions.tip: AM is half the diagonal of the base, not half the side (3 cm).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In triangle ABC, angle ABC = 90°, AB = 4√3 cm and angle BAC = 30°.
Show that BC = 4 cm and find the exact length of AC.
ms: B1 for AC = 8 cm (from cos 30°, or √(48 + 16) = √64)
questions.tip: Use the exact value 1/√3 for tan 30° and simplify √3/√3 = 1.

questions.q: [Calculator] In triangle ABC, AB = 7 cm, BC = 9 cm and angle ABC = 50°. Find AC to 3 significant figures.
ms: Cosine rule: AC² = 7² + 9² - 2 × 7 × 9 × cos 50° = 49.0..., AC = 7.00 cm.
questions.tip: Remember the square root at the end (49.0 is AC²), and the minus sign in the rule (14.5 uses +).

questions.q: [Calculator] Triangle PQR has PQ = 8 cm, PR = 11 cm and angle QPR = 35°. What is its area to 3 s.f.?
questions.tip: Use ½ab sin C with the angle between the two sides. Forgetting the ½ gives 50.5.

questions.q:
[Calculator] In triangle ABC, angle A = 40°, angle B = 65° and the side AC = 12 cm.
Work out the length of BC. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.tip: Pair each side with the angle opposite it. AC is opposite angle B.

questions.q:
[Calculator] In triangle PQR, PR = 10 cm, QR = 8.5 cm and angle QPR = 48°. Angle PQR is acute.
Work out the size of angle PQR. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: Put the angles on top when finding an angle: sin Q/q = sin P/p.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A triangle has sides of length 5 cm, 7 cm and 9 cm.
Work out the size of the largest angle. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: The largest angle is opposite the longest side (9 cm). A negative cosine gives an obtuse angle.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A ship sails 12 km from port A on a bearing of 070° to point B.
It then sails 8 km on a bearing of 160° to point C.
(a) Show that angle ABC = 90°.
(b) Work out the distance AC.
(c) Work out the bearing of C from A.
Give lengths to 3 s.f. and the bearing to the nearest degree.
questions.answer: (a) Bearing of A from B is 250°, 250 - 160 = 90°  (b) 14.4 km  (c) 104°
ms: B1 for showing angle ABC = 90°, e.g. bearing of A from B = 070 + 180 = 250°, and 250 - 160 = 90°
questions.tip: Bearings are measured clockwise from north and written with three figures. Draw a north line at every point.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The bearing of Q from P is 125°. What is the bearing of P from Q?
questions.tip: Add 180° if the bearing is under 180°, subtract 180° if over.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle ABC has area 45 cm². AB = 9 cm and angle BAC = 30°.
Work out the length of AC.
ms: M1 for using sin 30° = 1/2, giving 9/4 × AC = 45
questions.tip: Use the exact value sin 30° = 1/2 on a non-calculator paper.

questions.q:
[Calculator] ABCD is a quadrilateral. AB = 6 cm, BC = 8 cm, angle ABC = 110°, AD = 7 cm and angle CAD = 40°.
Work out the area of ABCD. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for area ABC = ½ × 6 × 8 × sin 110° (= 22.55)
questions.tip: Keep the unrounded value of AC in your calculator for the next step to avoid accuracy errors.

questions.q: [Calculator] You know two sides of a triangle and the angle between them. You want the third side. Which do you use?
ms: Two sides and the included angle (SAS) to find the opposite side needs the cosine rule a² = b² + c² - 2bc cos A.
questions.tip: The sine rule needs an angle and its opposite side as a pair.

questions.q: [Calculator] A sector has radius 9 cm and angle 40°. What is the arc length to 3 s.f.?
questions.tip: Arc length uses 2πr (circumference). 28.3 is the sector area.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A circle has radius 6 cm. What is its exact area?
questions.tip: Square the radius, not the diameter.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A sector of a circle has radius 12 cm and angle 150°.
Work out the area of the sector. Give your answer in terms of π.
questions.tip: Simplify 150/360 to 5/12 to make the arithmetic easy.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A sector has radius 7 cm and angle 100°.
Work out the perimeter of the sector. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: The perimeter includes the two radii as well as the arc.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A sector has radius 6 cm and arc length 11 cm.
Work out the angle of the sector, to the nearest degree.
questions.tip: Form an equation with θ and rearrange. Do not guess and check.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A chord AB cuts a circle of centre O and radius 10 cm. Angle AOB = 60°.
Work out the area of the minor segment cut off by AB. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for triangle area ½ × 10 × 10 × sin 60° (= 43.30)
questions.tip: Segment = sector - triangle. Use ½ab sin C for the triangle.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A sector has angle 60° and area 24π cm².
Work out the exact perimeter of the sector. Give your answer in the form a + bπ.
questions.tip: Find r first. The perimeter is 2r + arc.

questions.q: [Calculator] A square has side 8 cm. A quarter circle of radius 8 cm is drawn inside it, centred at one corner. What is the area of the square NOT inside the quarter circle, to 3 s.f.?
questions.tip: The quarter circle uses ¼πr², with r = 8 (the side of the square). Subtract it from the square: 114 comes from adding instead.

questions.q: [Calculator] A cone has radius 5 cm and perpendicular height 12 cm. What is its volume to 3 s.f.?
questions.tip: Do not forget the ⅓. 942 is the volume of a cylinder with the same dimensions.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A sphere has radius 3 cm. What is its exact volume?
questions.tip: Cube the radius first (27), then multiply by 4/3.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A cone has radius 6 cm and slant height 10 cm. What is its total surface area?
ms: Curved area = πrl = 60π, base = πr² = 36π, total = 96π cm².
questions.tip: 'Total' surface area includes the circular base. Curved surface uses slant height l, not h.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A solid hemisphere has radius 4 cm.
Work out its total surface area. Give your answer in terms of π.
ms: M1 for adding the flat circle π × 4² (= 16π)
questions.tip: A solid hemisphere has a flat circular face too. Half of 4πr² alone is only 32π.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A pyramid has a square base of side 6 cm and a perpendicular height of 10 cm.
Work out the volume of the pyramid.
questions.tip: Volume of a pyramid = ⅓ × base area × height. Use the perpendicular height, not a slant edge.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A frustum is made by removing a small cone from the top of a large cone. The large cone has base radius 10 cm and perpendicular height 24 cm. The small cone removed has base radius 5 cm and height 12 cm.
Work out the volume of the frustum. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for volume of large cone ⅓ × π × 10² × 24 (= 800π = 2513.3)
M1 for volume of small cone ⅓ × π × 5² × 12 (= 100π = 314.2)
questions.tip: A frustum is large cone minus small cone. You cannot use the average radius.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted down and recast into a solid cylinder of radius 4 cm.
Work out the height of the cylinder.
questions.tip: Equal volumes: set the two formulas equal. π cancels, so leave it as π.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cone has base radius 5 cm. The curved surface area of the cone is 65π cm².
Work out the volume of the cone. Give your answer in terms of π.
questions.tip: The volume needs the perpendicular height, so use Pythagoras on the slant height.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A solid is made from a cylinder with a hemisphere on top. The cylinder and hemisphere both have radius 3 cm. The cylinder has height h cm.
The total volume of the solid is 45π cm³.
Work out the value of h.
ms: M1 for cylinder volume π × 3² × h = 9πh
M1 for hemisphere volume ½ × 4/3 × π × 3³ = 18π
questions.tip: Halve the sphere volume for the hemisphere. Divide every term by π to simplify.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the locus of points that are exactly 4 cm from a fixed point P?
options: A circle of radius 4 cm centred on P
A circle of diameter 4 cm centred on P
ms: All points a fixed distance from a point form a circle with that radius.
questions.tip: Radius, not diameter, is the fixed distance.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the locus of points equidistant from two fixed points A and B?
options: A circle centred at the midpoint of AB
ms: Points the same distance from A and B lie on the perpendicular bisector of AB.
questions.tip: Equidistant from two POINTS = perpendicular bisector. Equidistant from two LINES = angle bisector.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the locus of points equidistant from two lines that meet at a point?
