options: A line parallel to one of the lines
The bisector of the angle between the lines
ms: Points equidistant from two intersecting lines lie on the angle bisector.
questions.tip: Do not confuse lines with points.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Describe how to construct the perpendicular bisector of a line segment AB using only a ruler and a pair of compasses.
questions.answer: Set compasses to more than half of AB. Draw arcs above and below AB from A. With the same radius, draw arcs from B to cross the first arcs. Join the two crossing points with a straight line.
ms: B1 for compasses set to more than half the length of AB
B1 for arcs drawn from both A and B with the SAME radius, crossing above and below the line
B1 for joining the two intersection points with a ruler (leave construction arcs showing)
questions.tip: Always leave your construction arcs visible. Without arcs, a correct line scores zero.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Describe how to construct the bisector of angle ABC using only a ruler and compasses.
questions.answer: With compasses centred on B, draw an arc crossing BA at P and BC at Q. With the same radius, draw arcs from P and from Q that cross at R. Draw the line from B through R.
ms: B1 for an arc centred at B cutting both arms of the angle
B1 for equal-radius arcs from the two crossing points, intersecting inside the angle
B1 for joining B to the intersection point
questions.tip: The two arcs from P and Q must use the same radius.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A rectangular garden ABCD has AB = 10 m and BC = 6 m. A tree is to be planted so that it is:
- closer to AB than to AD, and
- less than 4 m from C.
Describe fully the region where the tree can be planted.
questions.answer: The region inside the rectangle that is on the AB side of the bisector of angle DAB (the line from A at 45° to AB and AD), and inside the circle of radius 4 m centred at C.
ms: B1 for the bisector of angle DAB (angle at A between AB and AD), a line from A at 45° to AB
B1 for an arc/circle of radius 4 m centred at C
B1 for the correct region identified: on the AB side of the angle bisector and inside the circle centred at C
questions.tip: 'Closer to a line' uses an angle bisector. 'Less than 4 m from a point' means inside a circle.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Describe how to construct the perpendicular from a point P to a line L, where P is not on L, using a ruler and compasses.
questions.answer: With centre P draw an arc cutting L at two points, A and B. From A and from B, with the same radius, draw arcs crossing on the other side of L at Q. Join P to Q.
ms: B1 for an arc centred at P crossing L at two points
B1 for equal arcs from those two points intersecting (on the opposite side of L to P)
B1 for joining P to the intersection point
questions.tip: This is the perpendicular bisector of the two points where your first arc meets L.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A goat is tied to the corner A of a square shed ABCD with side 4 m, using a rope of length 6 m. The goat is outside the shed and cannot go through it.
Describe the region the goat can reach. Calculate the area of this region in terms of π.
questions.answer: Three-quarters of a circle of radius 6 m centred at A, plus two quarter circles of radius 2 m centred at B and D. Area = 27π + π + π = 29π m².
ms: B1 for ¾ of a circle radius 6 centred at A: ¾ × π × 36 = 27π
B1 for recognising the rope wraps round corners B and D, giving quarter circles of radius 2 m (π each)
questions.tip: The rope wraps around the corners of the shed, leaving 6 - 4 = 2 m of rope at B and D.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Describe how to construct an angle of 60° at point A on a line, using ruler and compasses only.
questions.answer: Draw an arc centred on A crossing the line at B. With the same radius, draw an arc centred on B crossing the first arc at C. Join A to C. Angle CAB = 60°.
ms: B1 for an arc centred on A and an arc of the same radius centred on the crossing point B
B1 for joining A to the intersection, forming an equilateral triangle so the angle is 60°
questions.tip: The radius must stay the same, because the method makes an equilateral triangle.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The point (3, -2) is reflected in the line y = x. What are its new coordinates?
ms: Reflection in y = x swaps the coordinates: (3, -2) becomes (-2, 3).
questions.tip: Reflection in y = -x swaps and changes both signs, giving (2, -3).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The point (4, 1) is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. What is its image?
ms: 90° clockwise about the origin maps (x, y) to (y, -x), so (4, 1) → (1, -4).
questions.tip: (-1, 4) is the anticlockwise rotation. Use tracing paper in the exam.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Triangle A has a vertex at (2, 4). It is enlarged with scale factor -2 and centre of enlargement the origin. Where does this vertex go?
ms: Negative scale factor: multiply the vector from the centre by -2, so (2, 4) → (-4, -8).
questions.tip: A negative scale factor puts the image on the opposite side of the centre and upside down.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Shape P has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 2). Shape Q has vertices (4, -2), (6, -2) and (4, -1).
Describe fully the single transformation that maps P onto Q.
ms: B1 for vector (3 over -3), written as a column vector
questions.tip: Write the word 'translation' and a column vector. 'Moved 3 right and 3 down' only gets 1 mark.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle A has vertices (2, 2), (6, 2) and (2, 6). Triangle B has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 3).
Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle A onto triangle B.
questions.tip: A fractional scale factor makes the shape smaller. You need all three facts: enlargement, scale factor, centre.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Point P has coordinates (5, 7). P is enlarged by scale factor -1/2 with centre of enlargement (1, 1).
Work out the coordinates of the image of P.
ms: M1 for the vector from the centre to P: (4, 6)
M1 for multiplying by -1/2 to get (-2, -3)
questions.tip: Always work from the centre, not from the origin, and add the scaled vector back onto the centre.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Shape A is reflected in the line x = 1 to give shape B. Shape B is then reflected in the line x = 4 to give shape C.
Describe fully the single transformation that maps shape A onto shape C.
ms: B1 for a horizontal translation to the right
B1 for vector (6, 0) (twice the distance between the mirror lines, 2 × 3)
questions.tip: Two reflections in parallel lines give a translation of twice the gap between the lines. Test with a point, e.g. (0, 0) → (2, 0) → (6, 0).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle T has vertices (1, 2), (3, 2) and (3, 5). It is rotated 180° about the point (2, 0).
Write down the coordinates of the vertices of the image.
ms: M1 for using (x, y) → (2 × 2 - x, 2 × 0 - y) = (4 - x, -y), or a correct rotation of at least one vertex
questions.tip: A rotation of 180° about (a, b) sends (x, y) to (2a - x, 2b - y).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] a = (3, -1) and b = (-2, 4) as column vectors. What is 2a + b?
questions.tip: Multiply both components by 2 before adding.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the magnitude of the vector (5, -12)?
questions.tip: Squaring -12 gives +144. The magnitude is always positive.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] OA = a and OB = b. What is the vector AB?
ms: AB = AO + OB = -a + b = b - a.
questions.tip: Go from A back to O (-a), then O to B (+b).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OAB is a triangle. OA = a and OB = b. M is the midpoint of AB.
Find the vector OM in terms of a and b. Give your answer in its simplest form.
ms: M1 for OM = a + ½(b - a)
A1 for ½a + ½b (or ½(a + b))
questions.tip: Write a route from O to M using vectors you know, then simplify.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OAB is a triangle. OA = a and OB = b. P is the point on AB such that AP : PB = 1 : 3.
Find OP in terms of a and b. Give your answer in its simplest form.
ms: M1 for OP = a + ¼(b - a)
questions.tip: AP : PB = 1 : 3 means AP is 1/4 of AB, not 1/3.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OABC is a parallelogram with OA = a and OC = c. M is the midpoint of AB. N is the point on OB such that ON : NB = 2 : 1.
Prove that C, N and M lie on a straight line.
questions.answer: OB = a + c. CN = -c + ⅔(a + c) = ⅔a - ⅓c. CM = -c + a + ½c = a - ½c. CM = 3/2 × CN, so CN and CM are parallel and share point C, so C, N and M are collinear.
ms: M1 for CN = -c + ⅔(a + c) = ⅔a - ⅓c
M1 for CM = -c + a + ½c = a - ½c (using AB = c, so AM = ½c)
M1 for showing one is a multiple of the other: CN = ⅔(a - ½c) = ⅔ CM
A1 for conclusion: CN and CM are parallel and have the common point C, so C, N, M are on a straight line
questions.tip: To prove collinear you need BOTH: one vector is a multiple of the other, AND they share a point.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OAB is a triangle with OA = a and OB = b. X is the midpoint of OA and Y is the midpoint of OB.
Prove that XY is parallel to AB and half its length.
questions.answer: AB = b - a. XY = -½a + ½b = ½(b - a) = ½AB. So XY is parallel to AB and half its length.
ms: M1 for XY = XO + OY = -½a + ½b
M1 for writing XY = ½(b - a)
A1 for concluding XY = ½AB, so parallel and half the length
questions.tip: Factorise to show one vector is a scalar multiple of the other, then write a conclusion in words.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The vectors p = (2, k) and q = (6, 9) are parallel.
Find the value of k.
questions.tip: Parallel vectors are scalar multiples of each other: compare the x and y components with the same multiplier.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which vector is parallel to 2a - 3b?
ms: -4a + 6b = -2(2a - 3b), a scalar multiple, so it is parallel.
questions.tip: Parallel means a multiple of the whole vector; both coefficients must scale by the same number.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A spinner can land on red, blue, green or yellow. P(red) = 0.35, P(blue) = 0.2, P(green) = 0.15. What is P(yellow)?
questions.tip: 0.7 is the total of the given probabilities, not the missing one.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The probability that a biased coin lands on heads is 0.12. It is thrown 250 times. What is the expected number of heads?
questions.tip: Multiply the probability by the number of trials.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A dice is rolled 80 times. It lands on six 22 times.
(a) Work out the relative frequency of rolling a six.
(b) Is the dice likely to be fair? Give a reason.
questions.answer: (a) 22/80 = 0.275  (b) Probably biased: 0.275 is much higher than 1/6 ≈ 0.167 (but more rolls would give a more reliable estimate).
ms: B1 for a comparison with 1/6 (≈ 0.167) and a conclusion, e.g. likely to be biased as 0.275 is much bigger than 1/6
questions.tip: Compare the relative frequency to the theoretical probability with actual numbers.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Two fair six-sided dice are rolled and the scores are added. What is the probability of a total of 8?
questions.tip: Use a sample space diagram. Totals are not all equally likely, so 1/11 is wrong.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A code is made of 2 letters (A to Z) followed by 3 digits (0 to 9). Letters and digits may repeat.
How many different codes are possible?
questions.tip: Use the product rule: multiply the number of choices for each position.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains n red counters and 5 blue counters only. A counter is taken at random. The probability it is red is 3/8.
Find the value of n.
questions.tip: The total number of counters is n + 5, not 5.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Events A and B are mutually exclusive. P(A) = 0.4 and P(B) = 0.25. What is P(A or B)?
ms: For mutually exclusive events, P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) = 0.65.
questions.tip: 0.1 is P(A) × P(B), which is for independent events happening together.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 200 students were asked how they travel to school. 85 walk. Of the students who do not walk, 40% come by bus and the rest come by car.
A student is chosen at random. Work out the probability that the student comes by car.
questions.tip: A frequency tree helps. 60% of the non-walkers, not 60% of everyone.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A bag has 3 red and 5 green balls. A ball is taken, replaced, and a second ball is taken. What is P(both red)?
questions.tip: With replacement the denominators stay at 8. 3/28 is without replacement.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A bag has 3 red and 5 green balls. Two balls are taken without replacement. What is P(both red)?
questions.tip: Without replacement, one fewer red AND one fewer ball in total for the second pick.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 3 red sweets and 5 green sweets. Kai takes a sweet at random and eats it. He then takes another sweet at random.
Work out the probability that he takes one sweet of each colour.
questions.tip: There are two ways to get one of each: red then green, or green then red.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A box has 6 working bulbs and 4 faulty bulbs. Three bulbs are taken at random without replacement.
Work out the probability that at least one of the bulbs works.
questions.tip: 'At least one' is easiest as 1 - P(none).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The probability that Jo passes her driving theory test is 0.7. The probability that she passes her practical test is 0.4. The two events are independent.
Work out the probability that she passes exactly one of the tests.
questions.tip: Exactly one: pass first and fail second, or fail first and pass second.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A box contains n pens. 5 of the pens are black. Two pens are taken at random without replacement.
The probability that both pens are black is 5/33.
(a) Show that n² - n - 132 = 0.
(b) Work out the value of n.
ms: A1 for rearranging correctly to n² - n - 132 = 0 (convincing, no errors)
questions.tip: For 'show that' every step must appear. Reject the negative solution with a reason.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 4 red, 5 blue and 3 yellow counters. Three counters are taken at random without replacement.
Work out the probability that the three counters are all different colours.
ms: M1 for one correct product, e.g. 4/12 × 5/11 × 3/10 (= 60/1320)
M1 for recognising there are 6 orders
questions.tip: Multiply one ordered product by the number of orders (3 × 2 × 1 = 6).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What does A ∩ B mean?
options: Elements in A or B or both
Elements in A but not B
Elements in both A and B
ms: ∩ is intersection: elements in both sets.
questions.tip: ∪ is union (A or B or both); ∩ is intersection (both).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] ξ = {1, 2, 3, ..., 10}. A = {even numbers}, B = {multiples of 3}. Which is A ∪ B?
ms: A = {2, 4, 6, 8, 10}, B = {3, 6, 9}. The union contains everything in either: {2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 10}.
questions.tip: List each set first. Do not count 6 twice.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] There are 60 students in a year group. 35 study French, 28 study Spanish and 10 study neither.
(a) Work out how many study both French and Spanish.
(b) A student is chosen at random. Find P(F ∩ S').
ms: M1 for 60 - 10 = 50 study at least one
questions.tip: F ∩ S' means in F and NOT in S, so French only.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] In a Venn diagram, 22 people are in F only, 13 are in F ∩ S, 15 are in S only and 10 are in neither. A person who is in F is chosen at random. What is the probability they are also in S?
ms: Given F: the total is 22 + 13 = 35, and 13 of these are in S, so 13/35.
questions.tip: 'Given F' changes the denominator to the number in F, not 60.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] In a Venn diagram for sets A and B: A only has 7, A ∩ B has 4, B only has 9, and outside both has 5. How many elements are in A' ∪ B?
ms: A' ∪ B = everything not in A, plus all of B: 9 + 5 + 4 = 18 (everything except A only).
questions.tip: A' ∪ B is everything except 'A only'. Total 25 - 7 = 18.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 50 people were asked whether they own a bike (B) or a car (C).
The number who own a bike only is 3x. The number who own both is x. The number who own a car only is 2x + 1. 7 people own neither.
(a) Find x.
(b) A person who owns a car is chosen at random. Find the probability they also own a bike.
ms: M1 for number who own a car = 7 + 15 = 22
questions.tip: The 'given' condition (owns a car) sets the denominator: both + car only.

questions.q:
[Calculator] P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.15.
(a) Find P(A ∪ B).
(b) Find P(A | B), the probability of A given B.
questions.tip: Draw a Venn diagram with probabilities: fill the intersection first.

questions.q:
[Calculator] P(A) = 0.3, P(B) = 0.6 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.2.
Are A and B independent? Give a reason.
questions.answer: No. P(A) × P(B) = 0.18, which is not equal to P(A ∩ B) = 0.2.
questions.tip: The test for independence: does P(A) × P(B) equal P(A ∩ B)?

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A two-way table shows 30 students: 12 boys like football, 6 boys do not; 5 girls like football, 7 girls do not. A girl is chosen at random. What is the probability she likes football?
ms: There are 5 + 7 = 12 girls; 5 like football, so 5/12.
questions.tip: 'A girl is chosen' means the denominator is the number of girls.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] P(A ∩ B) = 0.12 and P(B) = 0.3. What is P(A | B)?
questions.tip: Divide by the probability of the condition, do not multiply.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 80 people were asked if they prefer tea or coffee.
45 of them were adults, and the rest were teenagers. 28 adults prefer coffee. In total, 40 people prefer tea.
(a) Complete a two-way table and find how many teenagers prefer tea.
(b) A person who prefers tea is chosen at random. Find the probability that they are a teenager.
ms: M1 for adults who prefer tea = 45 - 28 = 17
A1 for teenagers who prefer tea = 40 - 17 = 23
M1 for denominator 40 (those who prefer tea)
questions.tip: Read 'a person who prefers tea is chosen' as the condition: use only the tea column.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The probability that it rains on a given day is 0.3.
If it rains, the probability that Leon is late for school is 0.4. If it does not rain, the probability that he is late is 0.1.
(a) Work out the probability that Leon is late on a given day.
(b) Given that Leon is late, work out the probability that it rained.
questions.tip: 'Given that he is late' means divide by P(late), not multiply.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Two fair dice are rolled. Given that the total is 8, what is the probability that at least one dice shows a 6?
ms: Totals of 8: (2,6), (3,5), (4,4), (5,3), (6,2). Two of these five contain a 6, so 2/5.
questions.tip: The condition restricts the sample space to the 5 outcomes with total 8.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue marbles. Two marbles are taken at random without replacement.
Given that both marbles are the same colour, work out the probability that they are both red.
questions.tip: The condition 'same colour' is your new total: P(RR) + P(BB).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] For a grouped frequency table, what value do you use for each group when estimating the mean?
ms: Multiply each midpoint by its frequency, add, then divide by the total frequency.
questions.tip: The answer is an estimate because the exact values are unknown.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The table shows the times, t minutes, that 30 people waited at a bus stop.
Time (t minutes) | Frequency
0 < t ≤ 10 | 4
10 < t ≤ 20 | 10
20 < t ≤ 30 | 12
30 < t ≤ 40 | 4
Work out an estimate for the mean waiting time.
questions.tip: Divide by the total frequency (30), not by the number of groups (4).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Using the same bus stop table (frequencies 4, 10, 12, 4 for 0-10, 10-20, 20-30, 30-40 minutes), which class contains the median?
ms: There are 30 values, so the median is about the 15.5th. Cumulative: 4, 14, 26, so it lies in 20 < t ≤ 30.
questions.tip: Use cumulative frequency to find which group holds the middle value.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A table shows the number of pets owned: 0 pets: 3 people; 1 pet: 8 people; 2 pets: 6 people; 3 pets: 2 people; 4 pets: 1 person. What is the mean number of pets?
questions.tip: Divide by the total frequency (20), not by the number of rows (5). Averaging the values 0 to 4 gives 2, which is wrong.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Class A has 12 students with a mean test score of 68. Class B has 18 students with a mean score of 73.
Work out the mean score of all 30 students.
questions.tip: Find the total scores first. Averaging 68 and 73 gives 70.5, which is wrong.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Five numbers have a mean of 8. A sixth number is added and the mean becomes 9.
Work out the sixth number.
questions.tip: Work with totals: mean × number of values.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Explain why the mean calculated from a grouped frequency table is only an estimate, and state one reason why the median might be a better average to use if the data contains an extreme value.
questions.answer: The exact data values are not known, so midpoints are used. The median is not affected by extreme values (outliers), whereas the mean is.
ms: B1 for: the actual values are unknown / midpoints are used to represent each group
B1 for: the median is not affected by extreme values (outliers)
questions.tip: Use the key words 'midpoint' and 'outlier' or 'extreme value'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the masses of some parcels.
Mass (m kg) | Frequency
0 < m ≤ 20 | 6
20 < m ≤ 40 | x
40 < m ≤ 60 | 4
An estimate of the mean mass is 28 kg.
Work out the value of x.
questions.tip: The total frequency is 10 + x, so it includes the unknown.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] On a cumulative frequency graph with total frequency 80, at what cumulative frequency do you read off the lower quartile?
ms: Lower quartile is at 1/4 of the total: 80 ÷ 4 = 20.
questions.tip: Upper quartile is at 3/4 (60). Median is at 1/2 (40).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] When plotting a cumulative frequency graph for grouped data, where do you plot each point?
options: At the midpoint of each class
ms: Cumulative frequency is the running total up to the END of each class, so plot at the upper bound.
questions.tip: Plotting at midpoints is the most common error and loses the marks.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A box plot has minimum 12, lower quartile 18, median 25, upper quartile 31, maximum 40. What is the interquartile range?
questions.tip: 28 is the range. IQR uses the quartiles.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two classes sat the same test.
Class P: median 54, IQR 12.
Class Q: median 61, IQR 25.
Compare the distributions of the scores for the two classes.
questions.answer: Class Q had a higher median, so on average Q scored higher. Class P had a smaller IQR, so P's scores were more consistent (less spread out).
ms: B1 for comparing medians in context, e.g. Class Q's scores were higher on average (median 61 > 54)
B1 for comparing IQRs in context, e.g. Class P's scores were more consistent as the IQR is smaller (12 < 25)
questions.tip: Compare one average and one measure of spread, both in context. Just stating the numbers does not score.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The cumulative frequency table shows the lengths of 80 phone calls.
Length (t minutes) | Cumulative frequency
t ≤ 10 | 8
t ≤ 20 | 26
t ≤ 30 | 52
t ≤ 40 | 70
t ≤ 50 | 80
(a) Which interval contains the median?
(b) Use the table to estimate how many calls lasted more than 40 minutes.
(c) Estimate how many calls lasted between 10 and 30 minutes.
ms: B1 for 20 < t ≤ 30 (40th value: cumulative frequency passes 40 there)
questions.tip: Subtract cumulative frequencies to get the number in a range.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cumulative frequency graph is drawn for the phone call data, by joining the points (0, 0), (10, 8), (20, 26), (30, 52), (40, 70) and (50, 80) with straight lines.
Use the graph to estimate the interquartile range of the call lengths.
ms: M1 for reading at cumulative frequency 20 and 60
A1 for LQ ≈ 16.7 and UQ ≈ 34.4 (accept 16 to 17.5 and 34 to 35)
questions.tip: Read across at n/4 and 3n/4 of the total frequency (80), not at 25 and 75.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The ages of members of a club are: lowest 16, highest 64, median 35, lower quartile 24, upper quartile 47.
(a) Describe what a box plot of this data would look like.
(b) An age of 64 is said to be an outlier if it is more than 1.5 × IQR above the upper quartile. Is 64 an outlier?
questions.answer: (a) Whiskers from 16 to 24 and 47 to 64, a box from 24 to 47 with a line at 35.  (b) IQR = 23, 1.5 × 23 = 34.5, 47 + 34.5 = 81.5; 64 < 81.5 so not an outlier.
ms: B1 for box from LQ 24 to UQ 47 with median line at 35, whiskers to 16 and 64
A1 for 81.5 and conclusion: not an outlier
questions.tip: A box plot needs five values: min, LQ, median, UQ, max.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] On a box plot, what percentage of the data lies between the lower quartile and the maximum?
ms: 25% of the data is below the LQ, so 75% is between the LQ and the maximum.
questions.tip: Each section of a box plot (whisker, half box, half box, whisker) holds 25% of the data.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] How do you calculate frequency density?
questions.tip: In a histogram, area of the bar (not height) represents frequency.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A histogram bar for 20 < h ≤ 35 has frequency density 2.4. What is the frequency?
questions.tip: The class width is 35 - 20 = 15.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the heights of some seedlings.
Height (h mm) | Frequency
0 < h ≤ 10 | 12
10 < h ≤ 20 | 30
20 < h ≤ 40 | 40
40 < h ≤ 70 | 18
Work out the frequency density for each class, ready to draw a histogram.
ms: M1 for frequency ÷ class width for at least one class
A1 for at least three correct
questions.tip: Check the class widths: they are 10, 10, 20 and 30, not all 10.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A histogram for seedling heights has these bars:
0 < h ≤ 10: frequency density 1.2
10 < h ≤ 20: frequency density 3
20 < h ≤ 40: frequency density 2
40 < h ≤ 70: frequency density 0.6
Estimate the number of seedlings with height between 15 mm and 30 mm.
ms: M1 for 5 × 3 (= 15) from the 15 to 20 part
M1 for 10 × 2 (= 20) from the 20 to 30 part
questions.tip: Use only the part of each bar inside the range: width × frequency density.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A histogram has no scale on the vertical axis. The bar for 10 < t ≤ 15 has height 4.8 cm and represents 12 people.
The bar for 15 < t ≤ 25 has height 3 cm.
Work out how many people are represented by the bar for 15 < t ≤ 25.
ms: M1 for frequency density of first bar = 12 ÷ 5 = 2.4, so 1 cm represents 0.5
M1 for second bar frequency density = 3 × 0.5 = 1.5
questions.tip: Area is proportional to frequency: first bar area 5 × 4.8 = 24 for 12 people, so 10 × 3 = 30 gives 15 people.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Using the seedling data (0 < h ≤ 10: 12, 10 < h ≤ 20: 30, 20 < h ≤ 40: 40, 40 < h ≤ 70: 18), estimate the median height.
ms: M1 for total = 100 so median is the 50th value, in 20 < h ≤ 40
questions.tip: Find how far into the median class the middle value is, assuming values are spread evenly.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Why are histograms with unequal class widths drawn using frequency density rather than frequency?
options: So the area of each bar is proportional to frequency
So the bars are all the same width
ms: Using frequency density makes area represent frequency, so wide classes are not over-represented.
questions.tip: Remember: area = frequency in a histogram.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which of these is a random sample?
options: Giving every student a number and picking 20 numbers using a random number generator
Asking the first 20 people to arrive at school
Asking 20 people at a football match
ms: In a random sample every member of the population has an equal chance of being chosen.
questions.tip: Convenience samples (first 20, friends) are biased.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A school has 1200 students, of which 300 are in Year 7. A stratified sample of 60 students is taken. How many should be from Year 7?
questions.tip: Stratified samples keep the same proportions as the population.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A scientist catches 40 fish in a lake, marks them and releases them.
Later she catches 50 fish and 8 of them are marked.
(a) Estimate the number of fish in the lake.
(b) State one assumption you have made.
questions.answer: (a) 250  (b) e.g. the population did not change between samples (no births, deaths, migration), or marked fish mixed evenly, or marks were not lost
ms: B1 for a valid assumption, e.g. the fish population stays the same / marked fish mix fully / marks do not come off
questions.tip: Proportion marked in the second sample = proportion marked in the whole population.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Jake wants to find out how often people in his town use the leisure centre. He asks 30 people at the leisure centre on a Saturday morning.
Give two reasons why his sample may be biased.
questions.answer: Everyone asked already uses the leisure centre; only people free on a Saturday morning are included; sample is small.
ms: B1 for one valid reason, e.g. people at the leisure centre are more likely to use it
B1 for a second valid reason, e.g. only one time/day, so excludes people who work Saturdays, or sample of 30 is too small
questions.tip: Reasons must be specific to the situation, not just 'it is biased'.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A gym has 850 members: 340 under 25, 260 aged 25 to 50 and 250 over 50.
A stratified sample of 50 members is taken by age group.
Work out the number in the sample from each age group.
ms: M1 for 340/850 × 50 (= 20) or equivalent method for another group
A1 for 15.29... and 14.7... rounded to 15 and 15
questions.tip: Round sensibly so the sample sizes add up to the total sample size.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A biologist estimates there are 600 rabbits in a field using capture-recapture. She marked 75 rabbits on the first day. On the second day she caught some rabbits, and 9 were marked.
How many rabbits did she catch on the second day?
questions.tip: Set the proportion marked in the sample equal to the proportion marked in the population.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the main advantage of taking a sample rather than surveying the whole population?
ms: Samples save time and money, but may not perfectly represent the population.
questions.tip: A larger sample is more reliable, but a sample is never exact.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] As the temperature increases, ice cream sales increase. What type of correlation is this?
ms: Both variables increase together: positive correlation.
questions.tip: Negative correlation is when one goes up as the other goes down.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A scatter graph shows the age of cars (1 to 8 years) against their value. A line of best fit is drawn. Why is it unreliable to estimate the value of a 15-year-old car?
options: Because the line of best fit must pass through the origin
Because cars have no value after 10 years
Because it is extrapolation outside the data range
ms: 15 years is outside the range of the data, so the trend may not continue (extrapolation).
questions.tip: Estimates inside the data range (interpolation) are more reliable.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A scatter graph shows strong positive correlation between ice cream sales and sunburn cases. Which statement is correct?
options: Correlation does not prove causation; both may be caused by hot weather
ms: A third factor (hot sunny weather) explains both. Correlation is not causation.
questions.tip: Never say one variable causes the other just from a scatter graph.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A line of best fit on a scatter graph passes through (2, 50) and (10, 10), where x is hours of TV watched per day and y is test score.
(a) Describe the correlation.
(b) Use the line to estimate the test score of someone who watches 6 hours of TV per day.
ms: B1 for 30 (gradient -5, so at x = 6, y = 50 - 20 = 30)
questions.tip: Read estimates from the line of best fit, not from individual points.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A scatter graph of height against shoe size for 15 adults shows positive correlation. One point is at height 120 cm with shoe size 11, far away from all the other points.
(a) What name is given to this point?
(b) Should it be used when drawing the line of best fit? Give a reason.
questions.answer: (a) An outlier  (b) No, it does not fit the pattern of the other data (it may be an error), so it would distort the line.
ms: B1 for ignoring it with a valid reason
questions.tip: Ignore outliers when you draw a line of best fit.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The line of best fit for a scatter graph of house price (y, in £1000s) against floor area (x, in m²) has equation y = 2.5x + 40.
(a) Interpret the gradient in context.
(b) Estimate the price of a house with floor area 90 m².
(c) Explain why the intercept 40 may not have a sensible meaning.
questions.answer: (a) Each extra 1 m² adds about £2500 to the price.  (b) £265 000  (c) A house with 0 m² floor area does not exist (outside data range).
ms: B1 for the price increases by £2500 for each extra square metre (in context with units)
B1 for: floor area 0 m² is impossible / outside the data range, so the intercept is extrapolation
questions.tip: Interpret the gradient as 'for every 1 unit increase in x, y increases by ...', with units.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Describe the difference between interpolation and extrapolation, and say which is more reliable.
questions.answer: Interpolation is estimating within the range of the data; extrapolation is estimating outside it. Interpolation is more reliable.
ms: B1 for correct definitions of both
B1 for interpolation being more reliable, as the pattern may not continue beyond the data
questions.tip: Use the words 'within the range of the data'.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A map has a scale of 1 : 25 000. Two villages are 6 cm apart on the map. What is the real distance between them?
questions.tip: 15 km comes from dividing cm by 10 000 instead of 100 000. 100 cm = 1 m and 1000 m = 1 km.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] In a class, 3/8 of the students are boys. The rest are girls. What is the ratio of boys to girls?
questions.tip: 3 : 8 is boys : total, not boys : girls.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Ali, Bo and Cy share some money in the ratio 2 : 3 : 7. Cy gets £60 more than Ali. How much money is shared altogether?
ms: Difference = 7 − 2 = 5 parts = £60, so 1 part = £12. Total = 12 parts × £12 = £144.
questions.tip: £84 is Cy's share. Read what the question actually asks for.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 45 minutes : 2 hours as a ratio in its simplest form.
ms: M1 for converting to the same units, e.g. 45 : 120
questions.tip: Units must match before you simplify. 45 : 2 scores zero.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Orange squash is made by mixing concentrate and water in the ratio 1 : 6.
Ben has 150 ml of concentrate and 1 litre of water.
Work out the greatest amount of orange squash Ben can make.
You must show your working.
ms: M1 for 150 × 6 = 900 ml of water needed (or 1000 ÷ 6 = 166.7 ml concentrate needed)
M1 for recognising concentrate is the limiting amount, e.g. 900 < 1000
questions.tip: Check which ingredient runs out first. Using all the water (1000 + 166.7) needs more concentrate than Ben has.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The ratio of the money Asha has to the money Ben has is 5 : 3.
Asha gives Ben £12.
Now they each have the same amount of money.
How much money did Asha have to start with?
ms: M1 for setting up 5x − 12 = 3x + 12 (or equivalent, e.g. difference of 2 parts = £24)
questions.tip: After the swap the total is unchanged, so each has half: 4 parts each. Asha lost 1 part = £12.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The length and width of a rectangle are in the ratio 5 : 2.
The area of the rectangle is 160 cm².
Work out the perimeter of the rectangle.
ms: M1 for x = 4 so sides 20 cm and 8 cm
questions.tip: Use 5x and 2x for the sides. Do not split 160 in the ratio 5 : 2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Box A and box B contain the same number of counters.
In box A, the ratio of red counters to blue counters is 3 : 5.
In box B, the ratio of red counters to blue counters is 1 : 3.
All the counters are put into one bag.
What fraction of the counters in the bag are red?
ms: M1 for writing both boxes with the same total, e.g. A: 3 red out of 8, B: 2 red out of 8
M1 for total red 5 out of a total of 16 (or (3/8 + 1/4) ÷ 2)
questions.tip: You cannot just add the ratios (4 : 8). Make the box totals equal first, e.g. both out of 8.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (x + 3y) : (2x − y) = 5 : 3
Find the ratio x : y. Give your answer in its simplest form.
ms: M1 for 7x = 14y or equivalent with like terms collected
questions.tip: Turn the ratio into an equation by cross-multiplying, then collect x and y terms.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cinema sells adult tickets for £8 and child tickets for £5.
One evening, the ratio of adult tickets sold to child tickets sold was 2 : 3.
The total money taken was £620.
How many more child tickets than adult tickets were sold?
ms: M1 for 2 × 8 + 3 × 5 = £31 for one 'group' of 2 adults and 3 children
M1 for 40 adult tickets and 60 child tickets
questions.tip: Work in 'groups' of tickets that match the ratio. Do not share £620 in the ratio 2 : 3.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] 300 g of flour makes 12 biscuits. How much flour is needed to make 20 biscuits?
questions.tip: Find the amount for one first (unitary method).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] y is inversely proportional to √x. x is multiplied by 4. What happens to y?
ms: y = k/√x. √(4x) = 2√x, so y becomes k/(2√x), which is half.
questions.tip: Square root the change in x first, then invert it because it is inverse proportion.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] y is directly proportional to x³. When x = 2, y = 20. What is y when x = 4?
questions.tip: x doubles so y is multiplied by 2³ = 8, not 2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 8 chocolate bars cost £3.60.
Work out the cost of 14 of these chocolate bars.
questions.tip: Write money answers to 2 decimal places: £6.3 can lose the accuracy mark.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y is inversely proportional to x.
When x = 5, y = 12.
(a) Find the value of y when x = 4.
(b) Find the value of x when y = 20.
ms: M1 for y = k/x and k = 60
questions.tip: Inverse proportion: xy is constant. Check: 4 × 15 = 60 and 3 × 20 = 60.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows some values of x and y.
x | 2 | 5 | 8
y | 40 | 16 | 10
Show that y is inversely proportional to x.
questions.answer: xy = 80 in every case, so y = 80/x
ms: M1 for finding xy for at least two pairs, e.g. 2 × 40 = 80, 5 × 16 = 80
A1 for showing all three products equal 80 and concluding y = 80/x
questions.tip: For inverse proportion, show the product xy is constant. For direct, show y ÷ x is constant.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 8 identical machines can produce a batch of parts in 15 hours.
The factory needs the same batch produced in 6 hours.
How many extra machines are needed? Assume all machines work at the same rate.
questions.tip: The question asks for EXTRA machines. 20 is the total, not the answer.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The intensity, I, of light from a lamp is inversely proportional to the square of the distance, d metres, from the lamp.
When d = 5, I = 36.
(a) Find a formula for I in terms of d.
(b) Work out I when d = 3.
(c) Work out d when I = 4.
questions.tip: Write the formula with k before substituting. 'Inversely proportional to the square' means k/d², not k/d.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The number of days it takes to build a wall is inversely proportional to the number of builders.
6 builders would take 20 days to build the wall.
The 6 builders start work. After 5 days, 4 more builders join them.
How many days does it take to build the wall altogether? Assume all builders work at the same rate.
ms: M1 for work done in first 5 days = 30 builder-days, so 90 left
questions.tip: Do not just use 10 builders for the whole job. Split the job into before and after the extra builders arrive.

questions.q:
[Calculator] P is inversely proportional to the cube of r.
r is increased by 25%.
Work out the percentage decrease in P.
ms: M1 for P = k/r³ and new P = k/(1.25r)³
questions.tip: 25% increase in r does not mean 75% decrease in P. Use the multiplier 1.25 and cube it.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] m is directly proportional to the cube of r.
When r = 2, m = 20.
Work out the value of r when m = 67.5.
ms: M1 for m = kr³ and k = 20 ÷ 8 = 2.5
questions.tip: Reverse the formula carefully: divide by k first, then cube root.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] y is inversely proportional to x and x > 0. Which statement describes the graph of y against x?
options: A curve that gets closer to both axes but never touches them
A U-shaped curve through the origin
A straight line through the origin
A straight line with negative gradient
ms: y = k/x is a reciprocal curve with both axes as asymptotes.
questions.tip: Direct proportion is the straight line through the origin; inverse proportion is the reciprocal curve.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A train travels at 80 km/h for 45 minutes. How far does it travel?
questions.tip: Change minutes into hours first: 45 min = 0.75 h, not 0.45 h (which gives 36 km).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Convert a density of 2.5 g/cm³ into kg/m³.
questions.tip: Two conversions here: g to kg (÷ 1000) and cm³ to m³ (× 1 000 000).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Hana runs 5 km in 24 minutes.
Work out her average speed in km/h.
questions.tip: Convert 24 minutes to 0.4 hours before dividing.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Car A travels 210 km in 2 hours 20 minutes.
Car B travels at an average speed of 25 m/s.
Show that the two cars have the same average speed.
ms: M1 for 210 ÷ 7/3 = 90 km/h, or 25 m/s converted: 25 × 3600 ÷ 1000
A1 for both shown as 90 km/h (or both as 25 m/s)
questions.tip: 2 h 20 min is not 2.2 hours. 20 minutes = 1/3 of an hour.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A force of 120 newtons acts on a circular area of radius 20 cm.
Work out the pressure in N/m². Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
(pressure = force ÷ area)
ms: M1 for area = π × 0.2² (= 0.1256...) in m²
questions.tip: Change cm to m before finding the area: 20 cm = 0.2 m. Using 20 gives an answer 10 000 times too small.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A water tank is a cylinder with radius 0.5 m and height 1.2 m.
The empty tank is filled with water at a rate of 12 litres per minute.
Work out how long it takes to fill the tank. Give your answer in minutes, to the nearest minute.
(1 m³ = 1000 litres)
questions.tip: Keep the full calculator value until the end. Rounding the volume to 0.9 m³ gives 75 minutes.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Sam runs a distance of 125 m, measured correct to the nearest metre.
His time is 14.5 seconds, measured correct to 1 decimal place.
Work out the upper bound for Sam's average speed. Give your answer to 4 significant figures.
You must show all your working.
questions.tip: Upper bound of a speed = upper bound distance ÷ LOWER bound time. Dividing by the upper bound time gives a smaller answer.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Metal A has density 8 g/cm³. Metal B has density 2 g/cm³.
An alloy is made by mixing metal A and metal B in the ratio 3 : 1 by MASS.
Work out the density of the alloy. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for choosing masses in ratio 3 : 1, e.g. 300 g and 100 g
M1 for volumes 300 ÷ 8 = 37.5 cm³ and 100 ÷ 2 = 50 cm³
M1 for total mass ÷ total volume = 400 ÷ 87.5
questions.tip: The ratio is by mass, so you cannot average the densities. (8 × 3 + 2 × 1) ÷ 4 = 6.5 is wrong.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Leah drives 40 km at an average speed of 50 km/h and then 20 km at an average speed of 40 km/h.
Work out her average speed for the whole 60 km journey. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for times 40 ÷ 50 = 0.8 h and 20 ÷ 40 = 0.5 h
questions.tip: Average speed is total distance ÷ total time, not (50 + 40) ÷ 2.

questions.q: [Calculator] What multiplier gives a decrease of 3.5%?
questions.tip: 0.65 is a 35% decrease. 3.5% as a decimal is 0.035.

questions.q: [Calculator] In a sale, the price of a coat is reduced by 15%. The sale price is £68. What was the original price?
questions.tip: Finding 15% of £68 and adding it on gives £78.20. Divide by the multiplier instead.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Kim invests £3500 for 3 years at 2.5% per annum compound interest.
Work out the total interest she earns.
questions.tip: The question asks for the interest, not the final amount. Subtract the £3500.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A town has a population of 48 000. The population increases by 2% each year.
Work out the population after 5 years. Give your answer to the nearest hundred.
questions.tip: Use the power key. Adding 2% of 48 000 five times is simple interest and is wrong.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The population of a species of bird is 25 000. The population is decreasing by 4% each year.
After how many whole years will the population first be below 20 000?
You must show your working.
ms: M1 for using 0.96 as a multiplier
M1 for trial values either side, e.g. 25 000 × 0.96⁵ = 20 384 and 25 000 × 0.96⁶ = 19 569
questions.tip: Show the values for both n = 5 and n = 6 to prove 6 is the first year.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Ravi has £8000 to invest for 6 years.
Account X pays 4.2% per year compound interest.
Account Y pays 5% per year simple interest.
Which account will give Ravi more interest, and by how much?
ms: M1 for comparing interest (2239.91 vs 2400) or totals (10 239.91 vs 10 400)
questions.tip: Compare like with like: interest with interest, or totals with totals.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The mass of a radioactive substance halves every 5 years. The mass decreases by the same percentage each year.
Show that the mass decreases by about 12.9% each year.
ms: A1 for 1 − 0.87055 = 0.12944... = 12.9% (must show more accuracy than 12.9)
questions.tip: In a 'show that' you must show a more accurate value, e.g. 12.94%, before rounding.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The value of a painting increased by 6% in the first year.
In the second year its value increased by r%.
Over the two years the value increased by 16.6% in total.
Work out the value of r.
questions.tip: Percentages multiply, not add: 16.6 − 6 = 10.6 is wrong.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The number of fish in a lake at the start of year n is Pₙ.
P₍ₙ₊₁₎ = 1.2Pₙ − 150
P₁ = 1000
(a) Work out P₄.
(b) Explain what the numbers 1.2 and 150 could mean in this context.
questions.answer: (a) 1182 (b) population grows by 20% each year; 150 fish are removed (e.g. caught) each year
ms: B1 for (b) 20% growth per year and 150 fish removed each year
questions.tip: P₄ is three steps after P₁, not four.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A van is bought for £24 000. Its value depreciates by 15% per year.
Show that its value after 2 years is £17 340.
ms: A1 for 17 340 shown with correct working
questions.tip: Taking off 30% in one go gives £16 800. Depreciation compounds.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A quantity increases by 20% and then decreases by 20%. What is the overall change?
questions.tip: Percentage changes multiply. +20% then −20% does not cancel out.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The angles in a quadrilateral are x, 2x, 3x and 4x. What is the size of the largest angle?
questions.tip: Angles in a quadrilateral add to 360°, not 180°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A regular octagon and a square share a common side AB. The two shapes are drawn on opposite sides of AB.
At the vertex A there is an angle x outside both shapes, between the other side of the octagon and the other side of the square.
Work out the size of angle x. Give a reason for each stage of your working.
ms: M1 for interior angle of octagon = 135° (e.g. 180 − 360 ÷ 8)
A1 for 135° with reasons (angles at a point add to 360°)
questions.tip: Interior angle of a regular polygon = 180° − (360° ÷ n).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The size of each interior angle of a regular polygon is 11 times the size of each exterior angle.
Work out the number of sides of the polygon.
questions.tip: Interior + exterior = 180° at each vertex. Use that to find the exterior angle first.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABC is an isosceles triangle with AB = AC. The side BC is extended to D. Angle BAC = 2x.
Show that angle ACD = 90° + x.
Give a reason for each stage of your working.
ms: M1 for angle ACB = (180 − 2x) ÷ 2 = 90 − x with reason: base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal and angles in a triangle add to 180°
A1 for 90 + x with reason: angles on a straight line add to 180°
questions.tip: Every step needs a geometric reason with the proper words, e.g. 'angles on a straight line add to 180°'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Regular polygon P has n sides. Regular polygon Q has 2n sides.
Each interior angle of Q is 30° larger than each interior angle of P.
Work out the value of n.
ms: M1 for an expression for an interior (or exterior) angle, e.g. 360/n and 360/(2n)
questions.tip: Work with exterior angles: they are easier, 360 ÷ n. The difference in interior angles equals the difference in exterior angles.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Two angles are co-interior between parallel lines. One is 3x + 10 and the other is 2x − 5. What is x?
questions.tip: Co-interior (allied) angles add to 180°, they are not equal.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Prove that the angles in a triangle add up to 180°.
You may draw a line through one vertex parallel to the opposite side.
ms: B1 for drawing line through A parallel to BC and labelling angles
B1 for identifying both pairs of alternate angles equal, with the reason 'alternate angles are equal'
B1 for completing: the three angles at A lie on a straight line so add to 180°
questions.tip: 'Z angles' and 'F angles' are not accepted as reasons. Use alternate and corresponding.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A pentagon has three angles of 100° each. The other two angles are equal.
Work out the size of one of the other two angles.
ms: M1 for 540 − 300 (sum of interior angles of pentagon = 540°)
questions.tip: Interior angle sum = (n − 2) × 180. For a pentagon this is 540°.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A, B and C are points on a circle with centre O. Angle ACB = 48° (C on the major arc). What is the reflex angle AOB?
questions.tip: Angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference. Then check whether the question wants the reflex angle.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] PT is a tangent to a circle with centre O, touching it at T. OP = 13 cm and the radius is 5 cm. What is PT?
ms: Angle OTP = 90° (tangent ⟂ radius), so PT = √(13² − 5²) = 12 cm.
questions.tip: The right angle is at T, so OP is the hypotenuse. Subtract the squares.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B, C and D are points on a circle. ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. Angle DAB = 3x and angle BCD = 2x + 30°.
Work out the value of x. Give a reason for your answer.
ms: A1 for x = 30 with reason: opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°
questions.tip: Write the full theorem. 'Cyclic quadrilateral' alone does not get the reason mark.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B and C are points on a circle with centre O. TA is a tangent to the circle at A.
Angle TAC = 62°. B is on the major arc AC.
(a) Write down the size of angle ABC. Give a reason.
(b) Work out the size of angle AOC. Give a reason.
ms: B1 for alternate segment theorem stated
B1 for (b) 124° with reason: the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference
questions.tip: Name the theorem in full: 'the angle between a tangent and a chord equals the angle in the alternate segment'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B, C and D lie on a circle with centre O. BD is a diameter. Angle ABD = 28°. Angle CBD = 40°.
Work out angle ADC. Give reasons for each stage of your working.
ms: M1 for angle BAD = 90° (angle in a semicircle is 90°) so angle ADB = 62°
M1 for angle BCD = 90° so angle BDC = 50°
A1 for 112° with all reasons given
questions.tip: Alternative: ABC = 68° and opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add to 180°. Either route needs reasons.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] AB is a diameter of a circle with centre O. C is a point on the circumference.
Prove that angle ACB = 90°.
You must not use the theorem 'the angle in a semicircle is 90°'.
questions.answer: Join OC; triangles AOC and BOC isosceles; 2x + 2y = 180 so x + y = 90
ms: B1 for joining OC and stating OA = OB = OC (radii)
M1 for angle OCA = angle OAC = x and angle OCB = angle OBC = y (base angles of isosceles triangles)
M1 for x + x + y + y = 180 (angles in triangle ABC add to 180°)
A1 for x + y = 90, so angle ACB = 90°
questions.tip: In circle proofs, 'radii are equal so the triangle is isosceles' is usually the key step. Write it.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B and C are points on a circle with centre O. The straight line DAE is a tangent to the circle at A.
Angle CAE = 58°. O lies inside triangle ABC. Angle OCB = 20°.
Work out the size of angle BAC.
Give a reason for each stage of your working.
ms: M1 for angle OAE = 90° (tangent is perpendicular to the radius) so angle OAC = 32°
M1 for angle OCA = 32° (triangle OAC is isosceles because OA = OC are radii)
M1 for angle ABC = 58° (alternate segment theorem)
A1 for angle BAC = 70° (angles in a triangle add to 180°) with all reasons
questions.tip: On a long circle theorem question, write each angle on your own sketch as you find it and give the reason straight away.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B, C and D are points on a circle with centre O. Angle AOC = 2y and D is on the minor arc AC, B is on the major arc.
Prove that angle ADC = 180° − y.
Hence prove that opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°.
questions.answer: ABC = y; reflex AOC = 360 − 2y so ADC = 180 − y; ABC + ADC = 180
ms: M1 for angle ABC = y (angle at centre is twice angle at circumference)
M1 for reflex angle AOC = 360° − 2y (angles at a point add to 360°)
M1 for angle ADC = (360 − 2y) ÷ 2 = 180 − y (angle at centre is twice angle at circumference)
A1 for ABC + ADC = y + 180 − y = 180°, so opposite angles add to 180°
questions.tip: Proofs need algebra AND reasons. Don't use the cyclic quadrilateral theorem itself; that is what you are proving.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which reason correctly explains why two angles subtended by the same chord, on the same side of it, are equal?
options: Angles in the same segment are equal
Angles at the centre are equal
ms: That is the exact circle theorem for angles subtended by the same arc.
questions.tip: Use the exact wording. Vague reasons like 'they're from the same chord' lose the mark.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Triangle A has sides 4 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm. Triangle B is similar with longest side 21 cm. What is the shortest side of triangle B?
questions.tip: Match the longest side with the longest side to find the scale factor.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Two similar cones have heights 6 cm and 9 cm. The smaller cone has volume 32 cm³. What is the volume of the larger cone?
questions.tip: Cube the length scale factor for volumes. 48 uses the length factor only, 72 uses the area factor.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In the triangle ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC so that DE is parallel to BC.
AD = 6 cm, DB = 3 cm, DE = 8 cm.
(a) Work out the length of BC.
(b) Explain why triangles ADE and ABC are similar.
ms: B1 for (b) angle A is common and angle ADE = angle ABC (corresponding angles), so all angles equal
questions.tip: Use AB = AD + DB = 9 cm, not DB = 3 cm, for the larger triangle.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two solid shapes, P and Q, are mathematically similar.
The volume of P is 250 cm³ and the volume of Q is 128 cm³.
The surface area of P is 150 cm².
Work out the surface area of Q.
ms: M1 for length scale factor ³√(64/125) = 4/5
questions.tip: Go volume → length (cube root) → area (square). Never go straight from volume to area.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A company makes two sizes of a bottle. They are mathematically similar.
The large bottle holds 1.728 litres. The small bottle holds 1 litre.
The large bottle is 24 cm tall.
Work out the height of the small bottle.
ms: M1 for volume scale factor 1.728 or 1/1.728
M1 for length scale factor ³√1.728 = 1.2
questions.tip: Volumes in litres are fine as a ratio. Cube root to get the length factor.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCD is a rectangle. M is the midpoint of AB.
Prove that triangle AMD is congruent to triangle BMC.
questions.answer: SAS: AM = MB, AD = BC, angle A = angle B = 90°
ms: B1 for AM = MB (M is the midpoint of AB)
B1 for AD = BC (opposite sides of a rectangle are equal) and angle DAM = angle CBM = 90°
B1 for conclusion: congruent by SAS
questions.tip: Name the condition (SAS, ASA, SSS or RHS) at the end and make sure your three facts match it.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A vertical post 1.8 m tall casts a shadow 2.4 m long. At the same time, a tree casts a shadow 12 m long.
The triangles formed by the posts and shadows are similar.
Work out the height of the tree.
questions.tip: Match the shadow with the shadow and the height with the height.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In triangle ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC with DE parallel to BC.
AD = x cm, DB = 4 cm, DE = 6 cm and BC = 9 cm.
Work out the value of x.
questions.tip: The large triangle's side is AB = x + 4, not 4.

questions.q: [Calculator] A rectangle is 9 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is the length of its diagonal to 1 decimal place?
questions.tip: For the diagonal you add the squares. 8.1 comes from subtracting.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the exact value of sin 60° × cos 30°?
ms: sin 60° = cos 30° = √3/2, so the product is 3/4.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A kite is flying on a string 40 m long. The string makes an angle of 52° with the horizontal ground.
Work out the height of the kite above the ground. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.tip: Check your calculator is in degrees mode.

questions.q:
[Calculator] In triangle ABC, angle ABC = 90°. AB = 7 cm and BC = 24 cm.
(a) Work out the length of AC.
(b) Work out the size of angle BAC. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: BC is opposite angle A and AB is adjacent. Label O, A, H from the angle you want.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Show that tan 30° + tan 60° can be written as 4/√3. Then write 4/√3 in the form a√3.
questions.tip: Rationalise by multiplying top and bottom by √3.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A cube has edges of length 10 cm. The base is ABCD and the top face is EFGH, with E above A, F above B, G above C and H above D.
Work out the angle between the diagonal AG and the base ABCD. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
ms: M1 for identifying the angle GAC with tan GAC = 10/√200
M1 for correct trig, e.g. tan⁻¹(10 ÷ 14.14)
questions.tip: The angle with a plane is between the line and its projection on the plane (here AC). Draw the right-angled triangle ACG.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A pyramid has a rectangular base ABCD with AB = 8 cm and BC = 6 cm. The apex V is vertically above the centre M of the base. Each sloping edge (VA, VB, VC, VD) is 13 cm.
(a) Work out the height VM of the pyramid.
(b) Work out the angle between VA and the base. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
ms: M1 for cos VAM = 5/13 or tan VAM = 12/5
questions.tip: M is the midpoint of the diagonal, so AM is half of AC, not half of AB.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A box is a cuboid measuring 12 cm by 9 cm by 20 cm.
Will a thin rod of length 26 cm fit inside the box? You must show your working.
questions.tip: The longest rod fits along the space diagonal: √(a² + b² + c²).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In triangle PQR, angle PQR = 90°, angle QPR = 45° and PR = 8 cm.
Show that the area of triangle PQR is 16 cm².
ms: M1 for PQ = 8 cos 45° or QR = 8 sin 45°
M1 for 4√2 for both shorter sides (isosceles right-angled triangle)
questions.tip: Non-calculator: use the exact value sin 45° = cos 45° = √2/2.

questions.q: [Calculator] Triangle ABC has AB = 6 cm, AC = 9 cm and angle BAC = 120°. What is its area to 3 s.f.?
questions.tip: 46.8 forgets the ½. sin 120° = sin 60°, so it is positive.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The bearing of B from A is 040°. What is the bearing of A from B?
questions.tip: Add 180° if the bearing is less than 180°, subtract 180° if it is more.

questions.q:
[Calculator] In triangle PQR, PQ = 11 cm, PR = 14 cm and angle QPR = 72°.
Work out the length of QR. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.tip: Work out 2bc cos A as one block and subtract it. Typing 121 + 196 − 2 × 11 × 14 then × cos 72 gives the wrong answer.

questions.q:
[Calculator] In triangle ABC, angle BAC = 65°, angle ABC = 75° and BC = 8 cm.
Work out the length of AC. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for using the sine rule with the correct pairs: AC/sin 75° = 8/sin 65°
questions.tip: Pair each side with the angle opposite it. AC is opposite angle B.

questions.q:
[Calculator] In triangle ABC, AB = 10 cm, BC = 12 cm and angle BAC = 70°.
(a) Work out the size of angle ACB. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
(b) Work out the size of angle ABC. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
ms: M1 for sin C/10 = sin 70°/12 (correct sides paired with opposite angles)
questions.tip: Pair each side with the angle opposite it. Put the unknown angle on top: sin C/c = sin A/a.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A walker leaves point P and walks 15 km on a bearing of 050° to point Q.
She then walks 9 km on a bearing of 160° to point R.
(a) Show that angle PQR = 70°.
(b) Work out the distance PR. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
(c) Work out the bearing of R from P. Give your answer to the nearest degree.
ms: B1 for (a): bearing of P from Q is 050° + 180° = 230°, so angle PQR = 230° − 160° = 70°
M1 for sine rule: sin QPR/9 = sin 70°/14.61..., giving angle QPR = 35.4°
questions.tip: Bearings: always three figures, measured clockwise from north. Draw a north line at every point.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle XYZ has area 20 cm². XY = 8 cm and angle YXZ = 30°.
Work out the length of XZ. You must show your working.
questions.tip: sin 30° = 1/2 exactly. This one can be done without a calculator.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A triangle has sides 7 cm, 8 cm and 13 cm.
Show that the largest angle is 120°.
ms: M1 for using the cosine rule with 13 opposite the angle: cos θ = (7² + 8² − 13²)/(2 × 7 × 8)
questions.tip: The largest angle is opposite the longest side.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] In triangle ABC, you know angle A, angle B and side AC. Which method finds BC?
ms: You have a side with its opposite angle (AC with B) and want BC opposite A: sine rule.
questions.tip: The cosine rule needs two sides and the included angle, or all three sides.

questions.q:
[Calculator] ABCD is a quadrilateral.
AB = 5 cm, BC = 8 cm and angle ABC = 100°.
CD = 9 cm and angle ACD = 30°.
Work out the area of ABCD. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for area ABC = ½ × 5 × 8 × sin 100° (= 19.69...)
M1 for area ACD = ½ × AC × 9 × sin 30° (= 22.82...)
M1 for adding the two areas
questions.tip: Keep AC unrounded in your calculator memory. Rounding AC to 10 early drops you out of the accuracy range.

questions.q: [Calculator] A semicircle has diameter 10 cm. What is its perimeter to 3 s.f.?
ms: Curved part = ½ × π × 10 = 15.7 cm, plus the diameter 10 cm = 25.7 cm.
questions.tip: 15.7 forgets the straight edge. Perimeter is all the way round.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A sector has radius 6 cm and area 15π cm². What is the angle of the sector?
questions.tip: Area of the full circle is 36π, so the fraction is 15/36.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A circle has circumference 30π cm.
Work out the area of the circle. Give your answer in terms of π.
questions.tip: Circumference = πd, so d = 30 and r = 15. Do not square 30.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A circle fits exactly inside a square of side 10 cm, touching all four sides.
Work out the area of the square not covered by the circle. Give your answer in the form a − bπ.
questions.tip: Exact form means leave π in. Don't round to 21.5 here.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A sector of a circle has angle 40° and perimeter 30 cm.
Work out the radius of the sector. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.tip: Perimeter includes the two radii as well as the arc. Factorise r out.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A chord AB of length 12 cm is drawn in a circle with centre O and radius 8 cm.
(a) Show that angle AOB = 97.2°, correct to 1 decimal place.
(b) Work out the area of the minor segment cut off by AB. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for half-angle sin⁻¹(6/8) or cosine rule cos AOB = (64 + 64 − 144)/128
M1 for triangle area = ½ × 8 × 8 × sin 97.18° (= 31.75...)
questions.tip: Segment = sector − triangle. Use ½ab sin C for the triangle because it is not right-angled.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A running track is made of two straight sections, each 40 m long, joined by two semicircles of diameter 25 m.
Work out the total distance around the track. Give your answer to the nearest metre.
ms: M1 for the two semicircles making a full circle: π × 25 (= 78.54...)
questions.tip: Two semicircles = one full circle.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A sector has angle 120° and arc length 8π cm.
Work out the area of the sector. Give your answer in terms of π.
questions.tip: Use the arc length to find the radius first, then the area formula.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A cylinder has radius 4 cm and height 10 cm. What is its volume in terms of π?
questions.tip: 80π is the curved surface area. 40π forgets to square the radius.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A sphere has surface area 100π cm². What is its radius?
questions.tip: Surface area of a sphere is 4πr², not πr².

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A cone and a cylinder have the same radius and the same volume. The cylinder has height 8 cm. What is the height of the cone?
questions.tip: A cone has one third the volume of a cylinder with the same height, so it must be 3 times as tall.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A pyramid has a square base of side 6 cm. Its volume is 72 cm³.
Work out the height of the pyramid.
questions.tip: Volume of a pyramid = ⅓ × base area × height.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A toy is made from a solid hemisphere of radius 3 cm joined to a solid cone of radius 3 cm. The flat faces are joined together.
The total volume of the toy is 30π cm³.
Work out the height of the cone.
ms: M1 for cone volume = ⅓π × 9 × h = 3πh
questions.tip: Half a sphere: ½ × (4/3)πr³ = (2/3)πr³.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A bucket is in the shape of a frustum. It is made by removing a cone of height 40 cm and base radius 10 cm from a cone of height 60 cm and base radius 15 cm.
(a) Show that the volume of the bucket is (9500/3)π cm³.
(b) Water is poured into the bucket until it is full. Will 10 litres of water fit in the bucket? Give a reason for your answer.
questions.answer: (a) ⅓π(15² × 60) − ⅓π(10² × 40) = 4500π − 4000π/3 = 9500π/3 (b) No: the bucket holds 9948 cm³ = 9.95 litres, which is less than 10 litres
ms: M1 for volume of large cone ⅓π × 15² × 60 = 4500π
M1 for volume of small cone ⅓π × 10² × 40 = 4000π/3
A1 for conclusion: No, 10 litres will not all fit, as the bucket holds 9.95 litres
questions.tip: 1 litre = 1000 cm³. State a clear conclusion that matches your number.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A solid cone has base radius 6 cm and perpendicular height 8 cm.
Work out the total surface area of the cone. Give your answer in terms of π.
ms: M1 for curved surface area πrl = 60π
questions.tip: Curved surface area uses the slant height l, not the perpendicular height.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A solid metal sphere of radius 6 cm is melted down. All of the metal is used to make small solid cones, each with radius 2 cm and height 3 cm.
Work out the number of cones made.
questions.tip: Leave π in both volumes and it cancels, so no calculator is needed.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cylinder of radius 9 cm contains water. Three identical solid spheres, each of radius 3 cm, are dropped into the water and are completely covered.
Work out how much the water level rises. Give your answer as a fraction.
ms: M1 for volume of one sphere (4/3)π × 27 = 36π
questions.tip: The rise in water level has the same volume as the spheres that went in.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A lampshade is the curved surface of a frustum. It is made by removing a small cone of base radius 6 cm and slant height 10 cm from a large cone of base radius 12 cm and slant height 20 cm.
Work out the area of material needed for the lampshade. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for curved surface area of large cone π × 12 × 20 = 240π
M1 for curved surface area of small cone π × 6 × 10 = 60π
questions.tip: Only the curved surface: no top or bottom circles in a lampshade.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the locus of points exactly 3 cm from a line segment AB of length 8 cm?
options: Two parallel lines 3 cm from AB joined by semicircles at A and B
Two parallel lines 3 cm from AB only
ms: The 'stadium' shape: parallel lines alongside, semicircles of radius 3 cm around each end.
questions.tip: Don't forget the rounded ends around A and B.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A point is closer to A than to B. Which side of which line does it lie?
options: On the angle bisector at A
The B side of the perpendicular bisector of AB
Inside a circle centred at A
The A side of the perpendicular bisector of AB
ms: The perpendicular bisector is the set of points equidistant from A and B; points closer to A are on A's side.
questions.tip: 'Closer to A than B' always means the perpendicular bisector of AB.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Describe how to construct an equilateral triangle with sides of 5 cm using only a ruler and compasses.
questions.answer: Draw AB = 5 cm; arcs radius 5 cm from A and B; join intersection
ms: B1 for drawing a line AB of 5 cm and setting compasses to 5 cm
B1 for drawing arcs centred on A and on B that intersect at C, then joining AC and BC, leaving arcs visible
questions.tip: Leave all your construction arcs. Rubbing them out loses the marks.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two radio masts, A and B, are 12 km apart.
A phone can receive a signal if it is within 8 km of mast A or within 6 km of mast B.
A phone is placed at point P on the straight line AB, 7 km from A.
(a) Can the phone receive a signal from both masts? Give a reason.
(b) Describe the region where a phone can receive a signal from both masts.
questions.answer: (a) Yes: 7 ≤ 8 from A and 5 ≤ 6 from B (b) the overlap of a circle radius 8 km centred A and a circle radius 6 km centred B
ms: B1 for (b) the region inside both circles (circle centre A radius 8 km, circle centre B radius 6 km)
questions.tip: Distances along the line add up: P is 7 km from A, so 5 km from B.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Describe how to construct an angle of 30° at point A on a straight line, using only a ruler and compasses.
ms: B1 for constructing a 60° angle: arc from A cutting line at B, same radius arc from B to give C, join AC
B1 for bisecting angle CAB: equal arcs from B and C crossing at D
B1 for joining AD, leaving all arcs
questions.tip: 30° = half of 60°. Every construction is built from the equilateral triangle and the bisector.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A horse is tied by a rope of length 7 m to a post at corner P of a rectangular stable. The stable measures 3 m by 5 m. The horse cannot go inside the stable. The ground around the stable is open grass.
Work out the area of grass the horse can reach. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for three-quarters of a circle of radius 7: (3/4) × π × 49 (= 36.75π)
M1 for a quarter circle of radius 7 − 3 = 4 round the 3 m side (4π)
M1 for a quarter circle of radius 7 − 5 = 2 round the 5 m side (π)
questions.tip: When the rope wraps round a corner, a new smaller quarter circle appears. Sketch every region.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABC is a triangle. A point P inside the triangle is equidistant from AB and AC, and is equidistant from B and C.
Describe how you would find the position of P using ruler and compasses constructions.
questions.answer: Intersection of the bisector of angle BAC and the perpendicular bisector of BC
ms: B1 for constructing the bisector of angle BAC (equidistant from lines AB and AC)
B1 for constructing the perpendicular bisector of BC (equidistant from points B and C)
B1 for P is where the two lines cross
questions.tip: Equidistant from two LINES → angle bisector. Equidistant from two POINTS → perpendicular bisector.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The point (2, 5) is translated by the vector (−3, 4). What are its new coordinates?
questions.tip: Translations add on: top number to x, bottom number to y.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The point (3, 1) is rotated 180° about the origin. Where does it go?
ms: A 180° rotation about the origin changes (x, y) to (−x, −y).
questions.tip: (3, −1) is a reflection in the x-axis, not a rotation.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A shape with area 5 cm² is enlarged by scale factor −3. What is the area of the image?
questions.tip: Negative scale factors flip the shape but areas are never negative.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle A has vertices (1, 1), (4, 1) and (1, 3).
It is reflected in the line x = 5 to give triangle B.
Write down the coordinates of the vertices of triangle B.
questions.tip: x = 5 is a vertical line. Each point keeps its y-coordinate and the same distance on the other side.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle P has vertices (2, 1), (4, 1) and (4, 2).
Triangle Q has vertices (−1, 2), (−1, 4) and (−2, 4).
Describe fully the single transformation that maps P onto Q.
questions.tip: A rotation needs three things: the word rotation, the angle with direction, and the centre.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle T has vertices (3, 4), (7, 4) and (3, 8).
Triangle T is enlarged by scale factor −1/2 with centre (1, 2).
Work out the coordinates of the vertices of the image.
ms: M1 for a correct vector from the centre to a vertex, e.g. (2, 2) for (3, 4)
M1 for multiplying by −1/2 and adding to the centre for at least one vertex
questions.tip: Negative scale factor: the image is on the opposite side of the centre and upside down.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Shape S is reflected in the line y = x to give shape S'. Shape S' is then rotated 90° clockwise about the origin to give shape S''.
Describe fully the single transformation that maps S onto S''.
ms: M1 for tracking a point, e.g. (3, 1) → (1, 3) → (3, −1)
A1 for in the line y = 0 (the x-axis)
questions.tip: Track the coordinates of a test point or two through both transformations. A sketch on squared paper helps.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Shape A is enlarged by scale factor 3 with centre (0, 0) to give shape B. The point (2, −1) is a vertex of shape A.
(a) Write down the coordinates of the corresponding vertex of B.
(b) Shape A has a perimeter of 14 cm. Write down the perimeter of shape B.
questions.tip: Lengths (including perimeter) multiply by the scale factor. Only areas multiply by its square.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] p = (4, −3). What is −2p?
questions.tip: Multiply both numbers, and watch the signs: −2 × −3 = +6.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] ABCD is a parallelogram with AB = p and AD = q. What is the vector BD?
questions.tip: Go from B to A (backwards along p) then A to D.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which of these vectors is parallel to 3a − 6b?
questions.tip: Parallel means one is a multiple of the other, even if the multiple is negative.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] a = (2, 5) and b = (−3, 1).
Work out 3a − 2b as a column vector.
questions.tip: Subtracting a negative: 6 − (−6) = 12.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OAB is a triangle. OA = a and OB = b.
P is the point on OA such that OP : PA = 2 : 1.
Q is the point on OB such that OQ : QB = 2 : 1.
Show that PQ is parallel to AB.
questions.answer: PQ = (2/3)(b − a) and AB = b − a
ms: A1 for PQ = (2/3)(b − a) = (2/3)AB so PQ is parallel to AB
questions.tip: To show parallel, write one vector as a number times the other, and say so in words.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OAB is a triangle. OA = 6a and OB = 6b.
C is the point on AB such that AC : CB = 1 : 2.
D is the midpoint of OB.
OA is extended to the point E so that A is the midpoint of OE.
Prove that D, C and E lie on a straight line.
questions.answer: DC = 4a − b and DE = 12a − 3b = 3(4a − b), so DE = 3DC; shared point D, so collinear
ms: A1 for DE = 3DC, so DE is parallel to DC and D is common, hence D, C, E are collinear
questions.tip: Find the vectors you need from a common point (D here). Then show one is a multiple of the other and mention the shared point.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OAB is a triangle. OA = a and OB = b.
P is a point on AB. OP is parallel to the vector a + 2b.
Work out the ratio AP : PB.
ms: M1 for OP = a + λ(b − a) = (1 − λ)a + λb, where AP = λAB
M1 for using parallel to a + 2b: λ = 2(1 − λ)
questions.tip: Write OP with an unknown fraction λ of AB, then compare the coefficients of a and b.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The vectors p = (k, 3) and q = (8, 6) are such that p + q is parallel to (2, 1).
Find the value of k.
questions.tip: Parallel to (2, 1) means the top number is twice the bottom number.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The vector v = (6, −8).
Work out the magnitude of 1/2 v.
questions.tip: Magnitude uses Pythagoras: √(x² + y²). It is always positive.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A fair spinner has 5 equal sections numbered 1 to 5. It is spun 60 times. How many times would you expect it to land on an even number?
questions.tip: 2 and 4 are the even numbers, so two out of five sections.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The probability that a train is late is 0.15. What is the probability it is not late?
questions.tip: Probabilities of 'A' and 'not A' always add to 1.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A menu has 4 starters, 6 mains and 3 desserts. How many different three-course meals (one of each) are possible?
questions.tip: Multiply the choices, don't add them.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the probabilities that a biased dice lands on each number.
Number | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6
Probability | 0.1 | 0.2 | x | 0.15 | 2x | 0.25
(a) Work out the value of x.
(b) The dice is rolled 200 times. Work out an estimate for the number of times it lands on 5.
questions.tip: In (b) the probability of 5 is 2x = 0.2, not x.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains only red, blue and green counters.
The ratio of red to blue to green is 2 : 5 : 3.
There are 18 more blue counters than red counters.
A counter is taken at random. Work out the probability that it is green, and the number of green counters in the bag.
questions.tip: The difference between blue and red is 3 parts, not 18 parts.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A four-digit code uses the digits 0 to 9.
The first digit cannot be 0 and no digit can be used more than once.
Work out how many different codes are possible.
ms: M1 for 9 choices for the first digit
M1 for 9 × 8 × 7 for the remaining digits (0 is now allowed)
questions.tip: After the first digit, 0 becomes available, so the second digit still has 9 options.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] At a fair, it costs £1 to roll a fair dice. If it lands on 6, the player wins £4. Otherwise they win nothing.
60 people play the game once each.
Work out an estimate for the profit the fair makes.
ms: M1 for expected number of sixes = 60 × 1/6 = 10
questions.tip: Profit = money taken in − prizes paid out.

questions.q:
