[Non-calculator] There are only red and yellow sweets in a bag. There are 5 more yellow sweets than red sweets.
The probability of taking a red sweet at random is 2/9.
Work out the number of yellow sweets in the bag.
questions.tip: Total sweets = r + (r + 5) = 2r + 5. Form an equation from the probability.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The probability that Ella wins a game is 0.6. She plays two games. The games are independent. What is the probability she wins both?
questions.tip: AND means multiply along the branches.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The probability it rains on Saturday is 0.3 and on Sunday is 0.4, independently. What is the probability it rains on exactly one of the days?
questions.tip: Exactly one has two routes: rain then dry, or dry then rain. Add them.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A bag has 5 red and 4 blue counters. Two are taken without replacement. What is P(two blue)?
questions.tip: 16/81 is with replacement. Without replacement, the second fraction is out of 8.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 5 red counters and 4 blue counters.
Two counters are taken at random without replacement.
Work out the probability that the two counters are different colours.
questions.tip: Different colours can happen in two orders: red then blue, or blue then red.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The probability that a seed germinates is 0.85.
Three seeds are planted. They germinate independently.
Work out the probability that at least one seed does NOT germinate.
questions.tip: 'At least one' questions: 1 − P(none). Here 'none fail' means all three germinate.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Bag A contains 3 red and 2 blue balls. Bag B contains 4 red and 4 blue balls.
A ball is taken at random from bag A and put into bag B.
A ball is then taken at random from bag B.
Work out the probability that the ball taken from bag B is red.
ms: M1 for adding the two products
questions.tip: After a ball is moved, bag B has 9 balls, not 8.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] There are n counters in a bag. 3 of the counters are green.
Two counters are taken at random without replacement.
The probability that both counters are green is 1/15.
(a) Show that n² − n − 90 = 0.
(b) Work out the value of n.
ms: A1 for 90 = n² − n, so n² − n − 90 = 0 shown
questions.tip: In a 'show that', every line of algebra must be written down. Reject the negative root with a reason.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The probability that Tom walks to school is 0.4. Otherwise he takes the bus.
If he walks, the probability he is late is 0.3. If he takes the bus, the probability he is late is 0.2.
Work out the probability that Tom is late.
questions.tip: Draw the tree: first branch walk/bus, second branch late/on time.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A box contains 4 red pens and 6 blue pens.
Three pens are taken at random without replacement.
Work out the probability that exactly two of the pens are red.
ms: M1 for one correct product, e.g. 4/10 × 3/9 × 6/8 (= 1/10)
M1 for recognising there are 3 orders (RRB, RBR, BRR)
questions.tip: List the orders. Each has the same probability, so multiply one by 3.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] ξ = {1, 2, ..., 12}. A = {factors of 12}. What is A'?
ms: Factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. A' is everything else in ξ.
questions.tip: A' means NOT in A. Don't forget 8, 9 and 10.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] In a Venn diagram, A only = 8, A ∩ B = 5, B only = 12, neither = 15. A person in set A is chosen at random. What is the probability that they are also in set B?
ms: There are 8 + 5 = 13 people in A, and 5 of them are also in B: 5/13.
questions.tip: The person is chosen from A, so the denominator is the total in A (13), not 40.
A ∪ B means in A, or B, or both. Don't count the overlap twice.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 60 people were asked if they like tea (T) or coffee (C).
30 like tea. 25 like coffee. 11 like neither.
(a) Draw a Venn diagram to show this information, giving the number in each region.
(b) One of the people who likes coffee is chosen at random. Work out the probability they also like tea.
questions.answer: (a) T only 24, T ∩ C 6, C only 19, neither 11 (b) 6/25
ms: A1 for all four regions correct: 24, 6, 19, 11
questions.tip: Find the intersection first, then work outwards.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 30 students were asked which of three sports they play: football (F), hockey (H) and netball (N).
2 play all three. 5 play football and hockey. 6 play hockey and netball. 3 play football and netball.
11 play football. 15 play hockey. 14 play netball.
(a) How many students play none of the three sports?
(b) A student who plays hockey is chosen at random. Work out the probability that they play exactly two sports.
ms: M1 for regions F∩H only = 3, H∩N only = 4, F∩N only = 1 (subtracting the 2 in the centre)
M1 for F only = 5, H only = 6, N only = 7
questions.tip: In three-set Venn diagrams start from the centre and subtract it from each pair before filling the 'only' regions.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which region does A' ∩ B describe?
options: In A but not in B
In B but not in A
ms: A' means not in A and ∩ B means also in B.
questions.tip: Read set notation from the symbols: ' is NOT, ∩ is AND, ∪ is OR.

questions.q:
[Calculator] P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.5 and P(A ∪ B) = 0.8.
(a) Work out P(A ∩ B).
(b) Are A and B independent? Give a reason for your answer.
questions.answer: (a) 0.3 (b) Yes, since P(A) × P(B) = 0.3 = P(A ∩ B)
ms: B1 for Yes with reason 0.6 × 0.5 = 0.3 = P(A ∩ B)
questions.tip: Independent means P(A ∩ B) = P(A) × P(B). Show both numbers.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] In a group of 40 people, 18 are left-handed. 10 of the left-handed people are female. A left-handed person is chosen at random. What is the probability they are female?
ms: The group is restricted to the 18 left-handed people, of whom 10 are female.
questions.tip: 'A left-handed person is chosen' means the denominator is 18.

questions.q:
[Calculator] For two events A and B, P(A) = 0.5.
If A happens, the probability that B happens is 0.4.
If A does not happen, the probability that B happens is 0.2.
Given that B happens, what is the probability that A happened?
ms: Tree diagram: P(A and B) = 0.5 × 0.4 = 0.2, P(not A and B) = 0.5 × 0.2 = 0.1, so P(B) = 0.3. Probability A happened given B = 0.2 ÷ 0.3 = 2/3.
questions.tip: Reverse the condition: P(A and B) ÷ P(B). Find P(B) by adding both branches that end in B.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The two-way table shows information about the 120 students in Year 11.
 | Walk | Bus | Car | Total
Boys | 25 | 18 | ? | 60
Girls | ? | 22 | 14 | 60
Total | ? | ? | ? | 120
(a) Complete the table (write down the missing values).
(b) A student who travels by bus is chosen at random. Work out the probability that the student is a girl.
(c) A student is chosen at random. Work out the probability that the student is a boy who travels by car.
questions.answer: (a) Boys car 17, Girls walk 24, Walk total 49, Bus total 40, Car total 31 (b) 22/40 = 11/20 (c) 17/120
ms: M1 for boys car = 60 − 25 − 18 = 17 and girls walk = 60 − 22 − 14 = 24
questions.tip: Read who is being chosen from. 'A student who travels by bus' means out of 40, not 120.

questions.q:
[Calculator] 2% of people in a town have a certain disease.
A test for the disease gives a positive result for 95% of people who have the disease.
The test also gives a positive result for 10% of people who do NOT have the disease.
A person is chosen at random and tests positive.
Work out the probability that the person has the disease. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for a correct tree or frequency method
M1 for P(no disease and positive) = 0.98 × 0.1 = 0.098
questions.tip: Most people who test positive do not have the disease here. Imagine 1000 people to make the numbers concrete.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 4 red and 6 blue counters. Two counters are taken at random without replacement.
Given that at least one of the counters is red, work out the probability that both counters are red.
ms: M1 for P(at least one red) = 1 − 6/10 × 5/9 = 2/3
questions.tip: P(both red | at least one red) = P(both red) ÷ P(at least one red), because 'both red' is inside 'at least one red'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] P(A) = 0.7. If A happens, the probability that B happens is 0.4.
(a) Work out P(A ∩ B).
(b) P(B) = 0.4. Are A and B independent? Give a reason.
ms: B1 for Yes with reason P(A) × P(B) = 0.28 = P(A ∩ B) (or the probability of B is 0.4 whether or not A happens)
questions.tip: If knowing A happened doesn't change the chance of B, the events are independent.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Two fair six-sided dice are rolled. Given that the total score is at least 10, work out the probability that both dice show the same number.
ms: M1 for listing the 6 outcomes with total at least 10: (4,6), (5,5), (6,4), (5,6), (6,5), (6,6)
questions.tip: Restrict the sample space to the outcomes you are given, then count.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The table gives information about the ages of 30 people at a party.
Age (a years) | Frequency
0 < a ≤ 10 | 3
10 < a ≤ 20 | 7
20 < a ≤ 30 | 12
30 < a ≤ 40 | 6
40 < a ≤ 50 | 2
(a) Write down the modal class.
(b) Work out an estimate for the mean age.
ms: M1 for Σfx = 720 and dividing by 30
questions.tip: Divide by the total frequency (30), not by the number of groups (5).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The ages of 30 people at a party are grouped: 0 < a ≤ 10: 3 people, 10 < a ≤ 20: 7, 20 < a ≤ 30: 12, 30 < a ≤ 40: 6, 40 < a ≤ 50: 2. Which class contains the median age?
ms: The median is between the 15th and 16th values. Running totals: 3, 10, 22, so it is in 20 < a ≤ 30.
questions.tip: Use running totals to locate the middle value. Don't pick the middle class.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The mean of 4 numbers is 12. When a fifth number x is added the mean is 14. What is x?
questions.tip: Work with totals, not means.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which average is most affected by one extreme value?
ms: The mean uses every value, so one extreme value can drag it a long way.
questions.tip: IQR is a measure of spread, not an average.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The mean weight of 20 boys is 58 kg. The mean weight of 30 girls is 52 kg.
Work out the mean weight of all 50 students.
questions.tip: (58 + 52) ÷ 2 = 55 is wrong because the groups are different sizes.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows information about the times taken by some students to solve a puzzle.
Time (t seconds) | Frequency
0 < t ≤ 10 | 4
10 < t ≤ 20 | x
20 < t ≤ 30 | 6
An estimate for the mean time is 16 seconds.
Work out the value of x.
questions.tip: Set up the mean equation with the total frequency 10 + x on the bottom, then multiply out.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the distances, d km, that 50 people travel to work.
Distance (d km) | Frequency
0 < d ≤ 10 | 20
10 < d ≤ 20 | 6
20 < d ≤ 30 | 8
30 < d ≤ 40 | 16
Amir says, 'The median must be in the class 0 < d ≤ 10 because that is the modal class.'
Is Amir correct? Give a reason for your answer.
questions.answer: No: the median is the 25.5th value; running totals 20, 26, so the median is in 10 < d ≤ 20
ms: M1 for median position 25th/26th (or 25.5th) and cumulative totals 20, 26
A1 for 'No' with the median class 10 < d ≤ 20
questions.tip: The modal class and the median class are often different. Always use running totals.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The mean of a set of 8 numbers is 15. The mean of a different set of 12 numbers is m.
The mean of all 20 numbers is 18.
Work out the value of m.
questions.tip: Turn every mean into a total first.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A box plot has lower quartile 32 and upper quartile 50. What is the interquartile range?
questions.tip: IQR is a difference, not an average of the two quartiles.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A cumulative frequency graph for 120 students shows 84 students scored 60 marks or less. How many scored more than 60?
questions.tip: Cumulative frequency counts 'up to'. Subtract from the total for 'more than'.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Group A: median 42, IQR 8. Group B: median 42, IQR 15. Which statement is correct?
options: Group B did better on average
Group A's results are more consistent
Group B's results are more consistent
ms: Smaller IQR means the middle 50% is less spread out, so more consistent.
questions.tip: Same median means neither did better on average. Look at the spread.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the times, t minutes, that 64 people waited in a queue.
Time (t minutes) | Frequency
0 < t ≤ 5 | 6
5 < t ≤ 10 | 14
10 < t ≤ 15 | 22
15 < t ≤ 20 | 16
20 < t ≤ 25 | 6
(a) Complete a cumulative frequency table.
(b) Write down the coordinates of the points you would plot to draw a cumulative frequency graph.
ms: M1 for plotting at the upper class boundaries 5, 10, 15, 20, 25
questions.tip: Plot cumulative frequency at the END of each class, not the midpoint.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The waiting times, t minutes, of 64 people in a queue are shown on a cumulative frequency graph. The graph is drawn by joining these points (t, cumulative frequency) with straight lines:
(0, 0), (5, 6), (10, 20), (15, 42), (20, 58), (25, 64).
(a) Use the graph to find an estimate for the median waiting time.
(b) Use the graph to find an estimate for the interquartile range.
(c) Estimate the percentage of people who waited more than 18 minutes.
ms: M1 for reading at cf 16 and 48 (LQ ≈ 8.6, UQ ≈ 16.9)
questions.tip: For n = 64 read the median at 32, the quartiles at 16 and 48. Draw the lines on the graph to show your method.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The box plots compare the reaction times (in ms) of two groups.
Group X: min 210, LQ 240, median 265, UQ 290, max 340
Group Y: min 190, LQ 230, median 250, UQ 260, max 330
Compare the reaction times of the two groups.
questions.answer: Group Y faster on average (median 250 < 265); Group Y more consistent (IQR 30 < 50)
ms: B1 for comparing medians with values: Y has lower median (250 vs 265) so Y is faster on average
B1 for comparing IQRs with values: X IQR 50, Y IQR 30
B1 for interpreting spread in context: Y's reaction times are more consistent
questions.tip: Two comparisons: one average and one spread, each with the numbers and a sentence in context.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] For a set of data, the lower quartile is 28 and the upper quartile is 40.
An outlier is a value more than 1.5 × IQR below the lower quartile or above the upper quartile.
The largest value is 60 and the smallest is 12.
Show that the largest value is an outlier but the smallest value is not.
questions.answer: IQR = 12, 1.5 × 12 = 18; upper limit 58 < 60 so outlier; lower limit 10 < 12 so not
ms: A1 for 60 > 58 is an outlier and 12 > 10 is not, both stated
questions.tip: State both limits and compare each value with the right one.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A class 10 < x ≤ 25 has frequency 45. What is the frequency density?
questions.tip: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width, not width ÷ frequency.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A histogram bar for 30 < t ≤ 50 has frequency density 1.5. What frequency does it represent?
questions.tip: Multiply by the class width (20), not the upper boundary (50).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the masses of 60 apples.
Mass (m grams) | Frequency
80 < m ≤ 100 | 8
100 < m ≤ 110 | 14
110 < m ≤ 120 | 18
120 < m ≤ 150 | 15
150 < m ≤ 200 | 5
Work out the frequency density for each class, ready to draw a histogram.
ms: M1 for using frequency ÷ class width for at least two classes
A1 for at least three correct
questions.tip: Check the class widths: they are 20, 10, 10, 30, 50 here.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A histogram shows the times, t minutes, that customers spent in a shop. The bars are:
0 < t ≤ 10: frequency density 1.5
10 < t ≤ 15: frequency density 4.4
15 < t ≤ 25: frequency density 3.2
25 < t ≤ 40: frequency density 1.2
40 < t ≤ 60: frequency density 0.4
(a) Work out the total number of customers.
(b) Work out an estimate for the number of customers who spent between 12 and 30 minutes in the shop.
ms: M1 for frequency = FD × width for at least two bars
M1 for a correct partial bar: 3 × 4.4 = 13.2 (12 to 15) or 5 × 1.2 = 6 (25 to 30)
questions.tip: For part of a bar, use FD × the part width, assuming values are spread evenly across the class.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A histogram has no scale on the frequency density axis.
The bar for 0 < x ≤ 20 is 3 cm tall and represents a frequency of 12.
The bar for 20 < x ≤ 30 is 7 cm tall.
The bar for 30 < x ≤ 50 is 4.5 cm tall.
Work out the frequencies for the classes 20 < x ≤ 30 and 30 < x ≤ 50.
ms: M1 for FD of first bar = 12 ÷ 20 = 0.6, so 1 cm = 0.2
M1 for FD × width for another bar, e.g. 1.4 × 10
questions.tip: Find what 1 cm of height means in frequency density first, then multiply by class widths.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The histogram for some data has bars:
0 < x ≤ 10: frequency density 2
10 < x ≤ 30: frequency density 3
30 < x ≤ 60: frequency density 1
Work out an estimate for the median.
ms: M1 for median at the 55th value, which is 35 into the 10 < x ≤ 30 class
questions.tip: Find the frequencies first, then the median position, then how far into the class it lies.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A histogram has a bar for 20 < x ≤ 50 with frequency density 0.8 and a bar for 50 < x ≤ 60 with frequency density 2.4. Which statement is true?
options: The 50-60 class has three times the frequency
The 50-60 class has a higher frequency
The 20-50 class has three times the frequency
Both classes have the same frequency
questions.tip: Area, not height, shows frequency in a histogram.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which of these is most likely to give a biased sample of a town's residents' views about the bus service?
options: Picking names at random from the electoral roll
Using a random number generator on a full list of households
A stratified sample by age group
Asking people waiting at a bus stop
ms: People at a bus stop all use buses, so they don't represent the whole town.
questions.tip: Bias means some groups are over- or under-represented.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A company has 800 workers: 240 in sales, 360 in production and 200 in admin. A stratified sample of 40 is taken. How many should be from production?
questions.tip: Use the fraction of the whole population in that group, multiplied by the sample size.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A pond contains an unknown number of frogs.
On Monday, 30 frogs are caught, marked and released.
On Tuesday, 45 frogs are caught. 6 of them are marked.
(a) Work out an estimate for the number of frogs in the pond.
(b) State one assumption you have made.
questions.answer: (a) 225 (b) e.g. the population did not change between Monday and Tuesday / marked frogs mix randomly
ms: B1 for a valid assumption, e.g. no frogs born, died, arrived or left; marks not lost; equal chance of being caught
questions.tip: Marked in the second sample over total second sample = marked total over population.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Mia wants to find the most popular sport at her school of 1200 students. She asks the first 20 students who arrive at the football club.
Give two reasons why her sample may not be reliable.
questions.answer: Sample too small; biased towards football players
ms: B1 for sample too small (20 out of 1200)
B1 for biased: students at the football club are likely to prefer football
questions.tip: Give specific reasons linked to the context, not just 'it's biased'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A college has 450 students: 180 in Year 1, 150 in Year 2 and 120 in Year 3.
A stratified sample of 30 students is to be taken by year.
Work out how many students from each year should be in the sample.
ms: M1 for 180/450 × 30 or equivalent for any group
questions.tip: Check your sample numbers add up to the sample size.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A scientist uses capture-recapture to estimate the number of fish in a lake as 480.
She marked 60 fish on the first day. On the second day she caught some fish and found that 8 of them were marked.
(a) How many fish did she catch on the second day?
(b) Explain why her estimate might be too high if some marks came off the fish.
questions.answer: (a) 64 (b) fewer marked fish would be recaptured, making the fraction marked look smaller, so the population estimate is bigger
ms: B1 for explanation: fewer fish counted as marked, so 8 would be lower than it should be, giving a larger estimate
questions.tip: In explanations, say which number changes and in which direction.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A scatter graph shows that as the number of hours of TV watched increases, test scores decrease. What type of correlation is this?
ms: One variable goes up as the other goes down.
questions.tip: Correlation describes the pattern; it does not prove one causes the other.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A line of best fit is used to estimate a value well outside the range of the data. Why is this unreliable?
options: Correlation is always weak at the ends
The pattern may not continue beyond the data
The line of best fit must pass through the origin
ms: This is extrapolation: there's no evidence the trend continues.
questions.tip: Estimates inside the data range (interpolation) are more reliable than outside it (extrapolation).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A scatter graph shows the engine size (litres) and fuel economy (miles per gallon) of 12 cars. The points show strong negative correlation.
(a) Describe the relationship between engine size and fuel economy.
(b) A 1.6 litre car has fuel economy 80 mpg, far above the other cars of similar size. What is this point called?
questions.answer: (a) As engine size increases, fuel economy decreases (b) an outlier
ms: B1 for (a) larger engine size, lower mpg (in context)
questions.tip: Describe the relationship in context, not just 'negative'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A line of best fit for a scatter graph of plant height, h cm, against time, t weeks, passes through the points (2, 6) and (10, 18).
(a) Find the equation of the line of best fit in the form h = mt + c.
(b) Use your equation to estimate the height at 7 weeks.
(c) Explain why it may not be sensible to use the equation to estimate the height at 40 weeks.
questions.answer: (a) h = 1.5t + 3 (b) 13.5 cm (c) extrapolation; plants stop growing
ms: B1 for (c) 40 weeks is outside the data range (extrapolation) and the plant will not keep growing at the same rate
questions.tip: The gradient in context is the growth rate: 1.5 cm per week.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A scatter graph shows the number of ice creams sold and the number of people swimming at a beach each day. There is strong positive correlation.
Kai says, 'Eating ice cream makes people go swimming.'
(a) Is Kai correct? Give a reason.
(b) Suggest a third variable that might explain the correlation.
questions.answer: (a) No, correlation does not prove causation (b) temperature / sunshine
ms: B1 for 'No' with reason: correlation does not show one causes the other
B1 for (b) temperature, hot weather or sunshine
B1 for explaining both increase on hotter days
questions.tip: Always separate 'related to' from 'causes'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The gradient of a line of best fit of the price of a used car (£) against its age (years) is −1200.
Interpret the gradient in this context.
questions.answer: The car's value decreases by about £1200 for each extra year of age
ms: B1 for per year of age (in context)
questions.tip: Interpret gradient as 'change in y for each 1 unit of x', with units.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OABC is a trapezium. OA = a and OC = c. CB is parallel to OA and CB = 2a.
X is the point on OB such that OX : XB = 1 : 2.
Prove that A, X and C lie on a straight line.
questions.answer: AX = (1/3)(c − a) and AC = c − a, so AX = (1/3)AC with A common
ms: A1 for AX = (1/3)AC, so AX is parallel to AC and they share point A, so A, X, C are collinear
questions.tip: Simplify each vector fully before comparing. The final sentence must mention 'parallel' and 'common point'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B, C and D are points on a circle. The chords AC and BD meet at E.
Prove that triangles ABE and DCE are similar.
questions.answer: Angle BAC = angle BDC (same segment), angle ABD = angle ACD (same segment), so AAA similar
ms: B1 for angle BAE = angle CDE with reason: angles in the same segment are equal
B1 for angle ABE = angle DCE with reason: angles in the same segment are equal
B1 for angle AEB = angle DEC (vertically opposite angles are equal), or noting the third angles must be equal
B1 for conclusion: all three angles equal, so the triangles are similar
questions.tip: Similar needs equal angles (or sides in the same ratio). Match each angle carefully to the correct partner.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A wedge has a horizontal rectangular base ABCD with AB = 12 cm and BC = 5 cm. The points E and F are vertically above D and C respectively, with DE = CF = 4 cm. The sloping face ABFE is a rectangle.
Work out the angle between AF and the base ABCD. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
ms: M1 for recognising the angle is FAC in the right-angled triangle ACF
questions.tip: The projection of AF on the base is AC, because F is directly above C.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A frustum is made by cutting a solid cone with base radius 9 cm and height 12 cm, parallel to its base. The small cone removed has height 4 cm.
Work out the volume of the frustum. Give your answer in terms of π.
ms: M1 for radius of small cone = 9 × 4/12 = 3 cm (similar triangles)
M1 for large cone volume ⅓π × 81 × 12 = 324π
M1 for small cone volume ⅓π × 9 × 4 = 12π
questions.tip: Find the small cone's radius using similar triangles. Don't assume it's a third of the height without checking.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two statues are mathematically similar. The small statue is 20 cm tall and the large statue is 50 cm tall.
(a) The small statue needs 0.4 litres of paint to cover it. How much paint is needed for the large statue?
(b) The small statue has mass 1.2 kg. Both statues are made of the same material. Work out the mass of the large statue.
questions.tip: Paint covers surface area (square the factor). Mass depends on volume (cube the factor).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The kinetic energy, E joules, of an object is directly proportional to the square of its speed, v m/s.
When v = 8, E = 192.
(a) Find a formula for E in terms of v.
(b) The speed increases from 8 m/s to 10 m/s. Work out the percentage increase in E.
ms: M1 for E at v = 10 is 300, or using (10/8)² = 1.5625
questions.tip: Percentage increase = (new − old) ÷ old × 100. The 25% increase in speed is not the answer.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The incomplete table and histogram give information about the lengths, L cm, of some leaves.
Length (L cm) | Frequency
0 < L ≤ 20 | 16
20 < L ≤ 30 | ?
30 < L ≤ 60 | 24
On the histogram, the bar for 20 < L ≤ 30 has frequency density 2.8.
(a) Work out the missing frequency.
(b) Work out the frequency densities of the other two bars.
(c) Work out an estimate for the mean length. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for midpoints 10, 25, 45 multiplied by frequencies
questions.tip: Two bars with the same height can still have different frequencies, because their widths differ.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Maya goes to school by bus or by bike. The probability she takes the bus is 0.6.
If she takes the bus, the probability she is late is 0.25. If she cycles, the probability she is late is 0.1.
One day Maya is late. Work out the probability that she took the bus.
questions.tip: 'Given she is late' means you divide by P(late), found from both branches.

questions.q:
[Calculator] At the end of year 1, a machine is worth £16 000. At the end of year 3, it is worth £12 960.
The value decreases by the same percentage each year.
(a) Work out the percentage decrease each year.
(b) Work out the value of the machine at the end of year 6.
questions.tip: There are TWO years between year 1 and year 3, so square root the overall multiplier.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cumulative frequency graph for the masses of 200 parcels passes through these points (joined by straight lines):
(0, 0), (2, 30), (4, 90), (6, 150), (8, 185), (10, 200), where the x-value is mass in kg.
Parcels over 7 kg cost extra to post.
Show that about 16% of the parcels cost extra.
ms: M1 for reading the cumulative frequency at 7 kg (167.5, accept 165 to 170)
questions.tip: Read UP at 7 kg, then subtract from the total for 'over 7 kg'.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Triangle ABC has AB = 8 cm, AC = 10 cm and area 30 cm². Angle BAC is obtuse.
(a) Work out the size of angle BAC. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
(b) Work out the length of BC. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for ½ × 8 × 10 × sin A = 30, so sin A = 0.75
M1 for recognising the obtuse angle: 180 − 48.6
questions.tip: sin⁻¹ only gives the acute angle. If the angle is obtuse, take it away from 180°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Tia rolls a fair six-sided dice until she gets a 6.
(a) Work out the probability that she gets her first 6 on the third roll.
(b) Work out the probability that she needs more than three rolls.
questions.tip: 'More than three rolls' means no 6 in the first three rolls.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A solid cube has mass 95 g, correct to the nearest gram. Each edge of the cube is 4.6 cm, correct to 1 decimal place.
Work out the lower bound for the density of the cube. Give your answer to 3 decimal places.
You must show all your working.
ms: M1 for 94.5 ÷ 4.65³ (lower bound mass ÷ upper bound volume)
questions.tip: Lower bound of a division = lower bound on top ÷ UPPER bound on the bottom. Cube the upper bound of the edge.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A solid metal cylinder has radius 4 cm and height 9 cm.
The cylinder is melted down and all the metal is used to make a solid cone with base radius 6 cm.
Work out the total surface area of the cone. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: M1 for total surface area = π × 6² + π × 6 × √180
questions.tip: Total surface area of a cone includes the circular base as well as the curved surface πrl.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Work out 2/3 ÷ 4/9
questions.tip: Flip the SECOND fraction only, then multiply. 8/27 comes from multiplying without flipping.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Write these numbers in order of size. Start with the smallest.
0.45    4/9    44%
ms: M1 converts all three to the same form, e.g. 0.45, 0.444..., 0.44
questions.tip: 4/9 = 0.444... sits between 0.44 and 0.45. Write at least 3 decimal places before comparing.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Work out 4 1/5 ÷ 1 3/4
Give your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.
ms: M1 converts to improper fractions 21/5 and 7/4
A1 2 2/5 (do not accept 12/5 as the final answer)
questions.tip: Never divide the whole numbers and the fractions separately. Convert to improper fractions first.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 0.0375 as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.tip: Count decimal places: 4 places means over 10000, then cancel fully.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The number of members of a gym increased from 240 to 324.
Work out the percentage increase.
questions.tip: Divide the change by the ORIGINAL amount (240), not the new amount.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A tank is 2/5 full of water. 21 litres of water are added. The tank is now 3/4 full.
(a) Work out the capacity of the tank. (3)
(b) How many more litres are needed to fill the tank? (1)
ms: M1 21 ÷ 7/20 (or 7/20 of the tank = 21 litres, so 1/20 = 3 litres)
questions.tip: 21 litres is the DIFFERENCE between the two fractions, so subtract the fractions first.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Sam spends 1/4 of his money on rent. He spends 2/5 of the remaining money on food. He saves the rest. He saves £540.
Work out how much money Sam had to start with.
ms: M1 remaining after rent is 3/4; food is 2/5 × 3/4 = 3/10
questions.tip: The 2/5 is of the REMAINING money, not of the total. Writing 1 − 1/4 − 2/5 loses the marks.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] x is 20% more than y.
y is 25% less than z.
Show that x is 10% less than z.
questions.answer: x = 1.2y and y = 0.75z, so x = 1.2 × 0.75z = 0.9z, which is 10% less than z
ms: A1 x = 0.9z and conclusion that this is 10% less than z
questions.tip: Use multipliers. Adding +20% and −25% to get −5% is the classic wrong answer.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A shop buys a sofa for £640. It sells the sofa at a profit of 35%.
In a sale, the selling price of the sofa is reduced by 12.5%.
Work out the percentage profit the shop makes on the original £640 if the sofa is sold in the sale.
questions.tip: 35% − 12.5% = 22.5% is wrong: the 12.5% is taken off the selling price, not the cost.

questions.q: [Calculator] Write £2.85 as a percentage of £38.
questions.tip: Part ÷ whole × 100. 13.3% comes from dividing 38 by 2.85 the wrong way round.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A car loses 10% of its value each year. It is worth £8000 now.
What will it be worth in 2 years' time?
questions.tip: £6400 is taking 20% off once. Each year's 10% is of the NEW value.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] £4000 is invested for 2 years at 5% per year compound interest.
Work out the total interest earned.
questions.tip: The question asks for the INTEREST, so subtract the £4000 at the end.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Kerry has £1000 to invest for 2 years.
Account A pays 6% per year simple interest.
Account B pays 5% per year compound interest.
Which account gives more money after 2 years, and by how much?
questions.tip: Simple interest is the same amount every year; compound interest is worked out on the new total.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] An amount of money is invested at 10% per year compound interest.
Work out the least number of whole years it takes for the investment to be worth more than 1.5 times the amount invested.
questions.tip: Show both the year just below 1.5 and the first year above it. The amount itself does not matter.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] £800 is invested at 5% per year simple interest for 3 years.
How much interest is earned?
questions.tip: £126.10 is compound interest. Read whether it is simple or compound.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The number of birds in a colony increases by 20% each year.
(a) Show that after 2 years the number of birds has increased by 44%. (2)
(b) Ravi says, 'After 3 years the number will have increased by 60%.'
Explain why Ravi is wrong. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 1.2 × 1.2 = 1.44, a 44% increase (b) 1.2³ = 1.728, so the increase is 72.8%, not 60%
ms: B1 the increase is compound (each 20% is of a larger amount), 1.2³ = 1.728 so 72.8%
questions.tip: Percentages compound: never add 20% three times.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The value of a painting increased by 10% in one year. In the next year the value decreased by 10%.
The painting is now worth £4950.
Work out the value of the painting at the start.
questions.tip: +10% then −10% is NOT back to the start. The overall multiplier is 0.99.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A ball is dropped from a height of 2.5 m. After each bounce it rises to 80% of the height it fell from.
After which bounce is the height of the ball first less than 1 m?
You must show your working.
ms: A1 0.8192 m after the 5th bounce, so the 5th bounce
questions.tip: The 4th bounce gives 1.024 m, which is still above 1 m. Check every value carefully.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Mia invests £3000 at 0.4% per month compound interest.
Work out the interest she earns in 2 years. Give your answer to the nearest penny.
questions.tip: The rate is per MONTH, so the power is 24, not 2.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A laptop is bought for £1250. Its value falls by 30% in the first year. In each year after that, its value falls by 12%.
Work out the value of the laptop after 4 years. Give your answer to the nearest penny.
questions.tip: After the first year there are only 3 more years, so the power on 0.88 is 3.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which of these numbers is written in standard form?
ms: Standard form is A × 10ⁿ with 1 ≤ A < 10. Only 3.07 × 10⁻⁶ fits.
questions.tip: The front number must be at least 1 and less than 10, and the base must be 10.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (a) Write 5.06 × 10⁵ as an ordinary number. (1)
(b) Write 48 000 000 in standard form. (1)
questions.tip: Count the jumps: 48 000 000 needs the decimal point to move 7 places.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Work out (4 × 10⁻³)²
Give your answer in standard form.
questions.tip: 16 × 10⁻⁶ is not standard form. Making 16 into 1.6 makes the power go UP by 1.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Work out 6.3 × 10⁻⁴ − 5 × 10⁻⁵
Give your answer in standard form.
ms: M1 writes both with the same power or as ordinary numbers, e.g. 0.00063 − 0.00005
questions.tip: You cannot subtract the front numbers until the powers of 10 match.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Work out (2.4 × 10⁶) ÷ (8 × 10⁻²)
Give your answer in standard form.
questions.tip: Subtracting a negative power: 6 − (−2) = 8. Then adjust 0.3 to 3, which lowers the power by 1.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Write these numbers in order of size. Start with the smallest.
3.2 × 10⁻³    0.00031    32 × 10⁻⁵    3.02 × 10⁻⁴
ms: M1 converts at least three to a common form, e.g. 0.0032, 0.00031, 0.00032, 0.000302
questions.tip: 32 × 10⁻⁵ is not in standard form: it equals 3.2 × 10⁻⁴. Convert before comparing.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The mass of one bacterium is 2.5 × 10⁻¹² grams.
Work out the number of bacteria in a total mass of 1 kg.
Give your answer in standard form.
questions.tip: Change kg to grams first. Leaving it as 1 ÷ (2.5 × 10⁻¹²) is out by a factor of 1000.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Work out √(1.6 × 10⁹)
Give your answer in standard form.
ms: M1 rewrites as 16 × 10⁸ (so the power is even)
questions.tip: √1.6 is not exact. Make the power of 10 even first: 1.6 × 10⁹ = 16 × 10⁸.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Show that (5 × 10⁶ + 7 × 10⁵) ÷ (3 × 10⁻²) = 1.9 × 10⁸
ms: A1 fully correct working leading to 1.9 × 10⁸
questions.tip: In a 'show that', every step must be written. Do the addition in the bracket first.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A grain of sand has a volume of 6.2 × 10⁻² mm³.
A beach contains 3.5 × 10⁹ m³ of sand.
1 m³ = 10⁹ mm³
Estimate the number of grains of sand on the beach. Give your answer in standard form correct to 2 significant figures.
questions.tip: Units must match before dividing. Forgetting the 10⁹ conversion gives 5.6 × 10¹⁰.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Work out the value of 64^(1/3)
ms: A power of 1/3 means cube root: ∛64 = 4
questions.tip: Power 1/2 is square root, power 1/3 is cube root. It does not mean divide by 3.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (a) Write down the value of 7⁰ (1)
(b) Work out the value of 2⁻³ (1)
questions.tip: A negative power gives a reciprocal, not a negative number. 2⁻³ is not −8.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Work out the value of (4/9)^(−1/2)
ms: Negative power: flip to (9/4)^(1/2), then square root = 3/2
questions.tip: Deal with the minus sign by flipping the fraction, then do the root.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Simplify fully (2a³b⁻¹)⁴
ms: B1 two of 16, a¹², b⁻⁴ correct
questions.tip: The power of 4 applies to the 2 as well: 2⁴ = 16, not 8.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Work out the value of
(a) 32^(3/5) (1)
(b) (32/243)^(−2/5) (2)
ms: M1 (b) fifth root of 32/243 is 2/3, or flips to (243/32)^(2/5)
questions.tip: Root first (the denominator of the power), then the power. It keeps the numbers small.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Simplify fully (27x⁶)^(2/3)
questions.tip: 27^(2/3) = (∛27)² = 9. Multiply the power on x: 6 × 2/3 = 4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] a and b are numbers such that
3^a × 9^b = 3⁷
2^a ÷ 4^b = 1/8
Work out the values of a and b.
ms: M1 correct method to solve the simultaneous equations
questions.tip: Write everything with the same base first, then compare powers. 1/8 = 2⁻³.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Work out the exact value of (0.125)^(−2/3) × 9^(1/2)
questions.tip: Change the decimal to a fraction. 0.125 = 1/8 is a must-know.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve x^(−3/2) = 1/27
questions.tip: Flip both sides to get rid of the negative, then raise to the power 2/3.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Write these numbers in order of size. Start with the smallest.
16^(1/2)    8^(−1/3)    27^(2/3)    (1/2)^(−3)
ms: M1 at least three correctly evaluated from 4, 1/2, 9, 8
questions.tip: Evaluate each one first. (1/2)^(−3) flips to 2³ = 8.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Simplify √50
questions.tip: Look for the largest square factor (25), not just any factor.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Simplify
(a) √3 × √12 (1)
(b) √20 ÷ √5 (1)
questions.tip: √a × √b = √(ab): √36 = 6. Do not leave it as √36.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Expand and simplify (3 + √2)(4 − √2)
ms: M1 three of the four terms correct: 12, −3√2, 4√2, −2
questions.tip: √2 × √2 = 2, and it is −2 here because of the minus sign.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Rationalise the denominator of 10/√5
questions.tip: Multiply top AND bottom by √5, then simplify the 10/5.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Show that √180 − √20 can be written in the form k√5, where k is an integer. State the value of k.
questions.tip: √180 − √20 is not √160. You can only subtract surds once they are like terms.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A square has an area of 72 cm².
Work out the perimeter of the square. Give your answer in the form a√2.
questions.tip: Simplify √72 before multiplying by 4, otherwise you get 4√72, which is not in the form asked.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] a and b are positive integers with a > b.
(√a + √b)² = 20 + 8√6
Work out the values of a and b.
ms: M1 a + b = 20 and 2√(ab) = 8√6 so ab = 96
M1 solves, e.g. t² − 20t + 96 = 0 or tries pairs adding to 20
questions.tip: Match the whole-number parts and the surd parts separately. 8√6 = 2√96.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A right-angled triangle has shorter sides of length (2 + √3) cm and (2 − √3) cm.
(a) Work out the area of the triangle. (2)
(b) Work out the exact length of the hypotenuse. (2)
questions.tip: (2 + √3)² is 7 + 4√3, not 4 + 3. Expand double brackets properly.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 2/(√7 − √5) − √7 in the form √n, where n is an integer.
ms: M1 multiplies top and bottom by (√7 + √5)
questions.tip: The conjugate of √7 − √5 is √7 + √5. Multiplying by √7 − √5 again does not rationalise.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve x√3 + 5 = 2x + √3
Give your answer in the form a + b√3, where a and b are integers.
ms: M1 x = (√3 − 5)/(√3 − 2) and multiplies top and bottom by (√3 + 2)
questions.tip: The denominator 3 − 4 = −1, so every sign flips. Watch the negatives.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] m = 250, correct to the nearest 10.
Which is the error interval for m?
questions.tip: Halve the unit you rounded to. The lower bound uses ≤ and the upper bound uses <.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] w = 0.36, correct to 2 significant figures.
Write down the error interval for w.
ms: B1 0.355 seen as the lower bound
questions.tip: 2 s.f. here means to the nearest 0.01, so add and subtract 0.005.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] a = 8, correct to the nearest integer.
b = 3, correct to the nearest integer.
Work out the upper bound of a − b.
questions.tip: To make a difference as big as possible, use the UPPER bound of a and the LOWER bound of b.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The side of a square is 6 cm, correct to the nearest cm.
What is the lower bound of the area of the square?
questions.tip: Find the bound of the length first, then square it. Do not round 36.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A rectangle has length 7 cm and width 4 cm, both correct to the nearest cm.
Work out the upper bound for the perimeter of the rectangle.
questions.tip: Use the upper bound for every side when you want the upper bound of a total.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 2400 people went to a concert, correct to the nearest 100.
Each person paid exactly £5.
Work out the lower bound for the total amount of money paid.
questions.tip: The £5 is exact, so only the number of people has bounds.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] p = 4.6 correct to 1 decimal place.
q = 2.3 correct to 1 decimal place.
(a) Work out the lower bound and the upper bound of pq. (2)
(b) Write down the value of pq to a suitable degree of accuracy. Give a reason for your answer. (2)
questions.answer: (a) LB 10.2375, UB 10.9275 (b) 10, because both bounds round to 10 to 1 significant figure
ms: M1 rounds both bounds to the same degree of accuracy
A1 10 with reason: both bounds round to 10 to 1 s.f. (but they differ to 2 s.f., 10 and 11)
questions.tip: A suitable degree of accuracy is one where the upper and lower bounds agree when rounded.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] When x is truncated to 1 decimal place, the result is 7.4
When x is rounded to 1 decimal place, the result is 7.5
Write down the error interval for x.
questions.tip: x must satisfy BOTH intervals, so take the overlap.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A cylinder has radius 4.2 cm, correct to 1 decimal place, and height 10 cm, correct to the nearest cm.
Work out the lower bound for the volume of the cylinder. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
questions.tip: Use the lower bound for both the radius and the height.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag can hold a maximum mass of 15 kg, correct to the nearest kg.
Each book has a mass of 1.2 kg, correct to 1 decimal place.
Work out the greatest number of books that can definitely be put in the bag without going over the maximum mass.
questions.tip: 'Definitely' means the worst case: smallest possible limit and heaviest possible books.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 0.777... (0.7 recurring) as a fraction.
questions.tip: One digit recurring goes over 9; two digits recurring go over 99.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 5/11 as a recurring decimal.
ms: A1 0.454545... with dots over the 4 and the 5
questions.tip: Show which digits recur. Writing 0.45 alone is wrong.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove algebraically that 0.727272... (0.72 recurring) = 8/11
questions.tip: 'Prove algebraically' needs x, 100x and the subtraction written out.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 0.060606... (0.06 recurring) as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.tip: Here both the 0 and the 6 recur. 1/15 is 0.0666..., where only the 6 recurs.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 0.58333... (0.583 with the 3 recurring) as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.tip: Only the 3 recurs, so subtract 100x from 1000x.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 2.151515... (2.15 with the 15 recurring) as a mixed number in its simplest form.
questions.tip: Deal with the whole number separately, then simplify 15/99 to 5/33.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove algebraically that 0.405405... (0.405 recurring) = 15/37
questions.tip: Three digits recur, so multiply by 1000.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Work out 0.8333... ÷ 0.444...
(0.83 with the 3 recurring, divided by 0.4 recurring)
Give your answer as a fraction in its simplest form.
questions.tip: Convert both to fractions first. Dividing the decimals directly cannot give an exact answer.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove algebraically that 0.0454545... (0.045 with the 45 recurring) = 1/22
questions.tip: Line up the recurring parts: 10x and 1000x both end in .4545...

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] a and b are digits.
(a) Prove that the recurring decimal 0.ababab... = (10a + b)/99 (2)
(b) Hence write 0.636363... as a fraction in its simplest form. (1)
ms: M1 x = 0.abab..., 100x = ab.abab... (the two-digit number 10a + b followed by the recurring part)
questions.tip: The two-digit number with digits a and b is 10a + b, not ab.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which of these is 120 written as a product of its prime factors?
questions.tip: Every factor must be prime. 15, 10 and 4 are not prime.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 588 as a product of its prime factors. Give your answer in index form.
ms: M1 a correct factor tree or division method with at least two correct primes
questions.tip: Check by multiplying back: 4 × 3 × 49 = 588.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find (a) the highest common factor (HCF) and (b) the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 48 and 180.
ms: M1 48 = 2⁴ × 3 and 180 = 2² × 3² × 5 (or a Venn diagram of prime factors)
questions.tip: HCF uses the LOWEST power of each shared prime; LCM uses the HIGHEST power of every prime.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A = 2⁴ × 3² × 7 and B = 2² × 3³ × 5
What is the HCF of A and B?
questions.tip: 5 and 7 are not in both numbers, so they are not in the HCF.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A florist has 84 roses and 126 tulips. She makes identical bunches using all the flowers. Each bunch has the same number of roses and the same number of tulips.
Work out the greatest number of bunches she can make, and the number of roses and tulips in each bunch.
questions.answer: 42 bunches, each with 2 roses and 3 tulips
ms: M1 finds HCF of 84 and 126 using prime factors or listing factors
A1 2 roses and 3 tulips in each bunch
questions.tip: 'Greatest number of identical groups' is an HCF question, not LCM.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find the smallest positive integer n such that 180n is a square number.
questions.tip: A square number has every prime to an EVEN power. Only the 5 has an odd power.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The LCM of 2^a × 3² × 5 and 2³ × 3^b × 7 is 2⁵ × 3⁴ × 5 × 7
(a) Write down the values of a and b. (2)
(b) Find the HCF of the two numbers. (1)
questions.tip: The LCM takes the highest power, so the 2⁵ must come from 2^a and the 3⁴ from 3^b.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] N = 2³⁰ × 5²⁸
How many digits does N have when it is written out in full?
You must show your working.
questions.tip: Pair each 2 with a 5 to make 10s. 10²⁸ has 29 digits, and 4 × 10²⁸ also has 29.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] a = 2³ × 3 × 7 and b = 2 × 3² × 7²
(a) Write ab as a product of prime factors in index form. (1)
(b) Explain why ab is not a square number. (1)
(c) Find the smallest positive integer k such that kab is a square number. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 2⁴ × 3³ × 7³ (b) the powers of 3 and 7 are odd (c) 21
ms: B1 a square number has all prime powers even, but 3³ and 7³ are odd powers
questions.tip: To multiply numbers in index form, ADD the powers of each prime.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] There are 604 800 seconds in a week.
(a) Show that 604 800 = 2⁷ × 3³ × 5² × 7 (2)
(b) Find the smallest positive integer k such that 604 800k is a square number. (1)
ms: M1 a method using prime factors, e.g. 7 × 24 × 3600 with 24 = 2³ × 3 and 3600 = 2⁴ × 3² × 5²
questions.tip: Make each odd power even: 2⁷ needs one more 2, 3³ one more 3, 7 one more 7.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A shirt comes in 5 colours and 3 sizes.
How many different choices of colour and size are there?
questions.tip: Multiply the number of options, do not add them.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] How many different ways can the letters of the word MATHS be arranged in a row?
questions.tip: Each time a letter is used there is one fewer choice for the next place.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] How many odd 3-digit numbers are there? (3-digit numbers go from 100 to 999.)
questions.tip: The first digit cannot be 0 (9 choices) and the last digit must be 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A password is 2 letters followed by 2 digits. The letters are from A to Z and must be different. The digits are from 0 to 9 and can repeat.
How many different passwords are possible?
questions.tip: Read the rule for each part: letters cannot repeat (26 then 25), digits can (10 then 10).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] There are 12 players in a squad.
(a) A captain and a vice-captain are chosen. Work out how many different ways this can be done. (1)
(b) Instead, two players are chosen to go to a meeting. Work out how many different pairs of players are possible. (2)
questions.tip: In (b) order does not matter (Ali and Ben is the same pair as Ben and Ali), so divide by 2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A lock has 3 dials, each showing a digit from 0 to 9.
Kim forgets the code. She knows that the first digit is even and the last digit is greater than 6.
How many different codes could it be?
questions.tip: 0 is even, so there are 5 even digits: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8. Greater than 6 means 7, 8, 9.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Three-digit numbers are made using the digits 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. No digit can be used more than once.
How many of these three-digit numbers are multiples of 5?
ms: M1 ending in 5: 4 × 4 = 16 (first digit cannot be 0 or 5)
questions.tip: Split into cases: ending in 0 and ending in 5. The first digit can never be 0.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Each person in a group shakes hands with every other person exactly once. There are 45 handshakes altogether.
Work out how many people are in the group.
questions.tip: Each handshake involves two people, so n(n − 1) counts every handshake twice.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Sam has 4 different maths books and 3 different science books. He puts all 7 books in a row on a shelf.
(a) How many arrangements have all 4 maths books on the left and all 3 science books on the right? (2)
(b) How many arrangements have the 4 maths books next to each other (anywhere on the shelf)? (2)
ms: M1 treats maths books as one block: 4 units arranged 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 ways, × 24 for inside the block
questions.tip: In (b) the block itself can move: the block plus 3 science books makes 4 items to arrange.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] An ice cream shop has x flavours and 3 toppings. A customer chooses 2 different flavours (the order does not matter) and 1 topping. There are 63 possible choices.
Work out the value of x.
questions.tip: Choosing 2 flavours where order does not matter is x(x − 1)/2, not x².

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 1.2 kg : 400 g as a ratio in its simplest form.
questions.tip: Change to the same units first. 12 : 4 is correct but not simplest.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (a) Write the ratio 12 : 30 in the form 1 : n (1)
(b) Write the ratio 15 : 4 in the form n : 1 (1)
questions.tip: Divide BOTH sides by the number you want to become 1. n does not have to be a whole number.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The angles in a triangle are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 7.
Show that the triangle is obtuse-angled.
questions.answer: 12 parts = 180°, 1 part = 15°, largest angle 7 × 15 = 105° which is more than 90°
questions.tip: Angles in a triangle add to 180°. Finish a 'show that' with a statement.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The ratio of red counters to blue counters in a bag is 4 : 7.
What fraction of the counters are blue?
questions.tip: The denominator is the TOTAL number of parts (4 + 7), not the other part.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] a : b = 3 : 4
Work out (2a + b) : (a + 3b). Give your answer in its simplest form.
ms: M1 uses a = 3k, b = 4k (or a = 3, b = 4) to get 10 : 15
questions.tip: Let a = 3k and b = 4k, then substitute. The k cancels at the end.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The ratio of students in a year group who walk to school to those who do not walk is 3 : 5.
1/3 of the students who do not walk cycle to school.
What fraction of all the students in the year group cycle to school?
ms: M1 fraction who do not walk = 5/8
questions.tip: The 1/3 is of the non-walkers only, so multiply by 5/8 first.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains red, blue and green counters only.
red : blue = 2 : 3
blue : green = 6 : 5
There are 36 more green counters than red counters.
Work out the total number of counters in the bag.
ms: M1 makes blue the same in both ratios: red : blue = 4 : 6
questions.tip: Blue appears in both ratios, so scale them until the blue parts match.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Drink A is made from juice and water in the ratio 1 : 4.
Drink B is made from juice and water in the ratio 2 : 3.
300 ml of drink A is mixed with 200 ml of drink B.
Work out the ratio of juice to water in the mixture. Give your answer in its simplest form.
ms: M1 drink A: juice 60 ml and water 240 ml
M1 drink B: juice 80 ml and water 120 ml
questions.tip: You cannot add the ratios (1 : 4 + 2 : 3). Work out the actual amounts of juice and water.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 3/4 of the money Ali has is equal to 2/3 of the money Bea has.
Work out the ratio of Ali's money to Bea's money. Give your answer in its simplest form.
questions.tip: Write an equation first. 3 : 4 or 2 : 3 are not the answer.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Concrete is made by mixing cement, sand and gravel in the ratio 1 : 2 : 4 by mass.
A builder needs 1.4 tonnes of concrete. 1 tonne = 1000 kg.
Cement is sold in 25 kg bags costing £5.85 each.
Sand costs £38 per tonne.
Gravel costs £32 per tonne.
Work out the total cost of the materials. The builder can only buy whole bags of cement.
questions.tip: Keep units consistent: sand and gravel are priced per TONNE, so use 0.4 t and 0.8 t.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which of these tables shows y directly proportional to x?
ms: y ÷ x is always 5, so y = 5x
questions.tip: Direct proportion needs y ÷ x to be constant. 4, 6, 8 goes up evenly but 4 ÷ 1 ≠ 6 ÷ 2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 5 litres of paint cover 40 m².
How many litres of the same paint are needed to cover 72 m²?
questions.tip: Find what one unit does first (unitary method).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The exchange rate is £1 = $1.25
(a) Change £240 into dollars. (1)
(b) Change $350 into pounds. (2)
questions.tip: Going from dollars to pounds you DIVIDE by the rate. Check: you should get fewer pounds than dollars.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y is inversely proportional to x².
x is doubled.
What happens to y?
ms: y = k/x². Doubling x multiplies x² by 4, so y is divided by 4.
questions.tip: Square the scale factor and then take the reciprocal because it is inverse.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] t is inversely proportional to s.
Complete the table.
s | 2 | 5 | ?
t | 30 | ? | 4
questions.answer: When s = 5, t = 12; when t = 4, s = 15
questions.tip: For inverse proportion s × t is constant. Check: 5 × 12 = 60 and 15 × 4 = 60.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A car uses 6.4 litres of fuel for every 100 km.
Fuel costs 148.9p per litre.
Work out the cost of the fuel for a journey of 365 km. Give your answer to the nearest penny.
questions.tip: Give money in pounds to 2 d.p. Leaving the answer as 3478.3 is wrong units.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y is directly proportional to the square of x.
When x = a, y = 18.
When x = a + 2, y = 50.
Given that a > 0, work out the value of a.
questions.tip: Divide the two equations to cancel k. Then square root both sides.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] p is inversely proportional to the square of q.
When q = 4, p = 0.5
Work out the positive value of q for which p = q.
questions.tip: Find k first, then set p equal to q in your formula.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Pump A on its own empties a full tank in 9 hours.
Pump B on its own empties the same full tank in 6 hours.
Both pumps start emptying the full tank at the same time and work at their usual rates.
Work out how long it takes to empty the tank. Give your answer in hours and minutes.
ms: M1 rates 1/9 and 1/6 of the tank per hour (or in 18 hours A empties 2 tanks and B empties 3 tanks)
M1 1/9 + 1/6 = 5/18 of the tank per hour (or 5 tanks in 18 hours)
questions.tip: Add the RATES (fractions of the tank per hour), not the times. 9 + 6 = 15 or (9 + 6) ÷ 2 = 7.5 hours are wrong because two pumps must be quicker than either one alone.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y is directly proportional to √x.
x is increased by 69%.
Show that y increases by 30%.
questions.answer: y = k√x; new x = 1.69x so new y = k√(1.69x) = 1.3k√x, a 30% increase
ms: M1 y = k√x and new x = 1.69x
A1 √1.69 = 1.3 so y is multiplied by 1.3, a 30% increase
questions.tip: Use the multiplier 1.69, then take the square root of the multiplier (13² = 169). Do not halve 69%.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A block has a mass of 600 g and a volume of 75 cm³.
What is its density?
questions.tip: Density is mass ÷ volume. 0.125 comes from dividing the wrong way round.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cyclist rides at an average speed of 18 km/h for 1 hour 40 minutes.
Work out the distance she travels.
questions.tip: 40 minutes is 2/3 of an hour, not 0.4 hours.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cheetah can run at 30 m/s.
A car is travelling at 100 km/h.
Which is faster? You must show your working.
questions.answer: Cheetah: 30 m/s = 108 km/h, which is more than 100 km/h
ms: A1 the cheetah is faster, with correct comparison
questions.tip: Convert to the same units before comparing, and state which is faster.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Water flows into a pond at 3 litres per second.
1 m³ = 1000 litres.
How many cubic metres of water flow into the pond in 10 minutes?
questions.tip: 10 minutes is 600 seconds. Then divide litres by 1000.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Kai runs 400 m in 80 seconds. He then runs a further 600 m in 170 seconds.
Work out his average speed for the whole 1000 m, in metres per second.
questions.tip: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Do not average the two speeds.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A box has a weight of 120 N. It rests on a face measuring 40 cm by 30 cm.
(a) Work out the pressure on the floor in N/m². (3)
(b) The box is turned so it rests on a face measuring 30 cm by 20 cm. Work out the increase in pressure. (1)
ms: B1 new pressure 120 ÷ 0.06 = 2000 N/m², increase 1000 N/m²
questions.tip: Change cm to m BEFORE finding the area. 1200 cm² is 0.12 m², not 12 m².

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Liquid A has density 0.9 g/cm³. Liquid B has density 1.3 g/cm³.
400 cm³ of liquid A is mixed with V cm³ of liquid B.
The mixture has density 1.05 g/cm³.
Work out the value of V.
questions.tip: Densities do not add. Use total mass ÷ total volume.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A force acts on an area A and produces a pressure P.
The same force acts on an area that is 20% smaller.
Work out the percentage increase in the pressure.
questions.tip: Pressure is inversely proportional to area. 20% smaller area does not give 20% more pressure.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Town X and town Y are 300 km apart.
A train leaves X at 09:00 and travels towards Y at a constant 80 km/h.
A second train leaves Y at 09:30 and travels towards X at a constant 120 km/h.
At what time do the trains pass each other?
ms: M1 by 09:30 the first train has travelled 40 km, so 260 km apart
questions.tip: 1.3 hours is 1 hour 18 minutes, not 1 hour 30 minutes.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Gold has a density of 19.3 g/cm³.
A gold bar is a cuboid measuring 18 cm by 5 cm by 3.5 cm.
Gold costs £62.40 per gram.
Work out the value of the gold bar.
questions.tip: Mass = density × volume. Do not divide.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A value is multiplied by 0.92 each year.
Which statement describes this?
ms: 0.92 = 1 − 0.08, so it decreases by 8% each year
questions.tip: A multiplier less than 1 means decrease. Subtract from 1 to get the percentage.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The population of a village is 3000. It increases by 10% each year.
Work out the population after 3 years.
questions.tip: Each year's 10% is of the NEW population. 3900 is simple growth, which is wrong.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The value, £V, of a machine t years after it is bought is given by V = 4000 × 0.9^t
(a) Write down the value of the machine when it is bought. (1)
(b) Work out the value after 2 years. (1)
(c) Write down the percentage the value decreases by each year. (1)
questions.tip: When t = 0, 0.9⁰ = 1, so the starting value is the number in front.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 640 g of a radioactive substance halves in mass every 3 days.
What mass is left after 12 days?
questions.tip: Count the halvings (12 ÷ 3 = 4). Do not divide 640 by 12.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A car is worth £12 000. Its value falls by 25% in the first year and by 20% in the second year.
Show that the car loses 40% of its value over the two years.
questions.answer: 0.75 × 0.8 = 0.6, so the car is worth 60% (£7200), a 40% loss
questions.tip: 25% + 20% = 45% is wrong. The 20% is of the reduced value.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A colony starts with 300 bacteria. The number doubles every 20 minutes.
How many bacteria are there after 2 hours?
questions.tip: Count how many 20-minute periods are in 2 hours (6), not 2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A price is decreased by x%. The new price is then increased by x%.
The final price is 4% lower than the original price.
Work out the value of x.
questions.tip: Use multipliers and expand: it is a difference of two squares.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] £P is invested for 2 years at 10% per year.
With compound interest it earns £21 more than it would with simple interest.
Work out the value of P.
questions.tip: Simple interest for 2 years at 10% is 20%; compound is 21%.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The population of bats in a cave was 2000 at the start of 2024 and 2662 at the start of 2027.
The population increased by the same percentage each year.
Work out (a) the percentage increase each year (2) and (b) the population at the start of 2025 (1).
questions.tip: 2024 to 2027 is THREE years, so 1.331 is a three-year multiplier. Take the cube root (11³ = 1331), not the square root, and do not divide 33.1% by 3.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A boat loses 12% of its value each year.
(a) Show that after 5 years it has lost about 47% of its value. (2)
(b) After how many whole years will it first have lost more than 60% of its value? (2)
questions.tip: Losing more than 60% means the value is LESS than 40%, so compare with 0.4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A fair six-sided dice is rolled.
What is the probability that it lands on a prime number?
questions.tip: 1 is NOT a prime number. 2 is prime.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 4 red, 7 green and 9 white counters only. A counter is taken at random.
(a) Work out the probability that it is red. (1)
(b) Work out the probability that it is not green. (1)
questions.tip: Count the total first (20). 'Not green' = 1 − P(green).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Spinner A has three equal sections numbered 1, 2 and 3.
Spinner B has four equal sections numbered 1, 2, 3 and 4.
Both spinners are spun and the two scores are multiplied.
Work out the probability that the product is an even number.
ms: M1 a sample space of 12 outcomes (e.g. a grid of products)
questions.tip: A product is even if EITHER number is even. Use a grid so you do not miss any.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A spinner has three sections A, B and C.
P(A) = 2 × P(B) and P(C) = 3 × P(B).
What is P(B)?
questions.tip: All the probabilities must add to 1. Write them in terms of P(B).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Kim spins a spinner 40 times. It lands on 5 eight times.
Ben spins the same spinner 160 times. It lands on 5 twenty times.
(a) Whose results give the better estimate of the probability of landing on 5? Give a reason. (1)
(b) Use all the results to work out the best estimate of the probability that the spinner lands on 5. (2)
questions.answer: (a) Ben, because he did more trials (b) 28/200 = 7/50 (0.14)
questions.tip: Combine the totals. Do not average the two relative frequencies (0.2 and 0.125).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The probability that a battery is faulty is 0.04.
A shop sells 150 packs of batteries. Each pack contains 8 batteries.
Work out an estimate for the number of faulty batteries.
questions.tip: Find the total number of batteries first, not the number of packs.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains red, blue and yellow counters only.
The probability of taking a red counter is 0.4
The probability of taking a blue counter is twice the probability of taking a yellow counter.
There are 26 blue counters in the bag.
Work out the total number of counters in the bag.
questions.tip: Blue and yellow share 0.6 in the ratio 2 : 1.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains x red counters and y blue counters only.
The probability of taking a red counter is 1/3.
4 more red counters are added to the bag. The probability of taking a red counter is now 1/2.
Work out the values of x and y.
questions.tip: Adding red counters changes BOTH the top and the bottom of the fraction.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two fair four-sided dice are numbered 1, 2, 3 and 4. Both are rolled and the scores are added.
(a) Work out the probability that the total is a prime number. (2)
(b) The two dice are rolled 80 times. Work out an estimate for the number of times the total is a prime number. (1)
ms: M1 16 outcomes with totals 2, 3, 5 and 7 identified (1 + 2 + 4 + 2 = 9)
questions.tip: List all 16 outcomes. A total of 5 can happen 4 ways.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] P(A) = 0.7 and P(B) = 0.45
Explain why events A and B cannot be mutually exclusive.
questions.answer: If they were mutually exclusive, P(A or B) = 0.7 + 0.45 = 1.15, which is more than 1, which is impossible
ms: A1 states a probability cannot be greater than 1, so A and B must overlap
questions.tip: Mutually exclusive means they cannot both happen, so their probabilities just add.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A fair coin is flipped and a fair six-sided dice is rolled.
What is the probability of getting a head and a 6?
questions.tip: AND means multiply. Adding gives 2/3, which is wrong.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The probability that Ali wins a game is 0.3. He plays 2 games. The results are independent.
Work out the probability that he wins at least one of the games.
questions.tip: 'At least one' is quickest as 1 − P(loses both). 0.3 + 0.3 = 0.6 is wrong because it double counts winning both.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 6 red and 4 yellow counters. A counter is taken at random, its colour is recorded and it is put back. A second counter is then taken.
Work out the probability that the two counters are different colours.
questions.tip: Different colours can happen two ways: red then yellow OR yellow then red.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 2 red and 3 blue balls. Two balls are taken at random without replacement.
What is the probability that both are blue?
questions.tip: Without replacement the second fraction has one fewer blue AND one fewer in total.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In each football match, the probability that a team wins is 0.5, draws is 0.2 and loses is 0.3.
A win scores 3 points, a draw 1 point and a loss 0 points.
The team plays two matches. The results are independent.
Work out the probability that the team scores at least 4 points.
ms: M1 identifies win-win (6 points) and win-draw in either order (4 points)
questions.tip: List the outcomes that give 4 or more points. Win-draw and draw-win are both needed.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A box contains 10 chocolates. 7 are milk and 3 are dark. Lily takes two chocolates at random and eats them.
Work out the probability that at least one of the chocolates is dark.
questions.tip: 'At least one' is quickest as 1 − P(none).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 5 red counters and 3 green counters.
Jo takes a counter at random.
If it is red, she keeps it.
If it is green, she puts it back and also adds another green counter to the bag.
She then takes a second counter at random.
Work out the probability that the second counter is green.
questions.tip: The bag changes differently on each branch: after red there are 7 counters, after green there are 9.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The probabilities that Sara passes her maths, English and science exams are 0.8, 0.7 and 0.6. The results are independent.
Work out the probability that she passes exactly two of the three exams.
questions.tip: Exactly two passed means exactly one failed. There are three ways.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A biased spinner lands on red with probability x. It is spun twice.
The probability that it lands on red both times is 0.36.
Work out the probability that it lands on red exactly once.
questions.tip: Exactly once means red-not red OR not red-red: multiply by 2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 2 red, 4 blue and 6 green counters. Two counters are taken at random without replacement.
Work out the probability that both counters are the same colour.
questions.tip: Same colour means both red OR both blue OR both green. Add the three products.
A' means NOT in A. 1 is not prime, so it is in A'.
∩ means in both; ∪ means in either (or both). Do not list elements twice.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] There are 32 students in a class. 18 have a dog, 12 have a cat and 7 have both.
(a) Work out how many students have neither a dog nor a cat. (2)
(b) A student is chosen at random. Work out the probability that they have exactly one of these pets. (1)
ms: M1 dog only 11 and cat only 5
questions.tip: Put the 7 in the overlap first, then subtract to get the 'only' regions.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which set describes the elements that are in neither A nor B?
ms: Not in A AND not in B is A' ∩ B', which is the same as (A ∪ B)'
questions.tip: A' ∪ B' includes everything except the overlap. That is not the same.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] P(A) = 0.45, P(B) = 0.3 and P(A ∩ B) = 0.1
Work out
(a) P(A ∩ B') (1)
(b) P(A' ∩ B') (2)
questions.tip: Draw the Venn diagram with probabilities: A only = 0.35, B only = 0.2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] There are 40 members in a club.
22 are in set A and 25 are in set B.
Work out (a) the least possible number and (b) the greatest possible number of members in A ∩ B.
ms: B1 (a) 7 (from 22 + 25 − 40, when nobody is in neither)
B1 (b) 22 (when all of A is inside B)
questions.tip: The overlap is smallest when everyone is in at least one set, and largest when the smaller set fits completely inside the bigger one.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 100 people were asked which of France (F), Germany (G) and Italy (I) they have visited.
5 have visited all three.
12 have visited France and Germany.
15 have visited France and Italy.
10 have visited Germany and Italy.
40 have visited France, 35 have visited Germany and 38 have visited Italy.
(a) Work out how many people have visited none of the three countries. (3)
(b) A person is chosen at random. Work out the probability that they have visited exactly one of the countries. (1)
ms: M1 pairs only: 7 (F and G), 10 (F and I), 5 (G and I)
M1 only regions: F only 18, G only 18, I only 18
questions.tip: The 12 who visited France and Germany include the 5 who visited all three. Subtract the 5.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] For two events A and B:
P(A only) = 0.2, P(A ∩ B) = x, P(B only) = 2x, P(neither) = 0.35
(a) Work out the value of x. (2)
(b) Are A and B independent? You must show your working. (2)
questions.tip: For independence compare P(A) × P(B) with P(A ∩ B). They must be equal.
A ∩ B is multiples of 12 (the LCM), not multiples of 24.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 80 people were asked if they like tea or coffee.
45 like tea and 50 like coffee.
The number who like both is twice the number who like neither.
Work out the number of people who like both.
questions.tip: Use one letter for the unknown and write every region in terms of it.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the colour and type of 40 cars.
| Red | Blue
Saloon | 12 | 8
Hatchback | 15 | 5
A blue car is chosen at random. What is the probability that it is a saloon?
ms: There are 8 + 5 = 13 blue cars, 8 are saloons: 8/13
questions.tip: 'Given blue' means the denominator is the number of blue cars only.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] There are 50 people in a room. 22 are men. 9 of the men wear glasses. 30 people in the room do not wear glasses.
(a) Work out how many women wear glasses. (1)
(b) A person who wears glasses is chosen at random. Work out the probability that this person is a woman. (1)
questions.tip: Draw a two-way table. 20 people wear glasses in total.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] P(A) = 0.6
If A happens, the probability that B happens is 0.3
P(B) = 0.38
(a) If A does not happen, work out the probability that B happens. (2)
(b) Given that B happens, work out the probability that A happened. (2)
questions.tip: Draw the tree. P(A') = 0.4, and the B branch after A' must make the two B branches add to 0.38.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Two fair coins are flipped. Given that at least one coin shows heads, what is the probability that both show heads?
ms: Outcomes with at least one head: HH, HT, TH. One of these is HH: 1/3
questions.tip: The condition removes TT, leaving 3 equally likely outcomes, not 4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 200 people were tested for a virus. 40 of them have the virus.
The test was positive for 36 of the people who have the virus.
The test was also positive for 16 of the people who do not have the virus.
(a) Show this information on a frequency tree. (2)
(b) A person tests positive. Work out the probability that they have the virus. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 200 → 40 virus (36 positive, 4 negative), 160 no virus (16 positive, 144 negative) (b) 36/52 = 9/13
ms: B1 40 and 160 on the first branches
questions.tip: The denominator is ALL positive tests (36 + 16), not just the people with the virus.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the options chosen by 90 students.
| Art | Music | Drama
Year 10 | 14 | 12 | 20
Year 11 | 18 | 10 | 16
(a) A student is chosen at random. Work out the probability that they chose music. (1)
(b) A Year 11 student is chosen at random. Work out the probability that they chose drama. (1)
(c) A student who chose art is chosen at random. Work out the probability that they are in Year 10. (1)
questions.tip: Each 'given' changes the denominator: total, Year 11 total, art total.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A bag contains 5 red and 3 blue counters. Two counters are taken at random without replacement.
Given that the second counter is red, work out the probability that the first counter was red.
questions.tip: Find P(second red) using both branches. Do not assume it is 4/7 straight away.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5 and P(A | B) = 0.3
(a) Work out P(A ∩ B). (1)
(b) Work out P(B | A). (2)
questions.tip: P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) ÷ P(B). Divide by the event you are GIVEN.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two fair six-sided dice are rolled.
Given that the product of the two scores is even, work out the probability that the sum of the two scores is also even.
ms: M1 27 outcomes have an even product (36 − 9 odd-odd)
M1 both even gives even product and even sum: 9 outcomes
questions.tip: An even product with an even sum needs BOTH dice even. Odd-odd gives an odd product.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A factory has two machines. Machine A makes 60% of the items and machine B makes 40%.
3% of the items made by A are faulty. 4% of the items made by B are faulty.
An item is chosen at random and is faulty.
Work out the probability that it was made by machine A.
questions.tip: This is a 'reverse' conditional probability: divide the A-and-faulty branch by all faulty.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the shoe sizes of 20 students.
Shoe size | Frequency
5 | 3
6 | 7
7 | 6
8 | 4
What is the median shoe size?
ms: Median is halfway between the 10th and 11th values. Cumulative: 3, 10, 16, 20, so the 10th is 6 and the 11th is 7: median 6.5
questions.tip: The median is a shoe size, not a frequency. Use running totals to find the middle position.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the times, t minutes, that 40 people waited for a train.
Time (t minutes) | Frequency
0 < t ≤ 5 | 14
5 < t ≤ 10 | 5
10 < t ≤ 15 | 6
15 < t ≤ 20 | 15
(a) Write down the modal class. (1)
(b) Write down the class that contains the median. (1)
