questions.tip: The median is the 20.5th value. Running totals 14, 19, 25 put it in the third class.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the masses, m kg, of 20 bags.
Mass (m kg) | Frequency
0 < m ≤ 4 | 3
4 < m ≤ 8 | 9
8 < m ≤ 12 | 6
12 < m ≤ 16 | 2
Work out an estimate for the mean mass.
questions.tip: Divide by the total frequency (20), not the number of classes (4).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Five whole numbers have a mean of 6, a median of 5, a mode of 4 and a range of 6.
Which could be the five numbers?
questions.tip: Check every condition. 4, 4, 5, 8, 9 has range 5; 4, 4, 5, 6, 10 adds to 29.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Here are five numbers.
3    7    9    12    x
x is greater than 9. The mean of the five numbers is equal to the median.
Work out the value of x.
questions.tip: With x bigger than 9, the numbers in order are 3, 7, 9, ... so the median is 9.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The annual salaries of 6 people working in a small office are
£18 000    £19 000    £21 000    £22 000    £24 000    £96 000
(a) Work out the mean salary and the median salary. (2)
(b) Which average better represents the salaries? Give a reason. (1)
questions.answer: (a) mean £33 333 (to nearest £), median £21 500 (b) median, because the mean is affected by the extreme value of £96 000
ms: B1 median, with reason that £96 000 is an outlier that raises the mean above 5 of the 6 salaries
questions.tip: Say WHY: the mean is pulled up by one extreme value.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the number of goals a team scored in each of 20 matches.
Goals | Frequency
0 | 4
1 | 7
2 | 5
3 | 3
4 | 1
(a) Work out the mean number of goals per match. (2)
(b) The team plays some more matches and scores exactly 4 goals in each of them. The mean for all the matches is now 2.
Work out how many more matches the team played. (2)
questions.tip: Work with TOTALS: total goals and total matches both increase.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the times, t minutes, 40 students took to complete a puzzle.
Time (t minutes) | Frequency
0 < t ≤ 10 | 5
10 < t ≤ 15 | 10
15 < t ≤ 20 | 15
20 < t ≤ 40 | 10
Work out an estimate for the mean time. Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: Unequal class widths do not change the method, but check each midpoint carefully (the last is 30).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A set of numbers has a mean of 8 and a range of 5.
Each number is multiplied by 3 and then 2 is added.
Work out the mean and the range of the new set of numbers.
questions.tip: Adding 2 to every number moves the data but does not change the spread.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The table shows the weekly pay, £p, of 60 workers.
Pay (£p) | Frequency
200 < p ≤ 300 | 12
300 < p ≤ 400 | 23
400 < p ≤ 600 | 18
600 < p ≤ 1000 | 7
(a) Work out an estimate for the mean weekly pay. (3)
(b) Estimate the number of workers who earn more than £500 a week. (1)
questions.tip: In (b), £500 is halfway through the 400 to 600 class, so take half of 18.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Here are 7 numbers in order.
3    5    6    8    9    11    14
What is the lower quartile?
questions.tip: Put data in order first. For n values the LQ is the (n + 1)/4 th value.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the masses, m kg, of 40 parcels.
Mass (m kg) | Frequency
0 < m ≤ 10 | 5
10 < m ≤ 20 | 12
20 < m ≤ 30 | 18
30 < m ≤ 40 | 5
(a) Complete a cumulative frequency table for this data. (1)
(b) How many parcels have a mass of 20 kg or less? (1)
questions.tip: Cumulative frequency is a running total. The last value must equal the total, 40.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Here are the ages of 15 people in order.
12  15  17  18  20  21  23  24  26  27  29  30  33  35  41
Work out (a) the median (1), (b) the interquartile range (2).
ms: M1 LQ = 18 (4th value) and UQ = 30 (12th value)
questions.tip: For 15 values the quartiles are the 4th and 12th values.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cumulative frequency graph for the times of 60 people is drawn by joining these points with straight lines:
(0, 0), (10, 6), (20, 21), (30, 45), (40, 57), (50, 60)
Estimate the median time.
ms: Median at cumulative frequency 30: between (20, 21) and (30, 45). 20 + (9/24) × 10 = 23.75
questions.tip: Read across at 30 (half of 60), then down to the time axis.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A box plot shows the test scores of 80 students.
Minimum 20, lower quartile 38, median 52, upper quartile 61, maximum 85.
(a) Estimate how many students scored more than 61. (1)
(b) Estimate how many students scored between 38 and 52. (1)
(c) Jamal says, 'Half the students scored between 38 and 61.' Is he correct? Give a reason. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 20 (b) 20 (c) Yes, the IQR contains the middle 50% of the data
ms: B1 yes, the values between the quartiles are the middle 50%
questions.tip: Each section of a box plot holds about 25% of the data, whatever its width.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The cumulative frequency table shows the heights, h cm, of 100 plants.
Height (h cm) | Cumulative frequency
h ≤ 10 | 5
h ≤ 20 | 25
h ≤ 30 | 65
h ≤ 40 | 85
h ≤ 50 | 100
A cumulative frequency graph is drawn by joining the points (0, 0), (10, 5), (20, 25), (30, 65), (40, 85) and (50, 100) with straight lines.
Use the graph to estimate the interquartile range.
questions.tip: For n = 100 read at 25 and 75 on the cumulative frequency axis.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cumulative frequency graph for the times, in minutes, of 120 runners is drawn by joining these points with straight lines:
(20, 0), (25, 12), (30, 42), (35, 84), (40, 108), (45, 120)
Estimate the percentage of runners who took more than 37 minutes.
questions.tip: The graph gives the number AT OR BELOW a value. Subtract from the total for 'more than'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cumulative frequency graph for the scores of 80 boys is drawn by joining these points with straight lines:
(0, 0), (10, 4), (20, 20), (30, 60), (40, 72), (50, 80)
For the girls, the median score was 31 and the interquartile range was 14.
Compare the scores of the boys and the girls.
questions.answer: Boys: median 25, IQR 10. Girls scored higher on average (31 > 25); boys' scores were more consistent (IQR 10 < 14)
ms: M1 boys' median 25 read from the graph
M1 boys' LQ 20 and UQ 30, IQR 10
A1 girls had a higher median so did better on average
A1 boys had a smaller IQR so their scores were more consistent
questions.tip: Make one comparison of average and one of spread, and say what each means in context.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The cumulative frequency table gives the times, t minutes, of 40 phone calls.
Time (t minutes) | Cumulative frequency
t ≤ 10 | 6
t ≤ 20 | 20
t ≤ 30 | 34
t ≤ 40 | 40
All times are greater than 0.
Work out an estimate for the mean length of a call.
questions.tip: You cannot use the cumulative frequencies in fx. Change them back into frequencies first.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cumulative frequency graph for the exam marks of 160 students is drawn by joining these points with straight lines:
(0, 0), (20, 8), (40, 40), (60, 104), (80, 148), (100, 160)
The pass mark is set so that 70% of the students pass.
Estimate the pass mark.
questions.tip: The students who fail are at the bottom of the graph, so read at 30%, not 70%.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the frequencies for some grouped data.
0 < x ≤ 10: 20
10 < x ≤ 15: 15
15 < x ≤ 30: 30
30 < x ≤ 50: 20
On a histogram, which class has the tallest bar?
ms: Frequency densities: 2, 3, 2, 1. The tallest bar is 10 < x ≤ 15
questions.tip: The tallest bar has the greatest frequency DENSITY, not the greatest frequency.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Work out the frequency density for each class.
Time (t s) | Frequency
0 < t ≤ 20 | 16
20 < t ≤ 30 | 24
30 < t ≤ 35 | 15
35 < t ≤ 50 | 9
ms: M1 frequency ÷ class width for at least one class
questions.tip: Class width is the difference between the boundaries (35 − 30 = 5), not the upper value.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A histogram has these bars.
0 < x ≤ 5: frequency density 4
5 < x ≤ 10: frequency density 6
10 < x ≤ 20: frequency density 3.5
20 < x ≤ 40: frequency density 1
Work out the total frequency.
ms: M1 frequency = fd × width for at least two bars (20, 30, 35, 20)
questions.tip: Frequency is the AREA of each bar: density × width.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In a histogram, the bar for 15 < x ≤ 25 represents 32 people.
The bar for 25 < x ≤ 30 is the same height.
How many people does the bar for 25 < x ≤ 30 represent?
ms: Same height, half the width, so half the area: 16
questions.tip: Same height does not mean same frequency when the widths differ.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A histogram has these bars.
0 < x ≤ 10: frequency density 1.2
10 < x ≤ 20: frequency density 2.8
20 < x ≤ 25: frequency density 6
25 < x ≤ 40: frequency density 2
Estimate the number of values between 15 and 30.
questions.tip: For part of a class, use the part of the width you need (5), not the whole width.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Complete the table.
Height (h cm) | Frequency | Frequency density
0 < h ≤ 10 | 15 | 1.5
10 < h ≤ 15 | ? | 5.2
15 < h ≤ 30 | 36 | ?
questions.tip: Frequency = fd × width (5 × 5.2); fd = frequency ÷ width (36 ÷ 15).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A histogram has these bars.
0 < x ≤ 10: frequency density 0.8
10 < x ≤ 20: frequency density 2
20 < x ≤ 30: frequency density 3.2
30 < x ≤ 50: frequency density 0.6
Work out an estimate for the mean.
questions.tip: Turn the densities back into frequencies before using midpoints.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The times, t minutes, of 100 people are shown in a histogram.
0 < t ≤ 10: frequency density 2
10 < t ≤ 15: frequency density 4.8
15 < t ≤ 25: frequency density not shown
25 < t ≤ 40: frequency density 1.2
(a) Work out the frequency density for 15 < t ≤ 25. (3)
(b) One of the people is chosen at random. Work out the probability that their time was more than 25 minutes. (1)
questions.tip: Use the total frequency: the missing class must make the frequencies add to 100.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In a histogram, the bar for 20 < x ≤ 30 is twice as tall as the bar for 30 < x ≤ 60.
Liam says, 'There are more values in 20 < x ≤ 30 than in 30 < x ≤ 60.'
Is Liam correct? Explain your answer.
questions.answer: No. If the shorter bar has height h, the frequencies are 10 × 2h = 20h and 30 × h = 30h, so 30 < x ≤ 60 has more
ms: M1 compares areas: 10 × 2h and 30 × h (or equivalent)
A1 Liam is wrong, 30 < x ≤ 60 has more values
questions.tip: Compare AREAS, not heights.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The table shows the lengths, L cm, of 79 fish.
Length (L cm) | Frequency
0 < L ≤ 5 | 12
5 < L ≤ 12 | 21
12 < L ≤ 20 | 28
20 < L ≤ 35 | 18
(a) Work out the frequency density for each class. (1)
(b) Estimate the number of fish longer than 16 cm. (2)
questions.tip: 16 is halfway through the 12 to 20 class, so take half its frequency, then add the whole of the next class.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A head teacher asks 50 of the 900 students in her school about school lunches.
What is the population?
ms: The population is the whole group being studied: all 900 students
questions.tip: The 50 students are the SAMPLE. The population is everyone the survey is about.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A gym has 600 members. Describe how to take a simple random sample of 40 members.
questions.answer: Number the members 1 to 600, use a random number generator to pick 40 different numbers, and select those members
ms: B1 give each member a number (or a list of all members)
B1 use a random number generator (or names drawn from a hat) to choose 40, ignoring repeats
questions.tip: 'Pick them randomly' is not enough. Say how each member gets an equal chance.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A stratified sample by gender of 45 students is taken from a school.
The sample contains 20 girls.
There are 360 boys in the school.
Work out the number of students in the school.
questions.tip: Each sampled boy represents the same fraction of the school as each sampled girl.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Capture-recapture is used to estimate the number of fish in a lake.
Which of these would make the estimate unreliable?
options: Some of the marks fall off the fish between the two samples
The marked fish are released back into the lake before the second sample
The second sample is the same size as the first
The fish are caught with the same type of net both times
ms: If marks fall off, fewer marked fish are recaptured, so the estimate is too high. The method assumes the marks stay on and the population does not change.
questions.tip: Releasing the marked fish so they mix back in is part of the method, not a problem.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] There are 240 students in Year 11: 132 boys and 108 girls.
Lucy wants to find the mean time Year 11 students spend on homework.
(a) She first asks 10 students. Give one reason why this sample may not be reliable. (1)
(b) She then takes a stratified sample of 60 students by gender. Work out the number of boys and the number of girls in her sample. (2)
questions.answer: (a) The sample is too small (b) 33 boys and 27 girls
ms: B1 sample too small to represent 240 students (or not stratified/random)
questions.tip: Check that your two numbers add to the sample size, 60.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A council wants to find out how residents travel to work.
It telephones 200 numbers from a landline phone book between 10 am and 2 pm on weekdays.
(a) Give two reasons why this sample is likely to be biased. (2)
(b) Suggest one way to improve the sampling method. (1)
questions.answer: (a) People at work in the day will not answer, so commuters are left out; people without landlines are left out (b) e.g. choose a random sample from the electoral register and survey at different times
ms: B1 calls during working hours miss people who are at work
B1 people without a landline are excluded
B1 a suitable improvement, e.g. random sample from a full list of residents, contact at different times or by different methods
questions.tip: Bias reasons must be specific to the context. 'It is not random' alone scores nothing.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] On Monday, 30 birds in a wood are caught, ringed and released.
On Tuesday, 50 birds are caught. 10 of them are ringed.
On Wednesday, 40 birds are caught. 6 of them are ringed.
(a) Work out an estimate of the number of birds using Tuesday's sample and using Wednesday's sample. (2)
(b) Which of the two estimates is likely to be more reliable? Give a reason. (1)
(c) Give a reason why the two estimates are different. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 150 and 200 (b) Tuesday's, because more birds were caught in that sample (c) e.g. samples are random so vary, or birds may have moved into or out of the wood
ms: B1 Tuesday's estimate, because the sample is larger (50 birds, with more ringed birds recaptured)
B1 a valid reason: natural variation between random samples, or the population changing
questions.tip: Use N = (number marked × second sample size) ÷ number marked in the sample.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A school has 1200 students.
Year 10 boys: 300
Year 10 girls: 240
Year 11 boys: 360
Year 11 girls: 300
A stratified sample by year group and gender is taken. The sample contains 18 Year 10 girls.
Work out the number of Year 11 boys in the sample.
questions.tip: The fraction sampled is the same for every group: 18 out of 240.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 120 birds on an island are caught, ringed and released.
A week later, 90 birds are caught and 18 of them are ringed.
(a) Estimate the number of birds on the island. (2)
(b) Ringed birds are easier to catch than birds without rings. Will your estimate be too high or too low? Explain why. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 600 (b) Too low: there will be too many ringed birds in the second sample, making the estimate smaller than the true population
ms: B1 too low, because a higher proportion of ringed birds in the sample makes the estimate smaller
questions.tip: More marked animals in the second sample means you divide by a bigger number, so the estimate falls.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two random samples are taken from the same population to estimate the mean number of hours of screen time people have each evening.
Sample A: 20 people, mean 4.2 hours.
Sample B: 80 people, mean 3.8 hours.
(a) Which sample is likely to give the more reliable estimate? Give a reason. (1)
(b) Use both samples to work out the best estimate of the population mean. (2)
questions.answer: (a) Sample B, it is larger (b) 3.88 hours
ms: B1 sample B because it is larger
questions.tip: Weight each mean by its sample size. (4.2 + 3.8) ÷ 2 = 4 is wrong.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] These points are plotted on a scatter graph.
(1, 9), (2, 7), (3, 6), (4, 4), (5, 2)
What type of correlation is shown?
ms: As x increases, y decreases: negative correlation
questions.tip: Negative correlation means one goes up while the other goes down.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the hours spent revising and the test scores of 6 students.
Hours | 2 | 4 | 5 | 7 | 8 | 10
Score | 35 | 48 | 52 | 66 | 70 | 81
(a) Describe the correlation. (1)
(b) Another student revised for 6 hours and scored 20. What name is given to a point like this? (1)
questions.tip: Write 'positive correlation', not just 'it goes up'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows five pairs of values.
x | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10
y | 15 | 19 | 26 | 29 | 36
A line of best fit should pass through the mean point.
Show that the mean point is (6, 25).
questions.answer: Mean of x = 30/5 = 6, mean of y = 125/5 = 25
questions.tip: Use the mean point to help you draw a good line of best fit.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The line of best fit for a scatter graph of temperature, x °C, and the number of hot drinks sold, y, has equation y = 120 − 8x.
Estimate the number of hot drinks sold when the temperature is 9 °C.
questions.tip: Multiply before subtracting. (120 − 8) × 9 is the wrong order.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A line of best fit on a scatter graph of temperature (x °C) against the number of cold drinks sold (y) passes through the points (12, 21) and (27, 57).
(a) Work out the gradient of the line. (2)
(b) Interpret the gradient in this context. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 2.4 (b) about 2.4 more cold drinks are sold for each 1 °C rise in temperature
ms: B1 for each extra 1 °C, about 2.4 more drinks are sold
questions.tip: Interpreting a gradient means 'for each extra 1 unit of x, y changes by...'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A scatter graph shows the heights and weights of 8 dogs. The points are widely spread but show a slight upward trend.
Tom uses a line of best fit to estimate the weight of a dog from its height.
Give two reasons why his estimate may not be reliable.
questions.answer: The correlation is weak; the sample of 8 dogs is small
ms: B1 the correlation is weak (points widely spread)
B1 the sample is small (only 8 dogs)
questions.tip: Reasons must refer to the data given: strength of correlation and sample size.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A scatter graph shows the outside temperature, x °C, and the amount of heating oil, y litres, a school uses each day.
The line of best fit passes through (5, 62) and (25, 22).
The data on the graph have x values from 5 to 25.
(a) Find the equation of the line of best fit in the form y = mx + c. (2)
(b) Use your equation to estimate the temperature on a day when the school uses 50 litres of oil. (1)
(c) Interpret the gradient of the line in this context. (1)
questions.answer: (a) y = −2x + 72 (b) 11 °C (c) for each 1 °C rise in temperature, the school uses about 2 litres less oil per day
ms: B1 about 2 litres less oil per day for each extra 1 °C (must mention both variables)
questions.tip: A falling line has a negative gradient. When interpreting it, say 'for each 1 °C increase, y decreases by about 2 litres'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the ages and values of 7 cars of the same model.
Age (years) | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7
Value (£1000s) | 18 | 16 | 14.5 | 13 | 20 | 10 | 8.5
(a) Identify the outlier. (1)
(b) Suggest a reason for the outlier. (1)
(c) Ignoring the outlier, estimate the value of a car that is 4.5 years old. (1)
questions.answer: (a) (5, 20) (b) e.g. it has very low mileage or is in excellent condition (c) about £12 000 (accept £11 500 to £12 500)
ms: B1 a sensible reason, e.g. low mileage, rare extras, excellent condition
B1 value in the range £11 500 to £12 500
questions.tip: Ignore the outlier when you draw or use the line of best fit.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The line of best fit on a scatter graph passes through the mean point (6, 25) and has gradient 2.5.
(a) Find the equation of the line of best fit. (2)
(b) Use it to estimate y when x = 9. (1)
questions.tip: Substitute the mean point to find c.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The table shows the number of weeks, x, since a plant was planted and its height, y cm.
x | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8
y | 5 | 12 | 17 | 20 | 22 | 23 | 23.5 | 24
(a) Describe the relationship between x and y. (1)
(b) Explain why a straight line of best fit is not suitable for this data. (1)
questions.answer: (a) As x increases y increases, but the rate of growth slows down and levels off (b) the points follow a curve, not a straight line
ms: B1 positive relationship that levels off / increases at a decreasing rate
B1 the relationship is non-linear (a curve), so a straight line would not fit well
questions.tip: Correlation describes the trend, but always check whether the trend is actually a straight line.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Expand and simplify (x + 5)(x - 3)
questions.tip: Watch the sign of the constant: (+5) × (-3) = -15, and the x terms are -3x + 5x = +2x.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise x² + 3x - 28
ms: M1 for (x ± 7)(x ± 4) or two numbers with product -28 and sum 3
questions.tip: Check by expanding: the pair must multiply to -28 AND add to +3, so the bigger number is positive.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise fully 8x²y - 12xy³
ms: The HCF of 8x²y and 12xy³ is 4xy, leaving 2x - 3y² inside the bracket.
questions.tip: 'Fully' means take out the highest common factor. If the bracket still has a common factor (like 4x - 6y²), it is not finished.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Expand and simplify (x + 4)(x - 1)(2x + 3)
ms: M1 for expanding two brackets correctly, e.g. x² + 3x - 4
M1 for multiplying their quadratic by the third bracket with at least 4 of the 6 terms correct
questions.tip: Expand two brackets first and simplify before multiplying by the third. Most lost marks are sign slips in the middle terms.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise 3x² - 14x + 8
ms: M1 for (3x ± 2)(x ± 4) or for splitting the middle term: 3x² - 12x - 2x + 8
questions.tip: Both signs must be negative because the constant is + and the x term is -. Expand to check you get -14x, not -10x.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise fully 2x³ - 32x
ms: M1 for taking out a common factor, e.g. 2x(x² - 16)
questions.tip: After taking out 2x, spot the difference of two squares. Stopping at 2x(x² - 16) loses the accuracy mark.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Show that (x + 3)(2x - 1)² can be written in the form ax³ + bx² + cx + d, where a, b, c and d are integers.
ms: M1 for multiplying by (x + 3) with at least 4 of the 6 terms correct
questions.tip: (2x - 1)² is NOT 4x² + 1. Write it as (2x - 1)(2x - 1) and expand properly.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise fully 4x² - (x - 3)²
ms: M1 for recognising a difference of two squares: (2x - (x - 3))(2x + (x - 3)) or for expanding to 3x² + 6x - 9
questions.tip: Use brackets when you subtract (x - 3): 2x - (x - 3) = x + 3, not x - 3. Then take out the common factor 3 for 'fully'.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Given that (2x + a)(x - 5) ≡ 2x² + bx - 15, find the value of a and the value of b.
questions.tip: Compare coefficients one at a time: the constants give a first, then use a to find b. Don't forget the -10x term.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Factorise 6x² - 7xy - 20y²
questions.tip: With two variables, factorise exactly as with one: the outer and inner products must add to -7xy. Swapping signs gives +7xy.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Simplify fully (x² + 4x)/(x² - 16)
questions.tip: Factorise top and bottom first. You can only cancel whole brackets, never individual terms like x² with x².

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write (x + 1)/3 + (x - 2)/4 as a single fraction in its simplest form.
ms: M1 for a common denominator of 12 with at least one numerator correct, e.g. (4(x + 1) + 3(x - 2))/12
questions.tip: Multiply the WHOLE numerator by the factor: 3(x - 2) = 3x - 6, not 3x - 2.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Simplify fully (3x² - 12)/(x² + x - 6)
ms: M1 for factorising the numerator: 3(x² - 4) or 3(x + 2)(x - 2)
questions.tip: Take out the common factor 3 first, then spot the difference of two squares. Cancel the (x - 2) bracket only.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 2/(x - 3) + 5/(x + 1) as a single fraction in its simplest form.
questions.tip: 5(x - 3) = 5x - 15, so the constant is 2 - 15 = -13. Leaving the bracket unexpanded loses the final mark.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Simplify fully (x² - 25)/(2x + 10) × 6/(x - 5)
questions.tip: Factorise everything before multiplying. Multiplying out first makes cancelling almost impossible.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 1/(x - 3) + 6/(x + 1) = 1
ms: M1 for reducing to a 3-term quadratic: x² - 9x + 14 = 0
M1 for correct factorisation (x - 2)(x - 7) = 0 or correct use of the formula
questions.tip: Multiply EVERY term by the common denominator, including the 1 on the right. Forgetting to multiply the 1 is the classic error.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 2x/(x + 3) - 1/(x - 1) = 1
questions.tip: When you reach x² - 5x = 0, factorise to x(x - 5) = 0. Dividing by x throws away the solution x = 0.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve 1/(x - 2) + 2/(x + 1) = 1
Give your answers in the form a ± √b, where a and b are integers.
ms: M1 for correct substitution into the formula, x = (4 ± √12)/2, or completing the square (x - 2)² = 3
questions.tip: Simplify √12 = 2√3 and then divide BOTH terms of 4 ± 2√3 by 2. Leaving (4 ± √12)/2 is not in the required form.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Show that (x² - 3x)/(x² - 9) ÷ 2x/(x + 3) simplifies to 1/2
ms: M1 for turning the division into multiplication by the reciprocal (x + 3)/(2x)
A1 for cancelling fully to 1/2 with all steps shown
questions.tip: Flip the SECOND fraction only, then cancel. In a 'show that' every factorising step must be written down.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Write 3/(x + 2) - (x - 7)/(x² + x - 2) as a single fraction in its simplest form.
questions.tip: Subtracting (x - 7) changes BOTH signs: -x + 7. Then look for a common factor in the numerator so you can cancel.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve x² - 5x - 24 = 0
questions.tip: Once factorised, change the sign: (x - 8) = 0 gives x = +8.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve x² = 6x
ms: A1 for both x = 0 and x = 6
questions.tip: Do not divide both sides by x: you lose the solution x = 0. Rearrange to = 0 and factorise.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve x² - 4x - 1 = 0
Give your solutions in the form a ± √b, where a and b are integers.
ms: M1 for correct substitution into the formula: (4 ± √(16 + 4))/2, or for (x - 2)² - 5 = 0
questions.tip: -4ac with a = 1, c = -1 is +4, so the discriminant is 16 + 4 = 20, not 12.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (a) Write x² - 10x + 31 in the form (x - a)² + b. (2)
(b) Hence write down the minimum value of x² - 10x + 31. (1)
ms: B1 for minimum value 6 (ft their b)
questions.tip: Subtract the square of half the coefficient: 31 - 25 = 6. The minimum value is b, not a.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 3x² + 10x - 8 = 0
ms: M1 for (3x ± 2)(x ± 4) or correct substitution into the formula
questions.tip: From (3x - 2) = 0, x = 2/3, not 2 or 3/2. Solve each bracket properly.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which expression gives the solutions of 2x² + 3x - 4 = 0?
questions.tip: The denominator is 2a = 4, and -4ac = -4(2)(-4) = +32. Square b before anything else.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (a) Write 2x² + 12x + 7 in the form a(x + b)² + c. (2)
(b) Hence solve 2x² + 12x + 7 = 0, giving your answers in surd form. (2)
questions.tip: Take out the 2 from the x² and x terms only. Then -9 inside the bracket becomes -18 outside: -18 + 7 = -11.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve 3x² - 2x - 2 = 0
Give your answers in the form (a ± √b)/c, where a, b and c are integers.
questions.tip: Simplify √28 to 2√7 then cancel the common factor 2 from every term. -4ac = -4(3)(-2) = +24.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A right-angled triangle has sides of length x cm and (x + 7) cm, and hypotenuse (x + 8) cm.
Work out the area of the triangle.
ms: A1 for x = 5 (rejecting x = -3 because a length cannot be negative)
questions.tip: (x + 7)² is x² + 14x + 49. Give a reason for rejecting the negative root.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 2(x + 3)² = 5(x + 3) + 3
ms: M1 for a substitution such as u = x + 3 giving 2u² - 5u - 3 = 0, or for expanding to 2x² + 7x = 0
questions.tip: If you substitute u = x + 3, remember to convert back to x at the end. u = 3 is not the answer.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
x + y = 10
x - y = 4
ms: Adding gives 2x = 14, so x = 7 and y = 3.
questions.tip: Always substitute back into BOTH equations to check: 7 + 3 = 10 and 7 - 3 = 4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
4x + 3y = 5
2x - y = 5
ms: M1 for a correct method to eliminate one variable, e.g. multiplying the second equation by 3 and adding, or y = 2x - 5 substituted
questions.tip: When you multiply an equation to match coefficients, multiply EVERY term, including the number on the right.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
3x - 4y = 18
5x + 3y = 1
ms: M1 for multiplying to get equal coefficients, e.g. 9x - 12y = 54 and 20x + 12y = 4
M1 for correctly adding or subtracting to eliminate one variable: 29x = 58
questions.tip: Same signs subtract, different signs add. Here the y terms are -12y and +12y, so ADD.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] 4 coffees and 3 muffins cost £13.70
2 coffees and 5 muffins cost £12.80
Work out the cost of one coffee and the cost of one muffin.
ms: M1 for forming both equations: 4c + 3m = 13.70 and 2c + 5m = 12.80 (or in pence)
M1 for a correct elimination, e.g. doubling the second: 4c + 10m = 25.60, then 7m = 11.90
questions.tip: Working in pence (1370 and 1280) avoids decimal slips. Give money answers with 2 decimal places and a £ sign.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which gives all the solutions of the simultaneous equations y = x² - 2 and y = x + 4?
questions.tip: Find y by substituting into the LINEAR equation; it is quicker and less error-prone. Pair each x with its own y.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
y = 2x² - 3x
y = x + 6
questions.tip: Rearrange to = 0 before factorising. Each x value needs its matching y value for full marks.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
x² + y² = 10
x + 2y = 5
ms: M1 for rearranging the linear equation: x = 5 - 2y
questions.tip: (5 - 2y)² = 25 - 20y + 4y². Write out both brackets: squaring term by term (25 + 4y²) is wrong.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve the simultaneous equations
x² + xy = 12
x - y = 2
ms: M1 for y = x - 2 substituted: x² + x(x - 2) = 12
questions.tip: x(x - 2) = x² - 2x. Divide the quadratic through by 2 to make factorising easier.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The line y = x + 1 meets the curve y = x² - 3x + 2 at the points A and B.
Find the exact coordinates of A and B.
ms: M1 for correct use of the formula or completing the square: (x - 2)² = 3
questions.tip: 'Exact' means leave answers as surds. y = x + 1, so add 1 to each x value, keeping the matching sign.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A rectangle has a perimeter of 34 cm and a diagonal of length 13 cm.
Use algebra to find the length and width of the rectangle.
ms: M1 for x² + (17 - x)² = 169 leading to x² - 17x + 60 = 0
questions.tip: Perimeter 34 means length + width = 17, not 34. 'Use algebra' means a trial-and-improvement answer scores nothing.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve 3(x - 2) ≥ 9
questions.tip: Expand the bracket fully: 3 × (-2) = -6. Writing 3x - 2 gives 11/3.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] -5 < 2x + 1 ≤ 9
x is an integer. Write down all the possible values of x.
questions.tip: < means the end value is NOT included, so -3 is not allowed, but ≤ means 4 is.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve (5 - 2x)/3 > x - 5
ms: M1 for multiplying both sides by 3: 5 - 2x > 3x - 15
questions.tip: Multiply the WHOLE right side by 3: 3(x - 5) = 3x - 15. If you divide by a negative, flip the sign.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve x² + 3x - 10 ≤ 0
ms: M1 for critical values found: (x + 5)(x - 2), giving -5 and 2
M1 for identifying the region between the roots (e.g. a sketch)
questions.tip: Sketch the U-shaped curve. ≤ 0 means the part BELOW the x-axis, which is between the roots.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which gives the solution of 2x² > 18 in set notation?
ms: x² > 9 means x is more than 3 away from 0: x < -3 or x > 3.
questions.tip: Square-rooting an inequality gives TWO regions. Writing x > ±3 is not accepted.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A region R is a triangle bounded by the three lines x = 1, y = x and x + y = 8. All boundary lines are solid and the point (2, 4) lies inside R.
Write down the three inequalities that define R.
questions.tip: Test a point inside the region in each line to find the direction. Solid lines mean ≤ or ≥, dashed mean < or >.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Solve 2x² - 5x - 12 > 0
Give your answer in set notation.
ms: M1 for (2x + 3)(x - 4) or critical values -3/2 and 4
M1 for identifying the regions outside the roots
B1 for correct set notation {x : x < -3/2} ∪ {x : x > 4}
questions.tip: > 0 means ABOVE the x-axis: the two outside regions. Don't join them as -3/2 > x > 4, which is impossible.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Find all the integers n that satisfy both
n² < 30
and 3n + 4 > n - 3
ms: M1 for -√30 < n < √30 or listing integers -5 to 5
M1 for combining the two conditions
questions.tip: n² < 30 includes negative values: (-5)² = 25 < 30. Combine both lists carefully.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Work out how many points with integer coordinates (x, y) satisfy all three inequalities
x ≥ 0
y ≤ 3
y > x - 2
ms: M1 for a systematic method, e.g. for each x listing the allowed y values
M1 for x = 0: y = -1 to 3 (5 points) and x = 1: y = 0 to 3 (4 points)
M1 for x = 2, 3, 4 giving 3, 2, 1 points and no points for x ≥ 5
questions.tip: y > x - 2 is strict, so points ON the line y = x - 2 do not count. Points on x = 0 and y = 3 do count.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Solve x² ≥ 4x
ms: M1 for x² - 4x ≥ 0 and x(x - 4) giving critical values 0 and 4
M1 for identifying the outside regions
questions.tip: Never divide an inequality by x: x could be negative or zero. Rearrange to x² - 4x ≥ 0 instead.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make x the subject of y = 4x - 7
ms: Add 7: y + 7 = 4x, then divide by 4: x = (y + 7)/4.
questions.tip: Undo in reverse order: deal with the -7 first, then the × 4. Divide the WHOLE of y + 7 by 4.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make w the subject of P = 2l + 2w
questions.tip: Subtract 2l from both sides first. Writing w = P - 2l/2 without brackets is wrong.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make h the subject of A = (1/2)(a + b)h
questions.tip: Divide by the whole bracket (a + b). Writing 2A/a + b is a different formula.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make x the subject of 3(x + 2a) = ax + 5
ms: M1 for collecting x terms and factorising: x(3 - a) = 5 - 6a
questions.tip: When x appears twice, get all x terms on one side and factorise x out. You cannot divide by 'x' to get rid of it.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make v the subject of E = (1/2)mv²
questions.tip: Multiplying by 2 puts the 2 on top with E. Square-root as the LAST step.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make y the subject of x = (3 - y)/(y + 2)
ms: M1 for multiplying by (y + 2): xy + 2x = 3 - y
M1 for collecting y terms: xy + y = 3 - 2x and factorising y(x + 1)
questions.tip: Expand x(y + 2) fully to xy + 2x. Then the y terms go on one side: xy + y = y(x + 1).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make u the subject of v² = u² + 2as
questions.tip: You cannot square-root term by term: √(v² - 2as) is NOT v - √(2as).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make x the subject of (x + 2)/a = (x - 1)/b
ms: M1 for bx + 2b = ax - a and collecting x terms
M1 for x(a - b) = a + 2b or x(b - a) = -a - 2b
questions.tip: Cross-multiply first so there are no fractions. Keep track of signs when moving -a and 2b across.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make m the subject of E = mgh + (1/2)mv²
ms: M1 for factorising m: E = m(gh + (1/2)v²)
M1 for dividing by the bracket
questions.tip: m appears in two terms, so factorise it out. Multiplying everything by 2 first removes the fraction.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Make x the subject of y = (x² + 1)/(x² - 3)
questions.tip: Treat x² as the thing to collect, factorise it out, and only square-root at the very end.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find the nth term of the sequence 20, 17, 14, 11, ...
ms: The difference is -3, so -3n; the zero term is 23. nth term = 23 - 3n.
questions.tip: Check with n = 1: 23 - 3 = 20. Using the first term (20) instead of the zero term (23) is the usual slip.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The nth term of a sequence is 3n² - 2.
Work out the difference between the 4th term and the 5th term.
questions.tip: Square n before multiplying by 3: 3 × 4² = 48, not 12² = 144.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find the nth term of the quadratic sequence 2, 9, 20, 35, 54, ...
ms: M1 for subtracting 2n² to get the linear sequence 0, 1, 2, 3, 4
questions.tip: The coefficient of n² is HALF the second difference. Then subtract 2n² from every term to find the linear part.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find the nth term of the quadratic sequence 3, 4, 9, 18, 31, ...
questions.tip: The remaining linear part has negative terms here: 1, -4, -9, ... is -5n + 6. Check your nth term with n = 2: 8 - 10 + 6 = 4.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find the nth term of the geometric sequence 5, 15, 45, 135, ...
ms: First term 5, common ratio 3, so the nth term is 5 × 3^(n - 1).
questions.tip: Check with n = 1: 5 × 3⁰ = 5. Using 3ⁿ gives 15 as the first term.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The 4th term of an arithmetic sequence is 19 and the 10th term is 49.
Find an expression for the nth term.
questions.tip: From the 4th to the 10th term there are 6 jumps, not 7.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find the nth term of the quadratic sequence 10, 9, 4, -5, -18, ...
questions.tip: A negative second difference gives a negative n² term. Subtracting -2n² means ADDING 2n² to each term.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The nth term of a sequence is n² - 10n + 30.
By completing the square, find the smallest term in the sequence and the value of n that gives it.
ms: A1 for smallest term 5 when n = 5
questions.tip: The minimum of (n - 5)² + 5 happens when the bracket is 0, so n = 5 and the term is 5.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The first three terms of a geometric sequence are x, x + 6 and x + 18.
(a) Find the value of x. (3)
(b) Find the 5th term of the sequence. (1)
questions.tip: In a geometric sequence the RATIO is constant, not the difference. The x² terms cancel, leaving a linear equation.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Here are the first five terms of a quadratic sequence: 5, 12, 21, 32, 45
(a) Find an expression for the nth term. (3)
(b) Which term of the sequence is equal to 140? (2)
ms: M1 for second difference 2, so n²
questions.tip: Reject n = -14: term positions must be positive integers.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = x² - 3x
Find f(-4)
questions.tip: Put negative inputs in brackets: (-4)² = 16 and -3 × -4 = +12.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = 7 - 2x
Find f⁻¹(x)
ms: M1 for y = 7 - 2x rearranged to 2x = 7 - y or for swapping x and y: x = 7 - 2y
questions.tip: Write the final answer in terms of x, starting f⁻¹(x) = .... Leaving it in terms of y loses the mark.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = 3x + 2 and g(x) = x² - 1
Find gf(x). Give your answer in its simplest form.
questions.tip: gf(x) means do f first, then g: put f(x) into g. (3x + 2)² has a middle term 12x.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = 2x - 5 and g(x) = 1/x
Which is fg(x)?
questions.tip: fg means g first, then f. 1/(2x - 5) is gf(x).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = 4x - 3
Solve f(x) = f⁻¹(x)
questions.tip: Find the inverse first, then form an equation. Multiplying both sides by 4 removes the fraction.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = x + 5 and g(x) = 2x²
Solve gf(x) = 32
questions.tip: Square-rooting gives ± 4. Forgetting the negative root loses x = -9.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = 2/(x - 1)
Show that ff(x) = 2(x - 1)/(3 - x)
ms: M1 for simplifying the denominator to (2 - (x - 1))/(x - 1) = (3 - x)/(x - 1)
A1 for 2(x - 1)/(3 - x) with all steps shown
questions.tip: Write 1 as (x - 1)/(x - 1) to combine the denominator. Then dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = 2x + 3 and g(x) = x² + c, where c is a constant.
gf(1) = 30
(a) Find the value of c. (2)
(b) Solve fg(x) = 19, giving your answers in surd form. (3)
questions.tip: gf(1): work out f(1) first, then put that number into g. In (b) remember the ± when square-rooting.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = x/(x + 1)
Solve ff(x) = 1/3
questions.tip: Multiply the top and bottom of the compound fraction by (x + 1) to simplify it in one go.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = 5 - x
Which is f⁻¹(x)?
ms: y = 5 - x gives x = 5 - y, so f⁻¹(x) = 5 - x. The function is its own inverse.
questions.tip: f⁻¹ is the inverse function, not the reciprocal 1/f(x). Check: f(f(2)) = f(3) = 2.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] n is an integer. Which expression represents the sum of two consecutive even numbers?
questions.tip: Consecutive even numbers differ by 2: 2n and 2n + 2, not 2n and 2n + 1.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove that the sum of any two odd numbers is even.
ms: M1 for using 2m + 1 and 2n + 1 (two different letters) and adding
A1 for 2(m + n + 1) with a statement that this is even
questions.tip: Use different letters for the two odd numbers, otherwise you have only proved it for two EQUAL odd numbers.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove that the product of two consecutive even numbers is always a multiple of 8.
questions.answer: 2n(2n + 2) = 4n(n + 1); n(n + 1) is even, so 4 × even is a multiple of 8
ms: A1 for explaining that one of n and n + 1 must be even, so n(n + 1) = 2k and the product is 8k
questions.tip: 4n(n + 1) only shows a multiple of 4. You must explain why n(n + 1) is even to get the extra factor of 2.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove that (n + 5)² - (n + 1)² is a multiple of 8 for all integer values of n.
ms: M1 for expanding both brackets correctly
questions.tip: Bracket the second expansion before subtracting: -(n² + 2n + 1) changes all three signs.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] n is a positive integer. Prove that (2n + 1)² - (2n + 1) is always even.
ms: A1 for 2(2n² + n) with conclusion 'so it is even'
questions.tip: Factor out the 2 explicitly and write a conclusion. Showing it works for n = 1, 2, 3 is not a proof.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Ben says 'n² + n + 41 is prime for every positive integer n.'
Which value of n shows that Ben is wrong?
ms: 40² + 40 + 41 = 1681 = 41², which is not prime. n = 1, 10 and 20 give 43, 151 and 461, which are all prime.
questions.tip: One counterexample is enough to disprove a statement. Try values that make every term share a factor, here 41.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove that the sum of the squares of any three consecutive integers is always one less than a multiple of 3.
ms: M1 for using (n - 1), n, (n + 1) or n, n + 1, n + 2 and squaring
questions.tip: To show '1 less than a multiple of 3', rewrite the constant as 3 - 1 and factorise the 3 out.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] n is an integer. Prove that (2n + 3)² - (2n - 1)(2n + 1) is always even but is never a multiple of 4.
questions.answer: = 4n² + 12n + 9 - (4n² - 1) = 12n + 10 = 2(6n + 5), even; = 4(3n + 2) + 2, so remainder 2 when divided by 4
ms: B1 for 4(3n + 2) + 2, or 6n + 5 is odd so the expression is 2 × odd, not a multiple of 4
questions.tip: Use brackets when subtracting 4n² - 1: the -1 becomes +1, giving 9 + 1 = 10.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Prove that the difference between the cubes of any two consecutive integers is always odd.
questions.answer: (n + 1)³ - n³ = 3n² + 3n + 1 = 3n(n + 1) + 1; n(n + 1) is even so 3n(n + 1) is even, and even + 1 is odd
ms: A1 for explaining n(n + 1) is even so the result is even + 1 = odd
questions.tip: Expand (n + 1)³ as (n + 1)(n + 1)(n + 1). The key step is spotting n(n + 1), a product of consecutive integers.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] n is a positive integer. Prove that 3^(n + 2) - 3ⁿ is always a multiple of 8.
questions.tip: Use the index law a^(m + n) = a^m × a^n. 3^(n + 2) is NOT 3ⁿ + 9.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = x³ - 5x + 1
Which of these intervals contains a solution of f(x) = 0?
ms: f(0) = 1 and f(1) = -3: the sign changes, so a solution lies between 0 and 1. f(-1) = 5, f(2) = -1, f(3) = 13, f(4) = 45, so the other intervals have no sign change.
questions.tip: Only a CHANGE of sign proves a root. f(1) = -3 and f(2) = -1 are both negative, so 1 to 2 is not proved.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Show that the equation x³ = 6x - 2 has a solution between x = 2 and x = 3.
questions.answer: Let f(x) = x³ - 6x + 2. f(2) = -2 < 0, f(3) = 11 > 0; change of sign so there is a solution between 2 and 3
ms: M1 for rearranging to x³ - 6x + 2 = 0 and finding f(2) = -2 and f(3) = 11
A1 for stating there is a change of sign (so a solution lies between 2 and 3)
questions.tip: Rearrange to = 0 first. Substituting into x³ and 6x - 2 separately and comparing is harder to justify. Write the words 'change of sign'.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Show that the equation x³ = 4x + 1 can be rearranged to give x = √(4 + 1/x)
questions.answer: Divide by x: x² = 4 + 1/x, then square-root: x = √(4 + 1/x)
ms: M1 for dividing every term by x: x² = 4 + 1/x
A1 for square-rooting to x = √(4 + 1/x) with all steps shown
questions.tip: Divide EVERY term by x: 4x ÷ x = 4 and 1 ÷ x = 1/x. Show each step in a 'show that'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Using xₙ₊₁ = 2 + 3/xₙ with x₀ = 1, find the values of x₁, x₂ and x₃.
Give x₂ and x₃ as fractions.
questions.tip: Use the previous value each time: x₃ = 2 + 3 ÷ (13/5) = 2 + 15/13. Dividing by a fraction means multiply by its reciprocal.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The iteration xₙ₊₁ = ∛(2xₙ + 7) converges to a value α.
Which equation has α as a solution?
ms: At the limit x = ∛(2x + 7), so x³ = 2x + 7, giving x³ - 2x - 7 = 0.
questions.tip: Replace both xₙ₊₁ and xₙ with x, then undo the cube root by cubing both sides.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Using xₙ₊₁ = (xₙ)²/4 + 1 with x₀ = 0,
(a) find the values of x₁, x₂ and x₃, giving each as a fraction. (3)
The values of xₙ converge to α.
(b) By forming and solving an equation, find the exact value of α. (2)
ms: M1 for x = x²/4 + 1 leading to x² - 4x + 4 = 0
questions.tip: (5/4)² = 25/16, then 25/16 ÷ 4 = 25/64. Square the whole fraction before dividing by 4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Show that the equation x³ - 3x + 1 = 0 has three solutions between x = -2 and x = 2.
State the pair of consecutive integers that each solution lies between.
questions.answer: f(-2) = -1, f(-1) = 3, f(0) = 1, f(1) = -1, f(2) = 3. Sign changes between -2 and -1, between 0 and 1, and between 1 and 2
ms: M1 for evaluating f at x = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 (at least 4 correct)
A1 for all five values correct: -1, 3, 1, -1, 3
B1 for identifying the three sign changes
B1 for the intervals -2 to -1, 0 to 1, and 1 to 2
questions.tip: Check every integer, not just the ends. Between -1 and 0 there is no sign change (3 and 1 are both positive).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (a) Show that the equation x² - 7x + 3 = 0 can be rearranged to give x = 7 - 3/x (1)
(b) Using xₙ₊₁ = 7 - 3/xₙ with x₀ = 1, find x₁ and x₂. Give x₂ as a fraction. (2)
(c) The iteration converges to the larger solution of x² - 7x + 3 = 0. Find the exact value of this solution. (2)
ms: B1 for dividing every term by x and rearranging
M1 for correct substitution into the formula: (7 ± √(49 - 12))/2
questions.tip: In (c) pick the + sign for the larger root, and check: (7 + √37)/2 is about 6.5, close to 25/4 = 6.25.

questions.q:
[Calculator] Using xₙ₊₁ = √(5 + 2/xₙ) with x₀ = 2, find the values of x₁, x₂ and x₃.
Give each answer to 4 decimal places.
questions.tip: Use the full calculator value of each answer (the ANS key) for the next step, and put the whole of 5 + 2/xₙ under the square root.

questions.q:
[Calculator] The equation x³ - 2x² - 5 = 0 has a solution between x = 2 and x = 3.
Use a decimal search to find this solution correct to 1 decimal place. You must show your working.
questions.answer: f(2.6) = -0.944 < 0 and f(2.7) = 0.103 > 0, so the solution is between 2.6 and 2.7. f(2.65) = -0.435 < 0, so it is between 2.65 and 2.7: x = 2.7 to 1 d.p.
ms: M1 for evaluating f(x) for at least two values between 2 and 3, e.g. f(2.6) = -0.944, f(2.7) = 0.103
M1 for identifying the sign change between 2.6 and 2.7
A1 for evaluating f(2.65) = -0.435 (negative) and concluding x = 2.7 to 1 d.p.
questions.tip: Finding the sign change between 2.6 and 2.7 is not enough: you must test 2.65 to know which way it rounds.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find the gradient of the line through (1, 7) and (4, -2).
questions.tip: Change in y over change in x, subtracting in the same order on top and bottom.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The line L has equation y = 5 - 2x.
(a) Write down the gradient and the y-intercept of L. (1)
(b) Does the point (3, -1) lie on L? Show how you decide. (1)
ms: B1 for substituting x = 3 to get y = -1, so yes
questions.tip: The gradient is the number in front of x, including its sign: -2, not 5.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A line has gradient 3 and passes through the point (-1, 4).
(a) Find the equation of the line. (2)
(b) Find the coordinates of the point where the line crosses the x-axis. (1)
questions.tip: Substitute carefully: 3 × (-1) = -3, so c = 4 + 3 = 7.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which line is perpendicular to 2x + 5y = 10?
ms: 5y = -2x + 10, so the gradient is -2/5. The perpendicular gradient is the negative reciprocal, 5/2.
questions.tip: Rearrange to y = mx + c first. Flip AND change the sign for perpendicular.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Show that the lines 3y = 2x + 6 and 4y + 6x = 1 are perpendicular.
ms: M1 for rearranging one line to find its gradient: 2/3 or -3/2
A1 for showing the product is -1 (or one is the negative reciprocal of the other) with a conclusion
questions.tip: 4y + 6x = 1 gives y = -(6/4)x + 1/4, so the gradient is -3/2. Divide every term by 4.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Find the coordinates of the point where the lines y = 2x - 3 and x + 3y = 12 intersect.
questions.tip: 3(2x - 3) = 6x - 9. Then find y by putting x back into the simpler equation.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A is the point (1, 2), B is the point (7, 6) and C is the point (5, k).
AB is perpendicular to BC.
Find the value of k.
ms: M1 for gradient of BC = -3/2 and (k - 6)/(5 - 7) = -3/2
questions.tip: The gradient of BC uses B and C: (k - 6)/(5 - 7) = (k - 6)/(-2). Watch the negative denominator.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The line L has equation y = 4 - x/2.
The line M passes through the origin and is perpendicular to L.
L and M meet at the point C.
Find the coordinates of C.
questions.tip: Perpendicular to gradient -1/2 is gradient 2. Through the origin means c = 0.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A is the point (-1, 4) and B is the point (5, 1).
The line L passes through (2, -3) and is perpendicular to AB.
Find the coordinates of the point where L crosses the x-axis.
questions.tip: Find the gradient of AB first, then the negative reciprocal. Set y = 0 to find where L crosses the x-axis.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The lines y = 3x + 2 and ky = x - 4 are perpendicular.
Find the value of k.
ms: ky = x - 4 has gradient 1/k. 3 × 1/k = -1 gives k = -3.
questions.tip: Divide by k to get y on its own before reading off the gradient.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] What is the equation of the line of symmetry of y = x² - 8x + 5?
ms: x² - 8x + 5 = (x - 4)² - 11, so the line of symmetry is x = 4.
questions.tip: The line of symmetry is vertical, so it is 'x = ...'. Halve the x coefficient and change its sign.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y = x² + 2x - 15
Find the coordinates of the points where the graph crosses the axes.
questions.tip: Don't forget the y-intercept: put x = 0 to get (0, -15).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] By completing the square, find the coordinates of the turning point of y = x² - 5x + 2.

[Non-calculator] A quadratic graph has equation y = x² + bx + c. Its turning point is (-3, 4).
Which is its equation?
questions.tip: Turning point (-3, 4) means (x + 3)², not (x - 3)². Expand the bracket fully before adding 4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y = (x - 1)(x - 7)
Find the coordinates of
(a) the points where the graph crosses the x-axis (1)
(b) the point where the graph crosses the y-axis (1)
(c) the turning point. (2)
ms: M1 for x = 4 (midway between the roots)
questions.tip: The turning point is halfway between the roots. Substitute x = 4: (3)(-3) = -9.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The graph of y = x² - 4x - 1 has been drawn.
Find the equation of the straight line that should be drawn on the same axes to solve x² - 6x + 2 = 0
ms: M1 for adding 2x - 3 to both sides of x² - 6x + 2 = 0 to get x² - 4x - 1 = 2x - 3, or for subtracting (x² - 6x + 2) from (x² - 4x - 1)
questions.tip: Rearrange the new equation so the left side is the curve you already have: x² - 4x - 1 = 2x - 3.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] (a) Write 3x² - 12x + 5 in the form a(x - p)² + q. (3)
(b) Write down the coordinates of the turning point of y = 3x² - 12x + 5 and state whether it is a maximum or a minimum. (1)
questions.tip: When the 3 is outside, -4 inside the bracket becomes -12 outside: -12 + 5 = -7.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A quadratic graph has equation y = x² + bx + c.
Its turning point is at (2, -9).
(a) Find the values of b and c. (2)
(b) Find the coordinates of the points where the graph crosses the x-axis. (2)
questions.tip: Use the completed square form directly: (x - 2)² - 9, then expand. For the roots, (x - 2) = ±3.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y = x² + 6x + 4
Find the coordinates of the turning point and the exact x-coordinates of the points where the graph crosses the x-axis.
questions.tip: Once you have (x + 3)² - 5, the roots come straight from it: x + 3 = ±√5. 'Exact' means surds, not decimals.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y = 8 + 2x - x²
(a) Find the coordinates of the turning point and state whether it is a maximum or minimum. (3)
(b) Find where the graph crosses the x-axis. (1)
questions.tip: A negative x² term makes an ∩ shape, so the turning point is a maximum. Factor out -1 carefully.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Describe the transformation that maps y = f(x) onto y = f(x + 4).
ms: f(x + a) is a translation by a units in the NEGATIVE x direction: vector (-4, 0).
questions.tip: Inside the bracket does the opposite of what you expect: + 4 moves the graph LEFT.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The point (3, 8) lies on the curve y = f(x).
Write down the coordinates of the image of this point on
(a) y = f(x) - 5 (1)
(b) y = f(x + 1) (1)
questions.tip: Outside changes y as you expect; inside changes x the opposite way: f(x + 1) moves 1 left.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The graph of y = x² is translated 2 units to the right and 3 units down.
Find the equation of the new graph in the form y = x² + bx + c.
questions.tip: Right 2 means (x - 2), not (x + 2). Expand and then subtract 3.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The curve y = f(x) has a maximum point at (-1, 6).
What is the turning point of y = -f(x)?
ms: -f(x) reflects in the x-axis: (x, y) to (x, -y). A maximum becomes a minimum at (-1, -6).
questions.tip: -f(x) changes the y-coordinate only. Reflecting a maximum upside down makes it a minimum.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] For 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°, the graph of y = sin x has a maximum point at (90°, 1).
Write down the coordinates of the maximum point, for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°, of
(a) y = sin(x + 45°) (1)
(b) y = -sin x (1)
questions.tip: sin(x + 45°) shifts the graph 45° LEFT. For -sin x, the old minimum at (270°, -1) becomes the maximum.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The graph of y = x² is reflected in the x-axis and then translated 3 units up.
(a) Write down the equation of the new graph. (1)
(b) Find the exact x-coordinates of the points where the new graph crosses the x-axis. (2)
questions.tip: Reflect first (y = -x²), then add 3. Doing it in the other order gives y = -(x² + 3), a different graph.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The curve y = f(x) crosses the x-axis only at x = -2 and x = 5.
Write down the x-coordinates of the points where each of these curves crosses the x-axis.
(a) y = f(x - 3) (1)
(b) y = f(-x) (1)
questions.tip: f(x - 3) moves the graph 3 RIGHT, so add 3. f(-x) reflects in the y-axis, so change the sign of each x.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The curve y = f(x) passes through the points A(1, 4), B(3, 0) and C(5, -2).
The curve is transformed to y = -f(x - 2).
Write down the coordinates of the images of A, B and C.
questions.tip: Apply both changes to each point: f(x - 2) adds 2 to x, and the minus outside changes the sign of y.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] f(x) = x² - 6x + 10
g(x) = f(x + 3)
(a) Show that g(x) = x² + 1. (2)
(b) Describe the transformation that maps y = f(x) onto y = g(x), and write down the turning point of y = g(x). (2)
questions.answer: (a) (x + 3)² - 6(x + 3) + 10 = x² + 1 (b) translation 3 units left (vector (-3, 0)); turning point (0, 1)
questions.tip: Replace EVERY x with (x + 3), including the one in -6x: -6(x + 3) = -6x - 18.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] For 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°, a graph has a maximum point at (0°, 3) and a minimum point at (180°, 1).
Which could be its equation?
ms: cos x has max (0°, 1) and min (180°, -1). Adding 2 moves these up to (0°, 3) and (180°, 1).
questions.tip: -cos x + 2 has its maximum at 180° instead. cos(x + 2) is a sideways shift, not a vertical one.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which is the equation of the circle with centre (0, 0) that passes through the point (5, -12)?
questions.tip: The equation uses r², not r. (-12)² = +144.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The circle C has equation x² + y² = 50.
(a) Show that the point (-5, 5) lies on C. (1)
(b) Find the radius of C. Give your answer as a surd in its simplest form. (1)
questions.tip: √50 = √25 × √2 = 5√2. Leaving √50 is not simplest form.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The point P(5, -12) lies on the circle x² + y² = 169.
Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at P.
Give your answer in the form ax + by = c, where a, b and c are integers.
ms: M1 for tangent gradient 5/12 and y + 12 = (5/12)(x - 5)
questions.tip: The tangent is perpendicular to the RADIUS OP. Multiply by 12 to clear the fraction and rearrange.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The point (2, 6) lies on the circle x² + y² = 40.
What is the gradient of the tangent to the circle at (2, 6)?
ms: Gradient of the radius = 6/2 = 3, so the tangent gradient is -1/3.
questions.tip: 3 is the gradient of the radius, not the tangent. Take the negative reciprocal.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The line x = 3 meets the circle x² + y² = 25 at the points A and B.
(a) Find the coordinates of A and B. (2)
(b) Find the length of AB. (1)
questions.tip: y² = 16 gives y = 4 AND y = -4. One answer only loses a mark.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The point (k, 4) lies on the circle x² + y² = 41, where k < 0.
(a) Find the value of k. (2)
(b) Find the equation of the tangent to the circle at (k, 4). Give your answer in the form y = mx + c. (3)
ms: M1 for tangent gradient 5/4 and y - 4 = (5/4)(x + 5)
questions.tip: Read the condition k < 0 so you take k = -5, not 5. Then x - (-5) = x + 5.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The points P(3, 4) and Q(3, -4) lie on the circle x² + y² = 25.
The tangent at P and the tangent at Q meet at the point T.
Find the coordinates of T.
ms: M1 for gradient of OP = 4/3 so tangent at P has gradient -3/4
M1 for tangent at P: y - 4 = -(3/4)(x - 3) or 3x + 4y = 25
questions.tip: By symmetry T lies on the x-axis, which is a good check, but you still need the working.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The line y = 2x + c is a tangent to the circle x² + y² = 5.
Find the two possible values of c.
ms: M1 for the radius to the point of contact having gradient -1/2
M1 for the point of contact being (2, -1) or (-2, 1) (on the line y = -x/2 and the circle)
M1 for substituting a point into y = 2x + c
questions.tip: The radius at the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent, so it lies on y = -x/2. Find where this meets the circle.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The points A(-3, 4) and B(4, 3) lie on the circle x² + y² = 25.
Show that the perpendicular bisector of AB passes through the centre of the circle.
questions.answer: Midpoint (1/2, 7/2), gradient AB = -1/7, perpendicular gradient 7, line y = 7x, which passes through (0, 0)
ms: A1 for simplifying to y = 7x and stating it passes through the centre (0, 0)
questions.tip: The centre is the origin, so you need the line to have c = 0. Show the simplification to y = 7x.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] P is a point on the circle x² + y² = 10.
The tangent to the circle at P has gradient 3, and P is in the fourth quadrant (x > 0, y < 0).
What are the coordinates of P?
ms: The radius OP is perpendicular to the tangent, so it has gradient -1/3 and lies on y = -x/3. Substituting: x² + x²/9 = 10 gives x² = 9, and x > 0 gives P(3, -1).
questions.tip: The radius gradient is the negative reciprocal of the tangent gradient (-1/3), not 3. (-3, 1) also has tangent gradient 3 but is in the wrong quadrant.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A velocity-time graph is a straight line from (0, 4) to (10, 24), where time is in seconds and velocity in m/s.
What is the acceleration?
questions.tip: Use the CHANGE in velocity (24 - 4), not the final velocity 24.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A distance-time graph for a runner has three straight sections:
from (0 minutes, 0 km) to (20 minutes, 3 km), then horizontal to (30 minutes, 3 km), then from (30 minutes, 3 km) back to (45 minutes, 0 km).
(a) Work out the speed for the first 20 minutes in km/h. (1)
(b) Work out the speed on the way back in km/h. (1)
questions.tip: Convert minutes to hours: 20 minutes is 1/3 hour, so 3 ÷ 1/3 = 9 km/h.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The velocity, v m/s, of an object t seconds after it starts is shown in the table.
t: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4
v: 0 | 3 | 8 | 15 | 24
The velocity-time graph is a smooth curve that bends upwards (it gets steeper as t increases).
(a) Use 4 strips of equal width to estimate the distance travelled in the first 4 seconds. (3)
(b) Is your answer an overestimate or an underestimate? Give a reason. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 38 m (b) overestimate: the curve bends upwards so the trapezium tops lie above the curve
ms: M1 for using trapezia with width 1
M1 for 1/2 × 1 × (0 + 24 + 2(3 + 8 + 15)) or the sum of 4 trapezium areas: 1.5 + 5.5 + 11.5 + 19.5
B1 for overestimate with a reason referring to the trapezium tops being above the curve
questions.tip: Strip width is 1, not 4. In the trapezium rule the first and last heights are counted once, the middle ones twice.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A velocity-time graph is horizontal at 15 m/s from t = 0 to t = 8 seconds.
How far does the object travel in this time?
ms: Distance = area under the graph = 15 × 8 = 120 m.
questions.tip: A horizontal line on a VELOCITY-time graph means constant speed, not stationary.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A car is travelling at 5 m/s. It then accelerates uniformly for 6 seconds and travels 66 m in that time.
(a) Work out the speed of the car at the end of the 6 seconds. (2)
(b) Work out the acceleration. (1)
ms: M1 for (5 + v)/2 × 6 = 66 (area of trapezium under the velocity-time graph)
questions.tip: The area under the graph is a trapezium, not a triangle, because the car does not start from rest: (5 + v)/2 × 6.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A curved distance-time graph shows a cyclist's journey (distance in metres, time in seconds).
A tangent is drawn to the curve at t = 4. The tangent passes through the points (2, 5) and (8, 26).
Estimate the speed of the cyclist at t = 4.
questions.tip: The gradient of a TANGENT gives the speed at an instant. A chord from the origin gives the average speed instead.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The velocity of a particle, v m/s, after t seconds is given by v = 20 - t², for 0 ≤ t ≤ 3.
(a) Use 3 strips of equal width to estimate the distance travelled in the first 3 seconds. (3)
(b) The graph of v = 20 - t² bends downwards. Is your estimate an overestimate or underestimate? Give a reason. (1)
questions.answer: (a) 50.5 m (b) underestimate: the curve is above the tops of the trapezia
ms: B1 for underestimate because the trapezia lie below the curve
questions.tip: Work out each v value carefully: at t = 3, v = 20 - 9 = 11. Check concavity before deciding over or under.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Water flows into a tank. The rate of flow, r litres per minute, t minutes after the start is shown in the table.
t: 0 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10
r: 4 | 7 | 9 | 10 | 8 | 3
(a) Use 5 strips of equal width to estimate the area under the graph of r against t for 0 ≤ t ≤ 10. (3)
(b) What does this area represent? (1)
questions.answer: (a) 75 (b) the total volume of water (in litres) that flows into the tank in the 10 minutes
ms: M1 for using strips of width 2
B1 for total volume of water in litres
questions.tip: Area = rate × time, so the units are litres per minute × minutes = litres.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A car travels at a constant speed of 12 m/s for T seconds. It then decelerates uniformly to rest in 8 seconds.
The total distance travelled is 252 m.
Work out the value of T.
questions.tip: The decelerating section is a triangle: 1/2 × 8 × 12 = 48 m. Don't use 8 × 12.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] On a velocity-time graph, between t = 10 and t = 15 the line has a negative gradient but the velocity stays above zero.
What is the object doing?
options: Slowing down but still moving forwards
ms: Negative gradient means negative acceleration (deceleration). Positive velocity means it is still moving forwards.
questions.tip: Don't read a velocity-time graph like a distance-time graph. Moving backwards needs v below zero.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A graph passes through (0, 1), is always above the x-axis and gets steeper as x increases.
Which could be its equation?
ms: y = 3ˣ is exponential: 3⁰ = 1, it is always positive and it grows faster and faster.
questions.tip: y = x³ passes through (0, 0) and goes negative. Exponential graphs never touch the x-axis.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Complete the table of values for y = 2/x
x: -2 | -1 | 1/2 | 1 | 4
y: ? | ? | ? | ? | ?
ms: B1 for at least 3 values correct
questions.tip: 2 ÷ 1/2 = 4, not 1. Dividing by a fraction less than 1 makes the answer bigger.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The graph of y = (x + 2)(x - 1)(x - 4) is drawn.
(a) Write down the x-coordinates of the points where it crosses the x-axis. (1)
(b) Find the coordinates of the point where it crosses the y-axis. (1)
(c) Using a sketch, write down the values of x for which y < 0. (1)
ms: B1 for x < -2 or 1 < x < 4 (both parts needed)
questions.tip: A positive x³ cubic starts bottom-left and ends top-right, so it is below the axis to the left of -2 and between 1 and 4. At x = 0: (2)(-1)(-4) = +8.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Which describes the graph of y = x²(x - 3) at the x-axis?
options: It crosses at x = 0 and touches at x = 3
It touches at x = 0 and crosses at x = 3
It crosses at x = -3, x = 0 and x = 3
ms: x² gives a repeated root at x = 0, so the curve touches the axis there. (x - 3) gives a single root where it crosses.
questions.tip: A squared factor means a repeated root: the curve touches the x-axis and turns back.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y = 5 × 2ˣ
(a) Find the value of y when x = 3. (1)
(b) Find the value of x when y = 5/4. (2)
questions.tip: Work out 2³ first, THEN multiply by 5. Don't multiply 5 × 2 first to get 10³.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A cubic graph crosses the x-axis at x = -1, x = 2 and x = 3 and crosses the y-axis at (0, 6).
Find the equation of the graph in the form y = ax³ + bx² + cx + d.
questions.tip: A root at x = -1 gives the factor (x + 1). Always check the y-intercept to find any multiplier.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The number of bacteria, P, after t hours is given by P = 200 × 3ᵗ.
After how many whole hours does the number of bacteria first exceed 10 000?
ms: M1 for trying values, e.g. t = 3 gives 5400
questions.tip: Show the values either side: 5400 at t = 3 and 16 200 at t = 4.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The value of a car, £V, t years after it was bought is modelled by V = abᵗ, where a and b are constants.
After 1 year the car is worth £16 000. After 3 years the car is worth £10 240.
(a) Find the values of a and b. (3)
(b) Write down the value of the car when it was bought. (1)
(c) By what percentage does the value fall each year? (1)
questions.tip: Divide the equations to eliminate a. b = 0.8 means 80% is kept each year, so the value falls by 20%.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The graph of y = x³ - 4x has been drawn.
Find the equation of the straight line that should be drawn on the same axes to solve x³ - 6x + 1 = 0.
questions.tip: Get x³ - 4x on its own on one side. Everything left over on the other side is the line.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] y = 8ˣ
Find the value of x when y = 1/2.
questions.tip: A negative power gives a reciprocal and a fractional power gives a root: 8^(1/3) = 2.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Each exterior angle of a regular polygon is 24°. What is the sum of its interior angles?
ms: Number of sides = 360 ÷ 24 = 15. Sum of interior angles = (15 - 2) × 180 = 13 × 180 = 2340°.
questions.tip: 2700° comes from 15 × 180. The sum is (n - 2) × 180, so subtract 2 from the number of sides first.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two straight lines AB and CD cross at the point X. Angle AXC = (3x + 12)° and angle BXD = (5x - 20)°.
(a) Work out the value of x.
(b) Work out the size of angle AXD.
Give reasons for your answers.
questions.answer: (a) x = 16 (vertically opposite angles are equal: 3x + 12 = 5x - 20). (b) Angle AXC = 60°, so angle AXD = 180° - 60° = 120° (angles on a straight line add up to 180°).
ms: M1 for 3x + 12 = 5x - 20 with the reason 'vertically opposite angles are equal'
B1 for angle AXD = 120° with the reason 'angles on a straight line add up to 180°' (ft their AXC)
questions.tip: Angles AXC and BXD are vertically opposite, so they are EQUAL. Do not add them to 180°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] AB and CD are two parallel horizontal lines, with AB above CD. A is to the left of B and C is to the left of D. A point E lies between the two lines, to the left of both B and D, and is joined to B and to D.
Angle ABE = 38° and angle CDE = 47°.
Show that angle BED = 85°. Give reasons for each stage of your working.
questions.answer: Draw a line through E parallel to AB (and so parallel to CD). The angle between EB and this line is 38° (alternate angles are equal). The angle between ED and this line is 47° (alternate angles are equal). So angle BED = 38° + 47° = 85°.
ms: M1 for drawing (or describing) a line through E parallel to AB and CD
M1 for identifying 38° and 47° as the two parts of angle BED
A1 for 85° with the reason 'alternate angles are equal' (both times)
questions.tip: You must add a construction line through E. Write 'alternate angles are equal', not 'Z angles'.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The interior angles of a polygon add up to 1980°. How many sides does the polygon have?
questions.tip: 1980 ÷ 180 = 11 gives n - 2, not n. Remember to add the 2 back on.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A square, a regular hexagon and a regular polygon with n sides all meet at a single point. They fit together around the point with no gaps and no overlaps.
Work out the value of n. Give reasons.
ms: M1 for 360 - 90 - 120 = 150° (angles around a point add up to 360°)
questions.tip: The hexagon's interior angle is 120°, not 60°. 60° is its exterior angle.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In triangle PQR, PQ = PR. Angle QPR = x° and angle PQR = (2x + 15)°.
Work out the value of x. Give reasons for your answer.
ms: B1 for angle PRQ = 2x + 15 (base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal)
M1 for x + 2(2x + 15) = 180 (angles in a triangle add up to 180°)
questions.tip: PQ = PR means the equal angles are at Q and R (opposite the equal sides), not at P.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Explain why it is not possible for a regular polygon to have an interior angle of 130°.
questions.answer: The exterior angle would be 180° - 130° = 50°. The number of sides would be 360 ÷ 50 = 7.2, which is not a whole number, so no such regular polygon exists.
ms: A1 for 7.2 and a statement that the number of sides must be a whole number
questions.tip: Just saying '360 does not divide by 130' gets no marks. Use the EXTERIOR angle.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCDE is a regular pentagon. F is a point inside the pentagon so that ABF is an equilateral triangle.
(a) Work out the size of angle AEF.
(b) Work out the size of angle DEF.
Give reasons for each stage of your working.
ms: B1 for interior angle of a regular pentagon = 108° (from (5 - 2) × 180 ÷ 5)
M1 for angle FAE = 108 - 60 = 48° (angles in an equilateral triangle are 60°)
M1 for recognising AF = AB = AE so triangle AEF is isosceles
questions.tip: The key step is spotting AF = AE (both equal to a side of the pentagon). Without it you cannot find angle AEF.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCD is a quadrilateral. AB is parallel to DC. Angle DAB = angle BCD.
Prove that AD is parallel to BC.
questions.answer: Let angle DAB = angle BCD = x. AB is parallel to DC, so angle ADC = 180° - x (co-interior angles add up to 180°). Then angle BCD + angle ADC = x + 180 - x = 180°. These are co-interior angles between AD and BC with DC as the transversal, and they add up to 180°, so AD is parallel to BC.
ms: M1 for angle ADC = 180° - angle DAB with reason 'co-interior angles add up to 180°'
M1 for showing angle BCD + angle ADC = 180°
A1 for concluding AD is parallel to BC because co-interior angles add to 180° (full reasons needed)
questions.tip: In a proof you must say which lines and which angles. 'Co-interior angles add to 180° so the lines are parallel' is the reason the examiner wants.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In triangle ABC, angle BAC = 70°. The bisector of angle ABC and the bisector of angle ACB meet at the point I.
Show that angle BIC = 125°. Give reasons.
questions.answer: Angle ABC + angle ACB = 180 - 70 = 110° (angles in a triangle). The bisectors halve these, so angle IBC + angle ICB = 55°. In triangle BIC, angle BIC = 180 - 55 = 125° (angles in a triangle).
ms: M1 for angle ABC + angle ACB = 110° (angles in a triangle add up to 180°)
M1 for angle IBC + angle ICB = 110 ÷ 2 = 55°
A1 for angle BIC = 125° with reason angles in triangle BIC add up to 180°
questions.tip: You do not know angles B and C separately, and you do not need to. Work with their SUM.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCDEFGH is a regular octagon.
(a) Work out the size of angle BAC.
(b) Show that AD is parallel to BC.
Give reasons for your answers.
questions.answer: (a) 22.5° (b) Interior angles are 135°. ABCD is a quadrilateral with angle ABC = angle BCD = 135°; it is symmetrical (AB = CD), so angle BAD = angle CDA = (360 - 270) ÷ 2 = 45°. Angle BAD + angle ABC = 45 + 135 = 180°, co-interior angles add up to 180°, so AD is parallel to BC.
ms: B1 for interior angle of a regular octagon = 135°
M1 for triangle ABC isosceles (AB = BC) so angle BAC = (180 - 135) ÷ 2
M1 for angle BAD = 45° (angles in quadrilateral ABCD add to 360° and ABCD is symmetrical)
A1 for 45 + 135 = 180 so AD is parallel to BC as co-interior angles add to 180°
questions.tip: Sides of a regular polygon are equal, so triangles like ABC are isosceles. State it.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Regular polygon A has n sides. Regular polygon B has (n + 2) sides.
Each exterior angle of A is 6° larger than each exterior angle of B.
Work out the value of n.
questions.tip: Reject the negative root and say why: a polygon cannot have a negative number of sides.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A and B are points on a circle with centre O. Angle OAB = 32°. C is a point on the MINOR arc AB. What is the size of angle ACB?
ms: OA = OB (radii), so angle OBA = 32° and angle AOB = 180 - 64 = 116°. Reflex angle AOB = 360 - 116 = 244°, and angle ACB = 244 ÷ 2 = 122° (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference).
questions.tip: C is on the minor arc, so angle ACB is half the REFLEX angle at O. 58° is the angle for a point on the major arc.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A circle has centre O. The line PT is a tangent to the circle at the point T. Angle TOP = 58°.
Work out the size of angle OPT. Give reasons for your answer.
ms: B1 for angle OTP = 90° with reason 'a tangent is perpendicular to the radius (at the point of contact)'
B1 for angle OPT = 180 - 90 - 58 = 32° (angles in a triangle add up to 180°)
questions.tip: Write the full reason: 'tangent meets radius at 90°'. Just '90°' is not a reason.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B, C and D are points on a circle, in that order, so ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral. The side DC is extended beyond C to the point E. Angle BCE = 78°.
Work out the size of angle DAB. Give reasons for your answer.
ms: B1 for angle BCD = 180 - 78 = 102° (angles on a straight line add up to 180°)
B1 for angle DAB = 180 - 102 = 78° (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral add up to 180°)
questions.tip: The exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior opposite angle. Show both steps with reasons.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A circle has centre O and radius 10 cm. AB and CD are parallel chords on opposite sides of O. AB = 16 cm and CD = 12 cm.
Work out the distance between the two chords. Give a reason for any circle fact you use.
questions.answer: 14 cm (AB is 6 cm from O and CD is 8 cm from O)
ms: B1 for stating the perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord (so the half-chords are 8 cm and 6 cm)
questions.tip: The chords are on OPPOSITE sides of the centre, so add the two distances. If they were on the same side you would subtract (8 - 6 = 2 cm).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B and C are points on a circle with BA = BC. The line TBS is the tangent to the circle at B, with T on the same side of B as A. Angle TBA = 65°.
Work out the size of angle ABC. Give reasons for each stage of your working.
ms: B1 for angle BCA = 65° with reason 'alternate segment theorem' (angle between tangent and chord equals angle in the alternate segment)
B1 for angle BAC = 65° with reason 'base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal'
B1 for angle ABC = 180 - 130 = 50° (angles in a triangle add up to 180°)
questions.tip: Name the alternate segment theorem in full. Make sure you pair the tangent angle with the angle in the OTHER segment.

questions.q:
