[Non-calculator] A, B, C and D are points on a circle, in that order. The chords AC and BD are drawn.
Angle BAC = (2x + 10)° and angle BDC = (70 - x)°. Angle ABD = (3x - 5)°.
(a) Work out the value of x.
(b) Work out the size of angle ACD.
Give reasons for your answers.
ms: M1 for 2x + 10 = 70 - x with reason 'angles in the same segment are equal'
M1 for angle ACD = angle ABD (angles in the same segment are equal, both subtended by AD)
questions.tip: Angles in the same segment must stand on the same chord. BAC and BDC both stand on BC.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] AB is a diameter of a circle with centre O, and C is a point on the circumference. Angle CAB = 2x and angle OCB = 3x. What is the value of x?
ms: OB = OC (radii), so angle OBC = angle OCB = 3x. Angle ACB = 90° (angle in a semicircle), so in triangle ABC: 2x + 3x + 90 = 180, 5x = 90, x = 18°.
questions.tip: Spot the isosceles triangle OBC first, so angle CBA is also 3x. 36° comes from 5x = 180, forgetting the 90° at C.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A and B are points on a circle with centre O. TA is the tangent to the circle at A. C is a point on the major arc AB. Angle TAB = x, where T is on the same side of AB as the minor arc.
Prove that angle ACB = x. You must not use the alternate segment theorem in your proof.
questions.answer: Angle OAT = 90° (tangent perpendicular to radius), so angle OAB = 90 - x. OA = OB (radii), so angle OBA = 90 - x (base angles of isosceles triangle). Angle AOB = 180 - 2(90 - x) = 2x (angles in a triangle). Angle ACB = 2x ÷ 2 = x (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference).
ms: M1 for angle OAB = 90° - x with reason tangent perpendicular to radius
M1 for angle OBA = 90° - x with reason radii equal / isosceles triangle
M1 for angle AOB = 2x (angles in a triangle add up to 180°)
A1 for angle ACB = x with reason 'angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference'
questions.tip: A proof needs a reason on EVERY line. Use algebra (x), not a number.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The straight line PAQ is the tangent to a circle at A. B and C are points on the circle and BC is a diameter. P is on the same side of A as B. Angle PAB = 34°.
(a) Work out the size of angle ABC.
(b) Work out the size of angle QAC.
Give reasons for each stage of your working.
ms: B1 for angle ACB = 34° with reason 'alternate segment theorem'
B1 for angle BAC = 90° with reason 'angle in a semicircle is 90°'
B1 for angle ABC = 180 - 90 - 34 = 56° (angles in a triangle)
B1 for angle QAC = 180 - 34 - 90 = 56° (angles on a straight line) or by the alternate segment theorem
questions.tip: BC is a diameter: always look for the 90° angle in the semicircle.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B, C and D are points on a circle. Prove that angle ACB = angle ADB, where C and D are on the same side of the chord AB.
You may use the theorem that the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.
questions.answer: Let O be the centre. Angle AOB = 2 × angle ACB (angle at centre is twice angle at circumference). Also angle AOB = 2 × angle ADB (same theorem, same arc AB). So 2 × angle ACB = 2 × angle ADB, giving angle ACB = angle ADB.
ms: M1 for joining OA and OB and stating angle AOB = 2 × angle ACB
M1 for angle AOB = 2 × angle ADB
A1 for concluding angle ACB = angle ADB with reasons
questions.tip: Introduce the centre O yourself and state the theorem in words both times.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] PA and PB are tangents to a circle with centre O, touching the circle at A and B. C is a point on the major arc AB. Angle APB = x.
Prove that angle ACB = 90° - x/2.
questions.answer: Angle OAP = angle OBP = 90° (tangent perpendicular to radius). Angles in quadrilateral OAPB add up to 360°, so angle AOB = 360 - 90 - 90 - x = 180 - x. Angle ACB = (180 - x) ÷ 2 = 90 - x/2 (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference).
ms: B1 for angle OAP = angle OBP = 90° with reason
M1 for angle AOB = 360 - 180 - x (angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360°)
M1 for halving angle AOB with reason 'angle at centre is twice angle at circumference'
questions.tip: OAPB is a quadrilateral, so its angles add to 360°, not 180°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B and C are points on a circle with centre O. O lies inside triangle ABC. D is a point on the minor arc AC.
Angle OAB = 20° and angle OCB = 35°.
(a) Work out the size of angle AOC.
(b) Work out the size of angle ADC.
Give reasons for each stage of your working.
ms: M1 for angle OBA = 20° and angle OBC = 35° (radii equal so triangles OAB and OCB are isosceles)
B1 for angle AOC = 110° (angle at centre is twice angle at circumference)
B1 for angle ADC = 180 - 55 = 125° (opposite angles of cyclic quadrilateral ABCD add up to 180°)
questions.tip: Join OB. Two isosceles triangles appear because OA = OB = OC.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Triangle X has angles 40° and 65°. Triangle Y has angles 65° and 75°. Which statement is correct?
options: You cannot tell without side lengths
They are similar: both have angles 40°, 65° and 75°
They are not similar: only one given angle matches
ms: Third angle of X = 180 - 105 = 75°. Third angle of Y = 180 - 140 = 40°. Same three angles, so similar.
questions.tip: Always work out the third angle before deciding.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two triangles are mathematically similar. The smaller triangle has sides 4 cm, 7 cm and 9 cm. The perimeter of the larger triangle is 50 cm.
Work out the length of the longest side of the larger triangle.
ms: M1 for perimeter of smaller triangle = 20 cm and scale factor 50 ÷ 20 = 2.5
questions.tip: Perimeter is a length, so it scales by the same factor as the sides. Do not square or cube the scale factor.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] AB and CD are parallel line segments. The straight lines AD and BC cross at the point X, with X between A and D and between B and C.
AB = 6 cm, CD = 9 cm, AX = 4 cm and CX = 7.5 cm.
(a) Explain why triangles ABX and DCX are similar.
(b) Work out the length of DX.
(c) Work out the length of BX.
questions.answer: (a) Angle AXB = angle DXC (vertically opposite); angle XAB = angle XDC (alternate angles, AB parallel to CD); so all angles match. (b) 6 cm (c) 5 cm
ms: B1 for two pairs of equal angles with reasons (vertically opposite, alternate)
questions.tip: Match the vertices carefully: A goes with D and B goes with C. Mixing them up gives the wrong pairs of sides.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] PQRS is a kite with PQ = PS and QR = SR.
Prove that triangle PQR is congruent to triangle PSR. Hence explain why angle PQR = angle PSR.
questions.answer: PQ = PS (given), QR = SR (given), PR is common to both triangles. So the triangles are congruent (SSS). Corresponding angles of congruent triangles are equal, so angle PQR = angle PSR.
ms: M1 for two correct pairs of equal sides with reasons
A1 for PR common and conclusion congruent (SSS)
B1 for angle PQR = angle PSR as corresponding angles of congruent triangles
questions.tip: State the condition (SSS) at the end. Giving three facts without naming the condition loses the final mark.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A photo is enlarged so that its area increases by 69%. The enlarged photo is mathematically similar to the original. By what percentage do its lengths increase?
ms: Area scale factor = 1.69. Length scale factor = √1.69 = 1.3, so lengths increase by 30%.
questions.tip: 34.5% just halves the percentage. Turn it into a multiplier (1.69) and square root that.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Two mathematically similar triangles have areas of 18 cm² and 50 cm². A side of the smaller triangle is 6 cm.
Work out the length of the corresponding side of the larger triangle.
questions.tip: Do not multiply the length by 25/9. Lengths use the square root of the area factor.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A model of a car is made using a scale of 1 : 40.
(a) The windscreen of the real car has an area of 1.6 m². Work out the area of the windscreen on the model, in cm².
(b) The fuel tank on the model has a volume of 0.8 cm³. Work out the volume of the real fuel tank in litres.
ms: M1 for 1.6 m² = 16 000 cm² or for dividing by 40² = 1600
questions.tip: Area scale factor is 40² and volume scale factor is 40³. And 1 m² = 10 000 cm², not 100 cm².

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle ABC has a right angle at A. D is the point on BC so that AD is perpendicular to BC. BD = 4 cm and DC = 9 cm.
Work out the length of AD. You must show that any triangles you use are similar.
ms: M1 for showing triangles ABD and CAD are similar: both have a right angle at D, and angle BAD = 90 - angle B = angle ACD (angles in a triangle)
M1 for matching sides: AD/BD = DC/AD
questions.tip: Write the similar triangles with matching vertices in order (A B D with C A D) so the side pairs come out right.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In triangle ABC, D is a point on AB and E is a point on AC so that DE is parallel to BC. AD : DB = 2 : 3.
The area of triangle ADE is 12 cm².
Work out the area of the trapezium DBCE.
ms: M1 for length scale factor AB : AD = 5 : 2
M1 for area of ABC = 12 × 25/4 = 75 cm²
questions.tip: The ratio 2 : 3 is AD : DB, not AD : AB. The whole side AB is 5 parts.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCD is a square. E is a point on BC and F is a point on CD so that BE = CF.
(a) Prove that triangle ABE is congruent to triangle BCF.
(b) Hence prove that AE is perpendicular to BF.
questions.answer: (a) AB = BC (sides of a square), angle ABE = angle BCF = 90° (angles of a square), BE = CF (given): congruent by SAS. (b) Let the lines meet at X. Angle BAE = angle CBF (corresponding angles of congruent triangles). In triangle ABE, angle BAE + angle AEB = 90°, so angle CBF + angle AEB = 90°, so in triangle BXE angle BXE = 180 - 90 = 90°.
ms: B1 for AB = BC and angle ABE = angle BCF = 90° with reasons
B1 for BE = CF and conclusion congruent (SAS)
M1 for angle BAE = angle CBF from congruence
A1 for showing angle BXE = 90° using angles in triangles
questions.tip: For SAS the angle must be BETWEEN the two sides. Here the right angle is between AB and BE, and between BC and CF.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In triangle ABC, D is a point on AC so that angle ABD = angle ACB. AB = 6 cm and AC = 9 cm.
(a) Prove that triangle ABD is similar to triangle ACB.
(b) Work out the length of AD.
(c) Work out the length of DC.
questions.answer: (a) Angle BAD = angle CAB (common angle) and angle ABD = angle ACB (given), so the triangles are similar (AA). (b) 4 cm (c) 5 cm
ms: B1 for common angle at A and the given equal angles, so similar
questions.tip: The triangles are not the 'parallel line' type. Match A with A, B with C, D with B before writing ratios.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCD is a parallelogram. The diagonals AC and BD meet at the point M.
Prove that M is the midpoint of both AC and BD.
questions.answer: Consider triangles ABM and CDM. AB = CD (opposite sides of a parallelogram). Angle BAM = angle DCM (alternate angles, AB parallel to DC). Angle ABM = angle CDM (alternate angles). So the triangles are congruent (ASA). Hence AM = CM and BM = DM, so M is the midpoint of both diagonals.
ms: B1 for AB = CD with reason
B1 for one pair of equal angles with reason 'alternate angles'
B1 for a second pair of equal angles with reason and conclusion congruent (ASA)
B1 for AM = MC and BM = MD so M is the midpoint of both
questions.tip: Choose triangles that contain the bits you want to prove equal (AM, MC, BM, MD).

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 13 cm and one shorter side 5 cm. What is the length of the other shorter side?
questions.tip: √194 comes from adding the squares. When finding a SHORTER side, subtract.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A triangle has sides of length 9 cm, 40 cm and 41 cm.
Show that the triangle is right-angled.
questions.answer: 9² + 40² = 81 + 1600 = 1681 = 41², so by the converse of Pythagoras the triangle is right-angled.
questions.tip: Write a conclusion sentence. Working alone is not 'showing'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A is the point (-3, 4) and B is the point (5, -2).
Work out the length of AB.
questions.tip: Subtracting a negative: 5 - (-3) = 8, not 2.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Work out the exact value of (sin 60°)² + tan 30° × cos 30°.
questions.tip: Learn the exact values cold. A calculator will not be allowed on Paper 1.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] An isosceles triangle has sides of length 10 cm, 10 cm and 12 cm.
Work out the area of the triangle.
ms: M1 for splitting into two right-angled triangles with base 6 cm
questions.tip: The slanted side (10 cm) is not the height. Find the perpendicular height first.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A straight ramp of length 8 m makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal ground.
(a) Work out the vertical height the ramp rises.
(b) Work out the exact horizontal distance covered by the ramp. Give your answer in surd form.
questions.tip: Height is opposite the angle (sin), horizontal is adjacent (cos).

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A right-angled triangle has shorter sides of length 2√3 cm and √6 cm.
Work out the length of the hypotenuse. Give your answer in the form a√2.
questions.tip: (2√3)² = 4 × 3 = 12. Square the 2 as well as the √3.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A cuboid measures 2 cm by 6 cm by h cm. Its space diagonal (the longest straight line that fits inside it) is 11 cm long. What is the value of h?
ms: 2² + 6² + h² = 11², so 4 + 36 + h² = 121, h² = 81 and h = 9 cm.
questions.tip: 3 cm comes from 11 - 2 - 6. Square everything first: the space diagonal d satisfies d² = a² + b² + c².

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A pyramid has a square base ABCD with sides of 4 cm. The apex V is vertically above the centre M of the base, and the perpendicular height VM is 7 cm.
(a) Work out the exact length of the sloping edge VA.
(b) Work out the exact total surface area of the pyramid. Give your answer in the form a + b√53.
ms: M1 for AM² = 2² + 2² = 8 (AM = 2√2, half the diagonal)
M1 for height of a triangular face = √(7² + 2²) = √53 (from V to the midpoint of a base edge)
questions.tip: The edge VA uses half the DIAGONAL (2√2), but the slant height of a face uses half a SIDE (2 cm). Mixing them up is the usual slip.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCD is a quadrilateral made from two right-angled triangles.
Triangle ABC has a right angle at B, angle BAC = 30° and BC = 6 cm.
Triangle ACD has a right angle at C and angle CAD = 45°.
Work out the exact length of AD.
questions.tip: Leave answers in surd form when the question says exact. 16.97 gets no accuracy mark.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In triangle ABC, AB = AC = 8 cm and angle BAC = 120°.
Work out the exact length of BC.
ms: M1 for drawing the perpendicular from A to M, the midpoint of BC, giving angle BAM = 60°
questions.tip: The perpendicular from the top of an isosceles triangle bisects both the base and the top angle.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A vertical tower stands on horizontal ground. Its base is at point O. Point A is 30 m due south of O. Point B is 40 m due east of O. The angle of elevation of the top of the tower from A is 35°.
Work out the angle of elevation of the top of the tower from B. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: Keep the unrounded height (21.006...) in your calculator for the second step. Rounding early can cost the accuracy mark.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A triangle has two sides of 6 cm and 10 cm with an angle of 30° between them. What is its area?
questions.tip: Use sin of the INCLUDED angle. 15√3 comes from using cos 30° by mistake.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The bearing of Q from P is 050°. The bearing of R from P is 140°. PQ = 5 km and PR = 12 km.
(a) Work out the size of angle QPR.
(b) Work out the distance QR.
questions.tip: Spot the right angle first. You do not need the cosine rule when the angle is 90°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In triangle ABC, AB = 5 cm, AC = 8 cm and angle BAC = 60°.
Work out the length of BC.
questions.tip: cos 60° = 1/2, so the last term is 80 × 1/2 = 40. Do it before adding.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In triangle PQR, PQ = 3 cm, PR = 5 cm and angle QPR = 120°.
Work out the length of QR.
questions.tip: cos 120° is NEGATIVE, so minus a negative becomes plus. QR must be longer than both other sides.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] In triangle ABC, angle BAC = 30°, angle ABC = 45° and BC = 6 cm.
Work out the exact length of AC. Give your answer in surd form.
questions.tip: Each side goes with the angle OPPOSITE it: BC is opposite A, and AC is opposite B.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle XYZ has XY = 6 cm, XZ = 8 cm and angle YXZ = 60°.
Work out the exact area of the triangle. Give your answer in the form k√3.
questions.tip: sin 60° = √3/2, not 1/2. Mixing up sin 60° and cos 60° is the most common slip here.

questions.q:
[Calculator] From a lighthouse L, boat A is 6 km away on a bearing of 035°. Boat B is 9 km from L on a bearing of 115°.
Work out the distance between the two boats. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.tip: Subtract the bearings to get the angle at L. Then cosine rule.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Town A is 5 km from town B. The bearing of B from A is 060°. Town C is 5 km due south of B.
Work out the bearing of C from A and the distance AC. Give reasons.
ms: M1 for angle ABC = 60° (alternate angles between the parallel north lines, or bearing of A from B is 240° so the angle between BA and due south is 60°)
M1 for triangle ABC isosceles (AB = BC) with angle 60° so equilateral
questions.tip: Draw a north line at every point. The angle between the two north lines and AB uses co-interior angles.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle ABC has AB = AC = 6 cm and area 9 cm².
Work out the two possible sizes of angle BAC.
questions.tip: sin 30° = sin 150°, and both give a real triangle here. Giving only 30° loses the last mark.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A triangle has sides of length 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm. The angle opposite the 7 cm side is θ.
(a) Show that cos θ = 1/5.
(b) Hence work out the exact area of the triangle. Give your answer in the form a√6.
questions.tip: You cannot find θ without a calculator. Use sin² θ + cos² θ = 1 to get sin θ exactly.

questions.q:
[Calculator] In triangle ABC, AB = 10 cm, BC = 7 cm and angle BAC = 40°.
Work out the two possible sizes of angle ACB. Give your answers to 1 decimal place.
questions.tip: Two different triangles fit this information. The calculator only gives the acute one.

questions.q:
[Calculator] In triangle ABC, AB = 8 cm, AC = 11 cm and angle BAC = 52°. D is the point on BC so that AD is perpendicular to BC.
Work out the length of AD. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.tip: AD is the height using BC as the base. Area = ½ × BC × AD gives a neat route.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A sector has radius 12 cm and angle 75°. What is its arc length?
questions.tip: 24π is the whole circumference. Multiply it by the fraction 75/360 = 5/24.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A quarter circle has radius 6 cm.
(a) Work out the area of the quarter circle. Give your answer in terms of π.
(b) Work out the perimeter of the quarter circle. Give your answer in terms of π.
questions.tip: The perimeter includes the TWO straight radii as well as the curved arc.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A sector of a circle has radius 8.5 cm and angle 72°.
Work out the area of the sector. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.tip: Square the radius before multiplying by π.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A sector has radius 15 cm and arc length 5π cm.
Work out the area of the sector. Give your answer in terms of π.
ms: M1 for angle = 5π ÷ 30π × 360 = 60°, or for area = ½ × r × arc length
questions.tip: Find the angle first (60°) or use area = ½ × r × arc length. The π cancels when finding the angle, so no calculator is needed.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A sector of a circle has radius 18 cm and angle 140°.
Work out the perimeter of the sector. Give your answer in the form a + bπ.
questions.tip: The perimeter of a sector includes TWO radii.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A circular pond of radius 5 m is surrounded by a path of width 3 m. The outer edge of the path is a circle with the same centre as the pond.
Work out the area of the path. Give your answer in terms of π.
questions.tip: The outer radius is 5 + 3 = 8 m. Do not subtract the radii before squaring: (8 - 5)² is wrong.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A sector has angle 120° and area 27π cm². What is the radius?
questions.tip: 81 is r². Remember to square root.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A shape is made from a rectangle 20 cm by 10 cm. A semicircle of diameter 10 cm is cut out of each of the two 10 cm ends, curving inwards.
(a) Work out the area of the shape. Give your answer in terms of π.
(b) Work out the perimeter of the shape. Give your answer in terms of π.
ms: M1 for two semicircle arcs = 2 × ½ × π × 10 = 10π
questions.tip: The 10 cm ends have been cut out, so they are NOT part of the perimeter. Use the two 20 cm sides plus the arcs.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A and B are points on a circle with centre O and radius 6 cm. Angle AOB = 120°.
Work out the exact area of the minor segment cut off by the chord AB. Give your answer in the form aπ - b√3.
ms: M1 for triangle OAB area = ½ × 6 × 6 × sin 120°
questions.tip: Segment = sector - triangle. sin 120° = sin 60° = √3/2, so the triangle area is still exact.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A sector of a circle has area 6π cm² and arc length 2π cm.
Work out the radius and the angle of the sector.
ms: M1 for θ/360 × πr² = 6π and θ/360 × 2πr = 2π (or area = ½ × r × arc length)
questions.tip: Divide the area equation by the arc equation. The θ/360 and π cancel, leaving r/2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCD is a square of side 4 cm. A quarter circle of radius 4 cm is drawn with centre A, from B to D. A second quarter circle of radius 4 cm is drawn with centre C, also from B to D. The two arcs enclose a leaf-shaped region.
Work out the area of the leaf-shaped region. Give your answer in the form aπ - b.
ms: M1 for one quarter circle = ¼ × π × 16 = 4π
M1 for half the leaf = 4π - ½ × 4 × 4 = 4π - 8 (quarter circle minus triangle ABD)
questions.tip: Each half of the leaf is a quarter circle minus a right-angled triangle. Adding the two quarter circles counts the leaf twice.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A sector of a circle has angle 75° and area 40 cm².
Work out the perimeter of the sector. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.tip: Keep the unrounded radius in your calculator for the arc length.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A triangular prism has a cross-section that is a right-angled triangle with shorter sides 6 cm and 8 cm. The prism is 10 cm long. What is its volume?
ms: Cross-section area = ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 cm². Volume = 24 × 10 = 240 cm³.
questions.tip: 480 forgets the ½ in the triangle area.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A sphere has volume 36π cm³.
(a) Work out the radius of the sphere.
(b) Work out the surface area of the sphere. Give your answer in terms of π.
ms: M1 for 4/3 × π × r³ = 36π, so r³ = 27
B1 for 4 × π × 3² = 36π cm² (ft their r)
questions.tip: Multiply 36 by 3/4 to get r³ = 27, then cube root. Surface area uses r², volume uses r³.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A solid cone has perpendicular height 15 cm and volume 320π cm³.
Work out the curved surface area of the cone. Give your answer in terms of π.
ms: M1 for ⅓ × π × r² × 15 = 320π, giving r² = 64 and r = 8
questions.tip: Curved surface area is πrl, using the SLANT height l, not the perpendicular height.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A solid cylinder has radius 3 cm and height h cm. A solid sphere also has radius 3 cm. The total surface area of the cylinder is equal to the surface area of the sphere.
Work out the value of h.
ms: M1 for sphere surface area 4 × π × 3² = 36π
questions.tip: The total surface area of a cylinder includes BOTH circular ends. The π cancels, so no calculator is needed.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A closed cylinder has radius 4 cm and height 7 cm.
Work out the total surface area of the cylinder. Give your answer in terms of π.
questions.tip: A CLOSED cylinder has two circular ends. Count both.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A solid is made of a cone on top of a cylinder. The cone and the cylinder both have radius 3 cm. The cylinder has height 10 cm and the cone has perpendicular height 4 cm.
Work out the total volume of the solid. Give your answer in terms of π.
questions.tip: Don't forget the ⅓ for the cone.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A cone has volume 96π cm³ and base radius 6 cm. What is its perpendicular height?
ms: ⅓ × π × 36 × h = 96π, so 12h = 96 and h = 8 cm.
questions.tip: 24 cm forgets the ⅓ in the cone formula.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A solid sphere fits exactly inside a closed cylinder. The sphere touches the top, the bottom and the curved side of the cylinder. The radius of the sphere is r.
(a) Show that the volume of the sphere is 2/3 of the volume of the cylinder.
(b) Show that the surface area of the sphere is equal to the curved surface area of the cylinder.
questions.answer: (a) Cylinder has radius r and height 2r, volume 2πr³. Sphere volume 4/3 πr³ = 2/3 × 2πr³. (b) Curved surface = 2πr × 2r = 4πr², the same as the sphere's 4πr².
ms: B1 for 2πr × 2r = 4πr² which equals the sphere's surface area
questions.tip: The cylinder height is the DIAMETER of the sphere, 2r, not r.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A solid cone has base radius 9 cm and slant height 15 cm. A small cone is cut off the top by a cut parallel to the base, leaving a frustum. The small cone has slant height 5 cm.
(a) Work out the curved surface area of the frustum. Give your answer in terms of π.
(b) Work out the total surface area of the frustum. Give your answer in terms of π.
ms: M1 for radius of small cone = 9 × 5/15 = 3 cm (similar cones)
questions.tip: A frustum has TWO flat circular faces, top and bottom. Use similar cones to get the top radius.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A solid cylinder has radius 2x cm and height x cm. A solid sphere has radius x cm.
Show that the total surface area of the cylinder is 3 times the surface area of the sphere.
questions.tip: (2x)² = 4x², not 2x². Use brackets.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Three solid metal spheres have radii 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. They are melted down and all the metal is made into one solid sphere.
(a) Show that the radius of the new sphere is 6 cm.
(b) Work out the change in total surface area. Give your answer in terms of π.
questions.answer: (a) 4/3 π(27 + 64 + 125) = 4/3 π × 216, so R³ = 216 and R = 6 cm. (b) Decrease of 56π cm²
questions.tip: Add the VOLUMES, not the radii. 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 is not the new radius.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A cylindrical water tank has radius 40 cm. Water flows into the empty tank at a rate of 2 litres per minute.
Work out how long it takes for the water to reach a depth of 1.2 m. Give your answer in hours and minutes, to the nearest minute.
questions.tip: Convert 1.2 m to 120 cm before multiplying, and 1 litre = 1000 cm³.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A dog is tied to a post in an open field by a rope 3 m long. Which describes the region the dog can reach?
options: The inside of a circle of radius 3 m centred on the post, including the circle
A circle of radius 3 m only
ms: The dog can reach every point up to 3 m from the post, so it is the whole disc, boundary included.
questions.tip: 'A circle' is only the edge. The region is everything inside it too.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A map has a scale of 1 cm to 2 km. Towns A and B are 7.5 cm apart on the map.
(a) Work out the real distance between A and B.
(b) A radio signal from A reaches everywhere within 5 km of A. What radius of circle should be drawn on the map to show this?
questions.tip: Going from real to map you DIVIDE by 2. Check your answer makes sense.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] P is a point on a straight line L.
Describe how to construct a line through P perpendicular to L, using only a ruler and a pair of compasses.
questions.answer: Compass on P, mark two arcs on L at equal distances either side (A and B). Open the compasses wider, from A and from B draw arcs above the line that cross at Q. Join PQ.
ms: B1 for arcs centred on P cutting L at two points A and B
B1 for equal-radius arcs (radius more than PA) from A and B intersecting at Q
B1 for joining P to Q and leaving all construction arcs
questions.tip: Keep the compass width the same for the two arcs from A and B, and never rub out construction arcs.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Describe how to construct an angle of 45° at a point A on a straight line, using only a ruler and a pair of compasses.
questions.answer: Construct the perpendicular to the line at A (90°): arcs from A to cut the line at two points, then equal arcs from those points crossing above A, join to A. Then bisect the 90° angle: arcs from A cutting both arms, equal arcs from those two points crossing, join to A.
ms: B1 for constructing a 90° angle at A with correct arcs
B1 for arcs from A cutting both arms of the right angle
B1 for equal arcs from those points crossing and joining to A to give 45°
questions.tip: 45° is half of 90°. Construct the right angle properly first, don't use a protractor.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A rectangular field ABCD has AB = 40 m and BC = 30 m. A sprinkler must be placed more than 10 m from every side of the field.
(a) Describe the region where the sprinkler can be placed.
(b) Work out the area of this region.
questions.answer: (a) A rectangle inside the field, with each side 10 m in from the matching side of the field (20 m by 10 m). (b) 200 m²
ms: B1 for the region being a rectangle with edges 10 m from each side
questions.tip: Each dimension loses 10 m at BOTH ends, so subtract 20, not 10.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A, B and C are three villages that do not lie on a straight line. A phone mast is to be built so that it is the same distance from all three villages.
Describe how to find the position of the mast using a ruler and a pair of compasses.
questions.answer: Construct the perpendicular bisector of AB and the perpendicular bisector of BC. The mast is where they cross.
ms: B1 for constructing perpendicular bisectors of two of the lines AB, BC, AC
B1 for the intersection being the position
questions.tip: Equidistant from two POINTS means perpendicular bisector, not angle bisector.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] A circle has centre O and radius 5 cm. What is the locus of points exactly 2 cm from the circle?
options: Two circles with centre O, radii 3 cm and 7 cm
One circle with centre O, radius 7 cm
One circle with centre O, radius 2 cm
Two circles with centre O, radii 2 cm and 5 cm
ms: Points 2 cm from the circle can be inside (5 - 2 = 3 cm from O) or outside (5 + 2 = 7 cm from O).
questions.tip: Remember the points inside the circle as well as outside.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A rectangle measures 6 cm by 4 cm. The locus of points outside the rectangle that are exactly 2 cm from the rectangle is drawn.
(a) Describe the shape of this locus.
(b) Work out the total length of the locus. Give your answer in terms of π.
questions.answer: (a) Four straight lines parallel to the sides, 2 cm away, joined by four quarter circles of radius 2 cm centred on the corners. (b) (20 + 4π) cm
ms: B1 for straight parallel lines 2 cm away from each side
B1 for quarter circles of radius 2 cm at the corners
M1 for straight parts 6 + 6 + 4 + 4 = 20 and four quarter circles = one full circle 2π × 2
questions.tip: The corners are ROUNDED. A rectangle with square corners is the classic mistake.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A is the point (2, 1) and B is the point (6, 5).
Find the equation of the locus of points that are equidistant from A and B. Give your answer in the form y = mx + c.
ms: M1 for perpendicular gradient -1 and substituting (4, 3)
questions.tip: The locus is the perpendicular bisector: it goes through the midpoint AND has gradient -1/m.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A point P in the first quadrant is equidistant from the x-axis and the y-axis. P is 5 units from the origin O.
Work out the exact coordinates of P.
ms: B1 for P lies on y = x (the angle bisector of the axes)
questions.tip: Rationalise 5/√2 to 5√2/2 and give BOTH coordinates.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCD is a square garden with sides of 10 m. A fountain is to be placed inside the garden so that it is equidistant from A and C and exactly 6 m from B.
(a) Explain why the fountain must lie on the diagonal BD.
(b) Work out the exact distance of the fountain from D.
questions.answer: (a) Points equidistant from A and C lie on the perpendicular bisector of AC, which is the other diagonal BD (diagonals of a square bisect each other at right angles). (b) (10√2 - 6) m
ms: B1 for perpendicular bisector of AC is BD with reason
questions.tip: Use the property that the diagonals of a square are perpendicular bisectors of each other.

questions.q:
[Calculator] A ship sails due east along a straight line. A rock R is 1.5 km due north of the line. The ship must be warned while it is within 2 km of R.
Work out the distance the ship travels while it is within 2 km of the rock. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
ms: B1 for recognising the locus is a circle of radius 2 km centred on R cutting the line at two points
questions.tip: The circle cuts the line in TWO places, so double the half-length.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The point (-2, 5) is reflected in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
ms: Reflecting in the x-axis keeps x the same and changes the sign of y.
questions.tip: (2, 5) is the reflection in the y-axis. The x-axis is the horizontal line y = 0.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A translation maps the point (1, 3) to the point (-4, 5).
(a) Write down the column vector of the translation.
(b) The same translation is applied to the point (2, -1). Write down the coordinates of its image.
questions.tip: Vector = image minus original. Getting the signs backwards is the usual slip.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle T has vertices (3, 2), (5, 2) and (5, 3). T is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the point (1, 2).
Write down the coordinates of the vertices of the image.
ms: M1 for using positions relative to the centre (2, 0), (4, 0), (4, 1)
questions.tip: Rotate about (1, 2), not the origin. Work relative to the centre, or use tracing paper.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle A has vertices (5, 2), (11, 2) and (8, 11). Triangle B has vertices (3, 0), (5, 0) and (4, 3).
Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle A onto triangle B.
questions.tip: A shape that gets smaller is still an 'enlargement'. Give all three facts.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle P has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 3). Triangle Q has vertices (0, -2), (0, -4) and (2, -2).
Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle P onto triangle Q.
questions.tip: Find the centre by checking each vertex is the same distance from it, or with perpendicular bisectors. Always state the direction.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] Shapes are reflected in the line y = x. Which of these points is invariant (stays in the same place)?
ms: Only points ON the mirror line y = x are invariant. (3, 3) has y = x.
questions.tip: (0, 3) maps to (3, 0), so it moves.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle T has vertices (3, 1), (4, 1) and (3, 3). T is enlarged by scale factor -3 with centre (2, 0).
Write down the coordinates of the vertices of the image.
ms: M1 for vectors from the centre (1, 1), (2, 1), (1, 3) multiplied by -3
questions.tip: Work from the centre (2, 0), not the origin. A negative scale factor puts the image on the opposite side of the centre.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Shape S is reflected in the y-axis and then rotated 90° anticlockwise about the origin, giving shape S''.
Shape T is rotated 90° anticlockwise about the origin FIRST and then reflected in the y-axis, giving shape T''.
(a) Describe fully the single transformation that maps S onto S''.
(b) Describe fully the single transformation that maps T onto T''.
questions.answer: (a) Reflection in the line y = -x (b) Reflection in the line y = x
ms: M1 for following a test point in (a), e.g. (1, 2) → (-1, 2) → (-2, -1)
M1 for following a test point in (b), e.g. (1, 2) → (-2, 1) → (2, 1)
A1 for reflection in y = x
questions.tip: The order of transformations matters. Use a non-symmetric test point like (1, 2) and follow it through each step.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Shape A is reflected in the line x = 2 to give shape B. Shape B is then reflected in the line y = 1 to give shape C.
Describe fully the single transformation that maps shape A onto shape C.
ms: M1 for a test point, e.g. (3, 4) → (1, 4) → (1, -2)
questions.tip: Two reflections in PERPENDICULAR lines make a half turn about the point where the lines cross. No direction is needed for 180°.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] Triangle A has vertices (2, 1), (4, 1) and (4, 2). Triangle B has vertices (-1, -5), (-5, -5) and (-5, -7).
Describe fully the single transformation that maps triangle A onto triangle B.
questions.tip: Join corresponding vertices with lines: they cross at the centre, which is BETWEEN the shapes for a negative scale factor.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A shape with area 12 cm² is enlarged by scale factor -1/2 with centre C. The image is then enlarged by scale factor 3 with the same centre C.
(a) Write down the scale factor of the single enlargement that maps the original shape to the final image.
(b) Work out the area of the final image.
questions.tip: Area scale factor is the square of the length scale factor, and squaring removes the minus sign.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] The point P is rotated 90° clockwise about the point (1, 1). Its image is the point (5, -2).
Work out the coordinates of P.
ms: M1 for the image relative to the centre: (4, -3)
M1 for rotating back 90° anticlockwise to (3, 4)
questions.tip: To undo a clockwise rotation, rotate the image ANTICLOCKWISE. Check by rotating your answer forward.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] a = (-1, 4) and b = (3, 2), written as column vectors. The vector c satisfies 2c + a = b. What is c?
questions.tip: Rearrange like an equation: subtract a, then halve. (4, -2) forgets to halve.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] A is the point (3, -1) and B is the point (-2, 4).
(a) Write AB as a column vector.
(b) Work out the magnitude of AB. Give your answer in surd form.
questions.tip: AB = B - A (end minus start). √50 = √25 × √2 = 5√2.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] p(2, 1) + q(1, -3) = (7, 0), where (2, 1), (1, -3) and (7, 0) are column vectors and p and q are numbers.
Work out the values of p and q.
questions.tip: Make one equation from the top numbers and one from the bottom numbers.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OABC is a parallelogram. OA = a and OC = c. M is the midpoint of BC.
Work out, in terms of a and c, (a) the vector OM (b) the vector AM.
ms: B1 for CB = a (parallel and equal to OA)
B1 for AM = -a + c + ½a = c - ½a
questions.tip: In a parallelogram, opposite sides are the same vector: CB = OA = a.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] ABCDEF is a regular hexagon with centre O. OA = a and OB = b.
Work out, in terms of a and b, (a) the vector AB (b) the vector OC (c) the vector AD.

B1 for AD = -2a (D is opposite A, through O)
questions.tip: A regular hexagon splits into six equilateral triangles, so lots of the lines are parallel and equal.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OAB is a triangle. OA = a and OB = b. The line AB is extended beyond B to the point C so that AB : BC = 2 : 1.
Work out OC in terms of a and b. Give your answer in its simplest form.
ms: A1 for OC = b + ½(b - a) = (3/2)b - (1/2)a
questions.tip: C is BEYOND B, so add half of AB onto OB. It is not a point between A and B.

questions.q: [Non-calculator] The vector (k, 6) has magnitude 10, and k is positive. What is the value of k?

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OABC is a quadrilateral. OA = 2a, AB = 3b and OC = 6b.
(a) Show that OC is parallel to AB.
(b) Work out the vector CB in terms of a and b.
questions.answer: (a) OC = 6b = 2 × 3b = 2AB, so OC is parallel to AB (and twice as long). (b) CB = 2a - 3b
ms: M1 for CB = CO + OA + AB = -6b + 2a + 3b
questions.tip: Parallel vectors are multiples of each other. Say 'OC is a multiple of AB'.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OAB is a triangle. OA = a and OB = b. M is the midpoint of OA. N is the point on AB so that AN : NB = 1 : 2. The line BO is extended beyond O to the point P so that OP = OB.
Prove that P, M and N lie on a straight line.
questions.answer: MN = ON - OM = (a + ⅓(b - a)) - ½a = (1/6)a + (1/3)b = (1/6)(a + 2b). PM = PO + OM = b + ½a = ½(a + 2b). So PM = 3MN: they are parallel and share the point M, so P, M and N are collinear.
ms: B1 for AN = ⅓(b - a) or ON = ⅔a + ⅓b
M1 for PM = ½a + b (using OP = -b)
M1 for showing PM is a multiple of MN (PM = 3MN)
A1 for conclusion: parallel AND a common point M, so collinear
questions.tip: For collinear you must state both: the vectors are parallel AND they share a point.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OAB is a triangle. OA = a and OB = b. X is the point on OA so that OX : XA = 1 : 3. Y is the midpoint of AB. The lines OY and BX meet at the point Z.
(a) Work out OZ in terms of a and b.
(b) Work out the ratio OZ : ZY.
ms: M1 for OY = ½(a + b) so OZ = μ × ½(a + b)
M1 for OZ = b + λ(¼a - b) using BX
M1 for equating coefficients: μ/2 = λ/4 and μ/2 = 1 - λ
A1 for λ = 4/5, μ = 2/5, giving OZ = (1/5)(a + b)
questions.tip: Write the same point two ways using two unknowns, then match the a parts and the b parts.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OABC is a quadrilateral. OA = a, OB = b and OC = c. P, Q, R and S are the midpoints of OA, AB, BC and CO respectively.
Prove that PQRS is a parallelogram.
questions.answer: PQ = OQ - OP = ½(a + b) - ½a = ½b. SR = OR - OS = ½(b + c) - ½c = ½b. So PQ = SR: one pair of opposite sides is parallel and equal, so PQRS is a parallelogram.
ms: B1 for OP = ½a and OQ = ½(a + b)
A1 for PQ = SR so parallel and equal, hence parallelogram
questions.tip: If two opposite sides are the same vector, they are parallel AND equal. That is enough for a parallelogram.

questions.q:
[Non-calculator] OABC is a parallelogram. OA = a and OC = c. M is the point on AB so that AM : MB = 1 : 2. The line OM meets the diagonal AC at the point P.
Show that AP : PC = 1 : 3.
questions.answer: OM = a + ⅓c, so OP = μ(a + ⅓c). Also OP = a + λ(c - a). Comparing coefficients: μ = 1 - λ and μ/3 = λ, so λ = 1/4. AP = ¼AC, so AP : PC = 1 : 3.
ms: M1 for OP = μ(a + ⅓c) and OP = a + λ(c - a)
M1 for equating coefficients of a and c: μ = 1 - λ and μ/3 = λ
questions.tip: AB = OC = c in a parallelogram, so AM = ⅓c. Then OM = a + ⅓c.

Translation a units RIGHT: (x, y) → (x + a, y)
(3, -4): move right 2, then reflect in the x-axis
Becomes a minimum at (-1, -6)
y = sin x translated 45° left: maximum at (45°, 1)

flashcards.front: Tangent gradient at (a, b) on x² + y² = r²
flashcards.back: Negative reciprocal of the radius gradient b/a, i.e. -a/b

flashcards.front: Shortcut: tangent to x² + y² = r² at (a, b)
flashcards.back: ax + by = r², e.g. at (3, 4) on x² + y² = 25: 3x + 4y = 25

flashcards.front: Radius of x² + y² = 50 in simplest surd form

flashcards.back: Always passes through the centre of the circle

flashcards.front: Trapezium rule with strip width h
flashcards.back: Area ≈ h/2 × (first + last + 2 × (all middle values))
Curve bends upwards: overestimate. Curve bends downwards: underestimate

flashcards.front: Instantaneous speed from a curved distance-time graph
flashcards.back: Draw a tangent at that time and find its gradient

flashcards.front: Area under a rate-time graph (e.g. litres per minute)
flashcards.back: Total amount, e.g. total litres
Decay: value falls by 20% each step; a is the starting value

flashcards.front: Squared factor in a cubic, e.g. y = x²(x - 3)
flashcards.back: Repeated root: the curve touches the x-axis at x = 0

flashcards.front: Line to draw on y = x³ - 4x to solve x³ - 6x + 1 = 0

flashcards.back: Reciprocal: two separate curves in the 1st and 3rd quadrants, asymptotes x = 0 and y = 0

flashcards.front: Interior angle of a regular n-sided polygon
flashcards.back: 180° - 360°/n (find the exterior angle first, then subtract from 180°)

flashcards.front: Bisectors of angles B and C in triangle ABC meet at I. Angle BIC?
flashcards.back: 90° + ½ × angle A (because angle B + angle C = 180° - angle A, then halve).

flashcards.front: Point between two parallel lines joined to both lines
flashcards.back: Draw an extra line through the point parallel to the others, then use alternate angles twice.

flashcards.front: Test: can a regular polygon have interior angle x?
flashcards.back: Work out 360 ÷ (180 - x). It must be a whole number (at least 3).

flashcards.front: Exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral
flashcards.back: Equals the interior angle at the opposite vertex (because opposite angles add to 180°).

flashcards.front: Two tangents PA and PB with centre O: angle APB and angle AOB
flashcards.back: Add up to 180° (OAPB has two 90° angles and angles in a quadrilateral add to 360°).

flashcards.front: Chord of length c, distance d from the centre, radius r
flashcards.back: (c/2)² + d² = r² (the perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord).

flashcards.front: Angle between a tangent and a diameter at the point of contact
flashcards.back: 90°. A tangent is perpendicular to the radius, and the diameter contains that radius.

flashcards.front: Right-angled triangle ABC (right angle at A) with perpendicular AD to BC
flashcards.back: Three similar triangles. AD² = BD × DC.

flashcards.front: Triangle ABC with D on AC and angle ABD = angle ACB
flashcards.back: Triangles ABD and ACB are similar (common angle A), so AB² = AD × AC.

flashcards.front: Hourglass shape: AB parallel to CD, AD and BC cross at X
flashcards.back: Triangles ABX and DCX are similar: vertically opposite angles and alternate angles are equal.
1 m² = 10 000 cm². 1 m³ = 1 000 000 cm³. 1 litre = 1000 cm³.
√((x₂ - x₁)² + (y₂ - y₁)²)
45°: sides 1, 1, √2. 30° and 60°: sides 1, √3, 2 (half an equilateral triangle of side 2).
Split it down the middle into two right-angled triangles, then use Pythagoras with half the base.

flashcards.front: Exact values for obtuse angles: sin 120°, cos 120°, sin 135°, cos 135°
Finding sin θ exactly from cos θ
flashcards.back: sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, so sin θ = √(1 - cos² θ) (positive for angles in a triangle).

flashcards.front: Perpendicular height of a triangle from its area
flashcards.back: h = 2 × area ÷ base
Draw a north line at each point. North lines are parallel, so use co-interior (add to 180°) or alternate angles.
Area = ½ × r × arc length

flashcards.front: Area of a ring (annulus) between radii R and r
flashcards.back: π(R² - r²). Square each radius first, then subtract.

flashcards.front: Area of an equilateral triangle of side s
flashcards.back: (√3/4)s², from ½ × s × s × sin 60°. Needed for 60° segments.

flashcards.front: Leaf shape from two quarter circles in a square of side s
flashcards.back: Area = 2 × (¼πs² - ½s²) = ½πs² - s²

flashcards.front: Sphere fitting exactly in a cylinder
flashcards.back: Cylinder height = 2r. Sphere volume is 2/3 of the cylinder volume.

flashcards.front: Volume of a hollow sphere with outer radius R and inner radius r
flashcards.back: 4/3 π(R³ - r³)

flashcards.front: Total surface area of a closed cylinder
flashcards.back: 2πr² + 2πrh
1 m³ = 1000 litres (1 litre = 1000 cm³)

flashcards.front: Locus of points a fixed distance outside a rectangle
flashcards.back: Straight lines parallel to the sides joined by quarter circles at each corner.

flashcards.front: Point equidistant from three points A, B and C
flashcards.back: Where the perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC cross.

flashcards.front: Equation of the locus equidistant from two coordinate points
flashcards.back: Perpendicular bisector: passes through the midpoint, gradient = -1 ÷ gradient of the line joining them.

flashcards.front: Locus of points distance d from a circle of radius r
flashcards.back: Two circles with the same centre, radii r - d and r + d (if d < r).
A point that does not move under a transformation, e.g. points on a mirror line, or the centre of a rotation or enlargement.
Equivalent to a rotation of 180° about the point where the lines meet.

flashcards.front: Finding the centre of a rotation
flashcards.back: Draw perpendicular bisectors of lines joining two pairs of corresponding points. They cross at the centre.

flashcards.front: Two enlargements with the same centre
flashcards.back: Equivalent to one enlargement with scale factor = the two scale factors multiplied.

flashcards.front: Regular hexagon ABCDEF with centre O
flashcards.back: OA + OC = OB, so OC = OB - OA. Opposite vertices: OD = -OA.

flashcards.front: Solving p(x₁, y₁) + q(x₂, y₂) = (x, y)
flashcards.back: Top numbers give one equation, bottom numbers give another. Solve simultaneously.

flashcards.front: Where two lines cross in a vector problem
flashcards.back: Write the point two ways (λ and μ), then equate the coefficients of a and of b.

flashcards.front: Point C beyond B on line AB with AB : BC = m : n
flashcards.back: OC = OB + (n/m)AB
